Question:
Question 2
The FDS manufacturing process development is with HC1, HC2, and further optimized to 
HC2 optimized, please provide the full report of the comparability studies, including 
comparative characterization data, comparative batch analysis, and comparative stability 
studies.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (3.2S.2.6):
Additional information related to comparability of HC1, HC2 and further optimized HC2 
optimized manufacturing processes are provided in CTD Section S.2.6.11 and is summarized 
below.
Analytical comparability of aflibercept high-dose HC1 and HC2 FDS was assessed with 
release, long-term storage, accelerated stability, and stress stability testing. This evaluation 
determined that HC2 FDS is comparable to HC1 FDS with no impact to potency, biochemical 
attributes, physicochemical attributes, or stability of the protein.
Production-scale aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS lots manufactured by the HC2 
process were evaluated for comparability to HC1 FDS lots.
The release results were evaluated against release specification acceptance criteria as well as 
historical results from HC1 lots. The long-term storage results were evaluated against stability 
specification acceptance criteria and the accelerated and stress stability results were compared 
to data from an HC1 FDS comparator lot (8305500001).
Comparability of aflibercept high-dose FDS manufactured by the HC1 and HC2 processes is 
supported by the following product quality assessments.
• 
The HC2 FDS lots met the release specification acceptance criteria. The HC2 FDS 
results for potency, purity, and physicochemical attributes were well aligned with 
historical HC1 FDS results. Differences in fragmentation and charge variants were 
likely attributable to process variability in the DSI source lots.
• 
HC1 and HC2 FDS showed little to no degradation under the long-term storage 
condition and HC2 FDS met the stability specification acceptance criteria through 36 
months.
• 
Common mechanisms and rates of fragmentation, aggregation, and charge variant 
formation were observed for HC1 and HC2 FDS under the accelerated and stress 
stability conditions. Additionally, potency by bioassay was largely unchanged for 
material from both processes under both conditions.
Overall, aflibercept high-dose HC1 and HC2 FDS are comparable and this assessment 
supports the use of the HC2 manufacturing process for production of aflibercept high-dose 
DS and FDS. Based on comparative batch analysis and comparative stability analysis, HC1 
and HC2 were found to be comparable and thus no extended characterization was deemed 
necessary. In addition, both HC1 and HC2 material was used in the clinical studies.
Analytical comparability of aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL HC2 and optimized HC2 was 
assessed with in-process, release, and stress stability data. Release results from optimized 
HC2 process are compared to release specifications and comparability limits.
The three production-scale optimized process lot results all meet the current and proposed 
release specification acceptance criteria. Additionally, all results fall within the comparability
limits. This evaluation demonstrates the product quality of the optimized process lots are 
highly similar to historical lots at release.
Extended characterization testing was performed to assess molecular weight, glycan identity 
and heterogeneity, molar mass, and size heterogeneity of the test articles and comparators.
Additionally, a side-by-side stress stability study at 37 °C was performed with the three 
optimized process lots and three representative historical lots to compare the degradation 
trends. Additional timepoints for long term stability studies have been provided with the 
response to Question 5.
The information including comparative characterization data, comparative batch analysis, and 
comparative stability studies is provided in CTD section S.2.6.11.
Source:  S.2.6.11-01 Manufacturing Process Development - Additional Information/
Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL (#022979588; new)

Question:
Question 1
In Regards to the stability study:
a) To present the extractable volume results numerically rather than simply stating 
"Complies." This request also applies to the batch analysis.
b) Provide the Osmolality and Viscosity results at the end of shelf life for batches 43002, 
43003, and 43004 for the 7.5mL pack size.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
a) To present the extractable volume results numerically rather than simply stating 
"Complies." This request also applies to the batch analysis.
We acknowledge your query regarding the presentation of extractable volume results in 
stability data and batch analysis, and we would like to provide the following clarification:
The extractable volume results in the submitted stability data and batch analysis were stated 
as "Complies" in accordance with our acceptance criterion, which specifies that the individual 
volume must be ≥ nominal volume. This complies with established regulatory guidelines, 
ensuring that the product meets the required specifications.
We confirm that all extractable volume results in the submitted stability data and batch 
analysis are within specification and meet the required acceptance criteria. We commit to 
provide further clarification or additional documentation if needed by HA.
The declaration for the same has been provided for your reference.
Source:  Justification -Extractable volume results in stability data & batch analysis

b) Provide the Osmolality and Viscosity results at the end of shelf life for batches 43002, 
43003, and 43004 for the 7.5mL pack size.
We acknowledge your query regarding the provision of osmolality and viscosity results at the 
end of shelf life.
Please note that osmolality and viscosity are not considered stability-indicating parameters for 
this product. As such, these parameters are not included in the shelf-life specifications. The 
stability of the product is assured through other validated stability-indicating tests, which are 
part of the established shelf-life specifications.
This approach aligns with internationally recognized regulatory guidelines, such as:
• 
ICH Q6A: Specifies that only stability-indicating parameters, which are directly 
relevant to the product’s quality, safety, and efficacy, are required as part of the 
stability testing program.
• 
ICH Q1A(R2): Emphasizes the need to monitor critical quality attributes during 
stability studies, focusing on parameters that are most likely to be affected by storage 
conditions.

Question:
Question 3
a) In in process validation report:
i. Conclude about the maximum acceptable filling time.
ii. Conclude about the product holding time after filling and before terminal sterilization.
iii. Identify the temperature range of product terminal sterilization in the autoclave (>121ºC), 
with submitting the process validation for product terminal sterilization in the autoclave.

b) Justify the OOS results for:
i. Extractable volume page 7, BN#43002 for filling volume 7.5mL.
ii. BN#43004 for filling volumes 5 , 7.5mL & 10mL.
iii. Stopper insertion for BN#43004.
iv. Endotoxin Results for stoppers used in BN#51003.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (P.3.5):
a) In in process validation report:
Please see the corresponding responses below:
i. Conclude about the maximum acceptable filling time.
Holding time of the bulk solution is defined from start of the filtration of the bulk into the 
holding tank until terminal sterilization of the last pre-filled plastic syringe. The maximum 
allowable holding time of Primovist bulk solution is 168 hours (7 days). All filling activities of 
pre-filled plastic syringes are performed within the holding time of the bulk solution. Adherence 
to the maximum allowable holding time is checked the batch record review process.
ii. Conclude about the product holding time after filling and before terminal sterilization.
The maximum product holding time after filling and before sterilization is 24 hours. Adherence 
to the maximum allowable holding time is checked the batch record review process.
iii. Identify the temperature range of product terminal sterilization in the autoclave 
(>121ºC), with submitting the process validation for product terminal sterilization in the 
autoclave.
During the 20 minutes sterilization phase the acceptable temperature range in the autoclave is 
122 – 124 °C. If the temperature deviates below the lower threshold the timer is automatically 
stopped and only continues once the temperature re-enters the acceptable temperature range. If 
the temperature exceeds the upper threshold the sterilization process is automatically aborted. 
All temperature excursions automatically generate an alarm and are reported in the sterilization 
protocol. Every sterilization protocol is checked by the operators and during the batch record 
review process

b) Justify the OOS results for:
i. Extractable volume page 7, BN#43002 for filling volume 7.5mL.
ii. BN#43004 for filling volumes 5 , 7.5mL & 10mL.
iii. Stopper insertion for BN#43004.
iv. Endotoxin Results for stoppers used in BN#51003.

Question:
Question 1
List of SFDA Questions to be sent to the MAH: Module 1.1  A justification letter to include 
the rationale along with supportive data for all proposed variations.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section):

Background and scope of these changes is related to the Letter of Recommendation from 
EMA to Bayer AG.  As per the letter of recommendation issued within procedure number 
EMEA/H/C/004054/0000 at the time of the Jivi CHMP Opinion for the Marketing 
Authorization, Bayer AG committed to re-evaluate the specification limits proposed for Drug 
Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP) after 30 batches have been manufactured and to 
continue the development and implementation of a process specific HCP assay.  
The first re-evaluation took place for the specification parameters Osmolality, Specific 
Activity and Total Protein and related changes were submitted for DS and DP for strengths 
500 - 3000 IU, which have been approved under Procedure No. 
EMEA/H/C/004054/II/0019/G. 
 
With this variation package we are presenting the re-evaluation of the other, remaining 
specification parameters for DS and DP and the new process specific HCP method and related 
specifications. Consequently, we would also like to introduce changes that are related to 
method improvements in the same variation package.

Description of the changes in this variation submission: 
Updated release and stability specifications for DS and Drug Product (DP) for Potency, High 
Molecular Weight (HMW), Low Molecular Weight (LMW), Purity, Glycine, Histidine and 
Calcium are being proposed. For content specific attributes (total protein, specific activity, 
and osmolality), specifications were not recalculated for the 250 IU dosage strength. There 
have been no commercial batches produced of the 250 IU strength since the initial product 
licensure and thus no new data to consider. Existing specifications are maintained for the 250 
IU dosage strength. Excipient specifications have been adjusted for all dosage strengths as 
they are independent of protein concentration. Additionally, the test methods SEC-HPLC and 
RP-HPLC for the determination of Purity are adjusted to include some of the Impurity region 
as a product variant and redefine some of the LMW region as belonging to the main product 
peak.  The new limits are based on redefinition of the test methods for Purity and LMW. No

methodology change: integration change only.  The specifications pertaining to the size 
exclusion and reverse phase HPLC (HMW, LMW, Purity and LC/HC ratio) have been 
recalculated for all dosage strengths due to changes in the assay integration.  
A new process specific Host Cell Protein (HCP) Immunoassay is proposed for replacement of 
the current method used for HCP determination which is not process-specific. Related 
updated specification limits are proposed for implementation in testing DS- Q Eluate. 
Additionally, the HCP as a process performance attribute for the Membrane Adsorption 
Eluate-Formulated (MAEF) process step is proposed for removal. 
An optimized test method of Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP) for determination of Sodium 
and Calcium is proposed. The optimized method will replace the current method used for 
testing Drug Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP). 
 
Changes in the acceptance criteria for peak ratios and revised peak calculations are proposed 
to optimize the Tryptic Digest Peptide Map (peptide map) method. 
Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate-Poly-Acrylamide Gel Electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) Silver Stain 
Method is proposed for replacement of the Reverse Phase HPLC method for identity testing 
of DP. 
 
Clinical Control CTL 2117 RM2 and its system suitability criteria will be replaced by 
Conformance Control CTL 2131 RM1 and its system suitability for Reverse Phase HPLC 
Methods for DS and DP considering that the clinical stability program for all Jivi clinical 
product ended in December 2020.  As such, clinical control CTL 2117 RM2 is no longer 
needed. Additionally, reference standard STD 0218 RM1 is being introduced for use in RP-
HPLC (2.5 µm) and peptide map assay. Reference standard is introduced using the 
limits/conditions as detailed in the approved qualification protocol.


• 
REC 18510: DP - Implement SDS-PAGE Silver Stain Drug Product Identity testing for Jivi 
Packaged Final Containers
• 
REC 30534: DS and DP - Implementation of new release and stability specifications for DS and 
DP for Potency, High Molecular Weight (HMW), Low Molecular Weight (LMW), Purity, LC/HC, 
Glycine, Histidine, Sodium and Calcium as well as redefinition of test methods for Purity and 
LMW
• 
REC 30567: DS - Implement a new process specific Host Cell Protein (HCP) Immunoassay and 
remove HCP as a process performance attribute for MAEF process step
• 
REC 30569: DS and DP - Replace Clinical Control CTL 2117 RM2 with Conformance Control 
CTL 2131 RM1 for QC method Reverse Phase HPLC Analysis

• 
REC 30570: Optimization of Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP) for determination of Sodium 
and Calcium in DS method and related changes in DP method
• 
REC 30577: Implement a revision to the acceptance criteria for Tryptic Peptide Map Analysis

Justification for grouping: 
It is justified based on Regulation 1234/2008, Annex III.2 because the same specification 
parameters and HCP method are being modified based on the same underlying evaluation and 
commitment, so that the variations are consequential. The justification for grouping of the 
other method changes is that these method changes are interrelated to the committed 
specification assessment and resulting changes too.

Question:
Question 1
The stability data were obtained from batches of 60 capsules packaged in a 120ml HDPE 
bottle. Please confirm whether the container closure system for the registered pack size is also 
a 120ml HDPE bottle. Please also provide justification for using the stability data of 60 
capsules per 120ml bottle to support the shelf life of the registered pack size of 56 capsules 
per bottle.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1
For the commercial 56 capsule count presentation, the headspace in the bottle is slightly 
increased compared to bottles filled with 60 capsules. A higher amount of oxygen is 
consequently included in the closed bottle. For the 100 mg formulation, which uses size 
0 capsule shells, the impact on changed headspace is 2.7 mL for a difference of four capsules 
in fill amount (0.68 mL is the volume of one size 0 capsule). With regard to variability of 
available headspace, the 75 cc bottle is specified to a nominal volume of 87 mL ± 4 mL. This 
variability is due to the blow molding manufacturing process of the bottle. Compared to the 
variability of the bottle volume, the variability in headspace between bottles filled with 
56 capsules and bottles filled with 60 capsules is even lower and therefore regarded as 
negligible. For the 120 cc bottle, the variability in nominal volume of the bottle will be even 
higher than for the 75 cc bottle (for the 25 mg capsule, filled in size 2 capsules). As the 
packaging material itself remained unchanged and 
therefore having the same water and air permeability, no impact stemming from the different 
capsule count is expected.

Question:

Change in gadolinium content (deletion of “conversion by residue on ignition”)
Deletion of the description is explained that the change is to reflect to the actual situation (from 
the new and old control table). Take the following actions.
(1) 
Explain in detail how the difference with the actual situation occurred, including the
time of occurrence and the time of diagnosis. If a difference has occurred before the 
simultaneous inspection (2016), explain the reason why it was not possible to deal with the 
simultaneous inspection.
(2) 
Submit GMP documents that provide the basis for confirming the actual situation (no
conversion has been performed) at the time of change (If there is a difference from the time of 
approval, the actual situation at the time of approval) (when residual ignition has not been 
converted). In addition, the relevant data should be labeled with markers to clarify the location 
on which the rationale is based.

on the fused basis". Confirm whether it is appropriate to remove the description on conversion 
based on the current control or the control after the partial change approval.

stability- indicating, the shelf-life specification must include all parameters which the product 
would be expected to comply with, if tested. The shelf-life specification in section 3.2.P.5.1 
must therefore retain the test for sterility. Alternatively, a single finished product specification 
covering both release and shelf-life could be provided, with footnotes added as to which

confirmed on stability batches at end of shelf-life, so section 3.2.P.8.2 should be revised

Question:
1) (S.2.2)
It is noted that the Proven Acceptable Ranges (PARs) have been determined and summarized in Section 4.1 of m3.2.S.2.6 and you have stated in each copy of the manufacturing process description provided in m3.2.S.2.2: “Acceptable ranges derived from process development studies are given in parenthesis”. When a process parameter is described as a target followed by a range proposed in parentheses, that range should be identified as a Proven Acceptable Ranges (PAR), e.g., 40 °C (PAR: 30 – 50 °C), instead of 40 °C (30 – 50 °C). Alternatively, to minimize changes that would be needed, a statement can be added at the beginning of S.2.2 to say that ranges reported in parentheses are considered Proven Acceptable Ranges (PARs).
Discrepancies were observed for some of the operating ranges of the process parameters in m3.2.S.2.2 versus the corresponding PARs in m3.2.S.2.6. You are requested to provide revised copies for the description of the commercial manufacturing process in m3.2.S.2.2, identify all the PARs in m3.2.S.2.2, and address the following discrepancies.

a) Step 1 - Bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7476):
i. The following PARs were not located in Step 1 of m3.2.S.2.2:
For acid chloride formation as per Table 4-1 – m3.2.S.2.6:
• Amount of toluene: 80 – 120%;
• Amount of dimethylformamide (DMF): 90 – 110%;
• Amount of thionyl chloride: 90 – 110%.
For amide formation as per Table 4-2 – m3.2.S.2.6:
• Amount of 7473: 95 – 105%, based on the used amount of 7475;
• Amount of toluene: 75 – 125%;
• Amount of pyridine: 90 – 110%, based on the used amount of 7475.
For seeding as per Table 4-4 – m3.2.S.2.6:
• Seeding temperature: 35 – 45 °C.

ii. It is noted that in-process control (IPC) of NMT 1% of remaining starting material 7473 to determine the end of reaction for the acid chloride formation was mentioned in m3.2.S.2.6. You are requested to include the type of the IPC testing method and the limit in the process description.

iii. The seed for crystallization in Step 1 is “Bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7476)”. You are requested to confirm whether the seed is from one of the intermediate 7476 lots previously synthesized and tested complying with the Bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7476) specification provided in m3.2.S.2.4. If different specification applies, please provide.

b) Step 2 - Methyl-bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7477):
i. The following PARs were not located in Step 2 of m3.2.S.2.2:
For N-methylation as per Table 4-7 – m3.2.S.2.6:
• Amount of DCM: 90 – 110%;
• Amount of NaOH (50%): 90 – 110%.
For isolation of 7477 as per Table 4-8 – m3.2.S.2.6:
• Amount of ethyl acetate: 83 – 117%;
• Amount of NaOH (50%): 90 – 110%;
• Amount of total water: 90 – 110%.

ii. Please specify the type of the IPC testing method to determine the content of Bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7476).

iii. The seed for crystallization in Step 2 is “Methyl-bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7477)”. You are requested to confirm whether the seed is from one of the intermediate 7477 lots previously synthesized and tested complying with the Methyl-bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7477) specification provided in m3.2.S.2.4. If different specification applies, please provide.

c) Step 3 – Benzyl-morpholinopyridyl amide intermediate (7561) solution in isopropanol:
It is noted that water content after azeotropic distillation was monitored during development and the validation campaign. You are requested to include the IPC of water content to NMT 0.3% after azeotropic distillation in the process description. Please specify the type of water content method in the process description.

d) Step 4 – Elinzanetant dihydrochloride isopropanol solvate intermediate (7485):
i. You are requested to specify the type of the method (HPLC) for the IPC of the Benzyl-morpholinopyridyl amide intermediate (7561) content in the process description.

ii. The seed for crystallization in Step 4 is “Elinzanetant dihydrochloride isopropanol solvate intermediate (7485)”. You are requested to confirm whether the seed is from one of the intermediate 7485 lots previously synthesized and tested complying with the Elinzanetant dihydrochloride isopropanol solvate intermediate (7485) specification provided in m3.2.S.2.4. If different specification applies, please provide.

e) Step 5 - Elinzanetant drug substance:
i. You are requested to address the following discrepancies:
• The salt break time of “not less than 120 min” is different than the PAR of “2 – 14 h” as per Table 4-22 – m3.2.S.S.2.6.
• The operating range for amount of isopropanol in the crystallization step is “62.3 – 78.9 kg”, equivalent to 88 – 112% of the target 70.6 kg. This is wider than the established PAR of “90 – 110%” in Table 4-23 – m3.2.S.2.6 (over ±1%).
• The defined washing amount of n-heptane of 50 – 200% in the isolation of elinzanetant drug substance step as per Table 4-25 – m3.2.S.2.6 was not located in m3.2.S.2.2.

ii. The seed for crystallization in Step 5 is “Elinzanetant drug substance crystals”. You are requested to confirm whether the seed is from one of the drug substance batches previously synthesized and released complying with the finished drug substance specification in m3.2.S.4.1. If different specification applies, please provide and justify.

f) You are requested to provide a table summary for all the IPC tests, method types and the acceptance criteria in either m3.2.S.2.2 or m3.2.S.2.4.
Answer:
Bayer acknowledges the authorities´ observation of discrepancies for some of the operating ranges of the process parameters in M3.2.S.2.2 (reported as “acceptable ranges”) versus the corresponding Proven Acceptable Ranges (PARs) described in M3.2.S.2.6 and agrees to change the manufacturing process descriptions provided in M3.2.S.2.2 as outlined in more detail below:
According to the definition of “Proven Acceptable Ranges (PARs)” as described in EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/354895/2017, the variation of a parameter within its PAR requires keeping other parameters constant. During the process understanding studies a variety of parameters were investigated. However, it was shown that some experimentally established PARs are very broad and independent from each other, while having no impact on quality attributes. Hence, Bayer believes such restriction is not generally required for all manufacturing process parameters of elinzanetant drug substance. Therefore, certain parameters were omitted in the submitted M3.2.S.2.2 process descriptions. The process knowledge obtained during development and through the process robustness studies, which have been carried out either through multivariate (DoE) and one-variable-at-a-time (OVAT) method studies, allowed for a sound selection of parameters presented in M3.2.S.2.6.01.
However, Bayer agrees that more information could be provided. In cases where multivariate studies (DoE) have been performed to investigate interdependencies of process parameters, Bayer likes to apply design spaces, respectively. Consequently, Bayer updated the manufacturing process descriptions M3.2.S.2.2 containing distinctions on which parameters are considered Normal Operating Range (NOR), Proven Acceptable Range (PAR), or Design Spaces (DSp). The additional data from multivariate (DoE) and OVAT studies are provided in the amended documentation on process development M3.2.S.2.6.11 to justify Design Spaces and Proven Acceptable Ranges.

a) Step 1 - Bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7476):
i. A revised copy for the description of the commercial manufacturing process in M3.2.S.2.2 is provided including the following amendments:
• Setpoints and Design Spaces were added for raw materials: toluene, dimethylformamide, thionyl chloride and pyridine.
• Normal operating ranges (NORs) were added for both starting materials 7473 and 7475.
• It was demonstrated that the seeding process is not mandatory but can be done optionally and the quality target profile of intermediate 7476 is not impacted by the seeding operation itself nor by the seeding temperature. Experiments with and w/o seeding are described in detail in Table 2-6 in chapter 2.1.5 “OVAT 1- Seeding parameters” in M3.2.S.2.6.11. The results justify, that seeding is a non-critical process step and accordingly the seeding temperature range of 35 – 45 °C, as depicted in M3.2.S.2.6, is not reported in M3.2.S.2.2.

Dichloromethane is controlled and specified in Methyl-bis-TFM-pyridyl amide intermediate (7477) with a limit of max. 600 ppm. Batch data reveal levels of dichloromethane below 60 ppm (LoQ) as shown in M3.2.S.2.4.01 and M3.2.S.2.4.05.

600 ppm x 0.030%
100%

Question:
17) (P.5.1 & P.5.6)
With respect to the drug product specifications provided in m3.2.P.5.1, you are requested to,
a) Revise the limit for dissolution at release and shelf life from “Q = 80% at 30 min” to “Q = 80% at 15 min”, based on the development data and the dissolution profiles of the batches used in the pivotal clinical studies, unless otherwise justified.
b) Tighten the Elinzanetant N-oxide limit at release from “max. 0.5%” to “max. 0.2%”, in line with batch data, unless otherwise justified.
c) Tighten the assay limit for shelf life from “90.0 – 105.0%” to “95.0 – 105.0%”, in line with stability data from the pivotal clinical batches, primary stability batches, and the representative commercial batches, unless otherwise justified.
d) Include the acceptance criteria for All-Rac-Alpha-Tocopherol in the drug product specifications (“min. 90%” at release and “min. 80%” for shelf life), consistent with the note for guidance on inclusion of antioxidants and antimicrobial preservatives in medicinal products (CPMP/CVMP/QWP/115/95). Skip testing may be appropriate. You are also referred to Health Canada’s Guidance Document Pharmaceutical Quality of Aqueous Solutions (Link) for further guidance.
e) Revised copies of m3.2.P.5.1 for the drug product release and shelf life specifications should be provided with your response.
Answer:
To a):
Bayer has reviewed the entirety of available batch release and stability data available from the pivotal clinical site and commercial site. Based on the review, Bayer agrees to an earlier sampling time point to be implemented prospectively for the commercial drug product. The in-vitro dissolution test method in Tier II (in case of capsule shell crosslinking) was developed and validated for a pepsin treatment of 15 min. The first sampling time point in Tier II is, however only at 20 min as the dispersion after the enzyme treatments requires stirring and homogenization before a first sample can be drawn. Therefore, the specified sampling time point can occur only after 20 minutes and a new acceptance criterion of Q = 80% at 20 min is proposed accordingly.
Batches of elinzanetant capsules 60 mg may show increasing ageing effects of the gelatine shell along with storage time and temperature.
With a modified specification, it is expected that a Tier II testing will occur with increased frequency for some of the batches during stability. It is therefore not possible to retrospectively compile Stage 2 or Tier II data for a modified sampling time point of 20 min as potentially required stage testing or Tier II procedures were only performed at the sampling time specified at the time of testing.

To b):
Bayer proposes a maximum release limit of 0.3% for elinzanetant N-oxide from now on, based on the data findings, analytical variability and batch to batch variability.
The highest batch release result above the reporting threshold was found at 0.16% (see M3.2.P.5.4.01), a release limit of 0.2% is therefore considered too tight. Considering the much higher qualified levels for elinzanetant N-oxide as well as analytical and batch-to-batch variation the limit for release is proposed to be narrowed to max 0.3%.

To c):
Bayer recognizes that the long-term stability data currently available do not indicate unambiguous decreasing trends in assay values. However, such trends do become visible under intermediate and accelerated conditions. Additionally, there is a clear increase in the sum of all degradation products, which is influenced by storage temperature. The variation of the assay data can be partially attributed to analytical variability. A batch assay result of not less than 95.0% at release has been set as per the acceptance criterion for release. Consequently, batches can be released even towards the lower limit of 95.0%. Considering the shelf life specifications allowing for the total degradation products of 5.0% and the observed actual increase in the data, a lower limit of 90.0% assay at the end of shelf life aligns reasonably with an allowed total increase of degradation products and is therefore considered justified.
In conclusion, Bayer proposes to keep the shelf life assay specification of 90.0%-105.0%.

To d):
With respect to the note for guidance on inclusion of antioxidants and antimicrobial preservatives in medicinal products (CPMP/CVMP/QWP/115/95), Bayer recognizes that as from 01 January 2008, this guideline is applicable only to veterinary medicinal products based on the reference information provided on the EMA website. In addition, Bayer would consider Health Canada’s Guidance Document Pharmaceutical Quality of Aqueous Solutions not applicable as the dosage form of elinzanetant capsule 60 mg is a non-aqueous lipid solution in a single dose soft gel capsule.
No current compendial requirements regarding specification of antioxidants in the formulation apply for the submitted dosage form elinzanetant capsule 60 mg. Harmonized Guideline ICH Q6A does not contain applicable requirements for new drug products as elinzanetant capsule 60 mg is not characterized as oral liquid.
As described in M3.2.P.8.3.01 stability data have been compiled using a validated HPLC method for all-rac-alpha tocopherol over the duration of the pivotal stability studies and will be continued until the end of the study. Batch release data for pivotal clinical and clinical/ technical batches from the final commercial manufacturing site are presented in section M3.2.P.5.4.01. No significant variation at time of release or meaningful trend has been observed during stability studies with respect to the alpha-tocopherol content where variation could only be observed within analytical variability. The justification of not testing for alpha-tocopherol has been provided in the justification of specification (M3.2.P.5.6.01).

To e):
Revised copies of the release and shelf life specifications in M3.2.P.5.1 are provided with this response.

Bayer is of the opinion that it is generally accepted, that under freezing conditions the flexible shell of soft gel capsules will be negatively impacted as the gelatin, the plasticizers and any remaining shell water may solidify. Consequently, the brittleness of the soft gel capsule will increase and therefore it is generally not recommended to freeze soft gelatin capsules.
Thus, the proposed storage statement “Do not freeze” is essential to guarantee the physical integrity of the chosen dosage form “soft gel capsule”.

Question:
Question 2
The specification for pre-sterile filtration bioburden should be ≤ 10 CFU/100 mL (TAMC).
Answer:
For Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in vials, the applicant considers the applied comprehensive
microbiological control strategy including a pre-sterile filtration testing volume of two times 50 mL
the quality of the product. A similar bioburden control strategy is applied for Aflibercept solution
114.3 mg/mL in prefilled syringes (PFS) and was accepted by EMA with procedure
EMEA/H/C/002392/IB/0091/G based on scientific justifications that are also applicable to the vial
and as presented in the following.
The total testing volume for pre-sterile filtration bioburden at Bayer AG, Berlin (BAG) is 100 mL of
Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL, which is divided into two times 50 mL: 50 mL are used for
testing of TAMC (Total Aerobic Microbial Count) and another 50 mL for testing of TYMC (Total
Yeasts and Molds Count) according to the membrane filtration procedures as described in Ph.Eur.
monograph 2.6.12. For each test a limit of ≤ 5 CFU/50 mL is set as also reflected in CTD sections
P.2.3.01-04, P.3.3.01-01 and P.3.4.01-01.
Using different incubation media and incubation temperatures for TAMC and TYMC enables
optimized growth conditions for bacteria, yeasts and molds and hence improves the likelihood of
detecting any bioburden. If molds or yeasts grow under the TAMC incubation conditions, their
counts are included in the TAMC reporting, and if bacteria grow under the TYMC incubation
conditions, their counts are included in TYMC reporting, respectively.
The manufacturing process of the Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL vial presentation at BAG was
developed and validated with an in-process control limit of two times ≤ 5 CFU/50 mL for TAMC and
TYMC each. The pre-sterile filtration bioburden method has been verified at BAG ahead of process
validation according to the requirements in Ph.Eur. monograph 2.6.12 for testing TAMC and TYMC
in two times of 50 mL volume.
In contrast, the manufacturing process of the vial at the currently approved manufacturing site
Catalent Indiana, LLC, Bloomington, US (Catalent) has been developed and validated with an in-
process control limit of ≤ 10 CFU/100 mL (total viable count). The bioburden method suitability
test was successfully demonstrated per Ph.Eur. 2.6.12 with a volume of 100 mL. Since process
validation and initial method verification were performed at Catalent using 100 mL, the same
volume is used during routine manufacturing at that site, applying an acceptance criterion of ≤ 10
CFU/100 mL for pre-filtration bioburden.
The sampling volume approach used at BAG for the Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in vial is
supported by the following considerations.
A statistical model to determine a suitable test volume for prefiltration bioburden is outlined in the
PDA publication “A risk-based Approach to Setting Sterile Filtration bioburden Limits” (Yang H:PDA
J Pharm Sci Technol:2013:67:601-609). The publication considers the microbial retention capacity
of the sterilizing filter in relation to the batch volume and the filter surface area as well as the risk
factors associated with bioburden testing [A) risk for false negative bioburden testing results and
B) risk of breakthrough of ≥ 1 CFU through the sterile filter].
Transferring these calculations to the Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL vial process at BAG by
considering a microbiological retention rate of > 107 CFU/cm², a filter size of 800 cm2 as well as a
risk A) of  ≤ 0.1% (probability of passing a batch with bioburden exceeding the acceptance limit)
and a risk B) of factor 10-5 (filter penetration of < 1 in 100,000 batches), a maximum batch
volume of 46 L is acceptable in a very conservative scenario by sampling 30 mL with an acceptance
limit of 3 CFU/30 mL. That means with a pre-sterile bioburden limit of 3 CFU/30 mL only 1 batch
out of 100,000 batches would have a theoretical risk of bioburden breakthrough.
As the actual batch volume for the manufacturing process applied at BAG is with 5.2 – 21.5 kg
(corresponding to 4.9 – 20.3 L) lower, the validated filter retention capacity is significantly higher
with > 6 × 107 CFU/cm² and the sampling volume is with two times 50 mL notably larger than in
the calculation, the probability of a bioburden breakthrough is even further decreased.
BAG two filtration steps are performed: a bioburden reduction filtration and the sterile filtration.
For the bioburden reduction filtration, the same sterile grade filter is applied assuring the same
microbiological retention capacity during bioburden reduction filtration and a very low bioburden
load prior inline sterile filtration. The bioburden reduction filtration is employed as a precaution
only. The unfiltered bulk solution has already a low bioburden, as the bulk solution is provided
bioburden controlled.
Apart from this, the pre-sterile filtration bioburden testing is only one piece in the integral process
control strategy which also includes further measures applied by BAG to control the microbiological
quality of Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL vial as summarized below:
 
Formulated Drug Substance (FDS) utilized in the manufacturing process is microbiologically
controlled with a release specification limit of ≤ 1 CFU/10 mL as presented in CTD section
S.4.1.01-01.
 
The sterile filtration and filling process is conducted by trained operators under aseptic
conditions compliant to recent cGMP guidelines. Sterile filtration is conducted in a Grade C
environment. Aseptic filling of vials is performed in a Grade A isolator environment under
LAF surrounded by a Grade C environment involving equipment which is single use.
 
The sterilizing filter was validated in a worst-case approach. A retention capacity of at least
6.0 × 107 bacteria per cm2 filter was proven for Brevundimonas diminuta (as described in
CTD section A.1.03-01) which is exceeding the requirements as per
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/BWP/850374/2015 (retention capacity 107 bacteria per cm2 filter).
 
During the manufacture of Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL vial two filtration steps are
performed with the same microbiological retention capacity.
 
For both filtrations, pre-filtration bioburden is controlled by testing with a total testing
volume of 100 mL (two times 50 mL of the Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL each for
TAMC and TYMC with a limit ≤ 5 CFU/50 mL each).
 
The manufacturing hold times are controlled and minimized between processing steps.
Refrigerated storage of process intermediates further reduces the risk of microbial growth
in the course of the manufacturing process.
 
Release samples are tested for sterility as critical quality attribute indicative for microbial
contamination.
The aforementioned procedures efficiently mitigate risks of bioburden preload or contamination
during processing as acknowledged by the pharmaceutical industry (Bechtold-Peters K:Eur J Pharm
Biopharm:2024:198:114151, “Risk-based approach to setting sterile filtration microbial bioburden
limits – Focus on biotech-derived products”), and as also supported by the applicant’s experience in
the manufacture of Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL presentations. Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL in
vials and PFS, which are using the same kind of control strategy, demonstrated no concern with
regards to sterility since marketing of the product in 2012. In particular, the experience with
Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL presentations underlines the suitability of the IPC in controlling the
manufacturing process when being embedded in a holistic approach to control microbiological
quality.
In summary, the bioburden testing method compliant with Ph.Eur. 2.6.12, with a sampling volume
of two times 50 mL and an acceptance criterion of ≤ 5 CFU/50 mL for TAMC and TYMC each,
sufficiently ensures detection requirements for in-process testing as part of the overall product
control strategy. The IPC is embedded in a set of further control measures to ensure
packaging materials are tightly controlled. The applicant is convinced that the collective measures
which are implemented to control microbiological quality, as validated, are adequate to assure
sterility and quality of the finished product.

Question:
Question 1
A) In the FDS process validation of Regeneron Ireland,
- Justification of acceptance criteria of protein concentration in UF/DF process
- TMP limit and result of UF/DF process in all batches
B) Hold time data of Intermediate performed by Regeneron Ireland (microbial and physicochemical stability data per process)
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.S.2.5):
A) In the FDS process validation of Regeneron Ireland,
- Justification of acceptance criteria of protein concentration in UF/DF process
During manufacturing process development, the acceptable manufacturing range for the target final concentrated pool (FCP) protein concentration was established based on development and characterization studies, and historical manufacturing experience. A high protein concentration in the FCP would be diluted through the sucrose adjustment and formulation unit operations to acceptable levels. A low protein concentration at the FCP stage could cause over-dilution during formulation, potentially leading to a formulated drug substance (FDS) that is below the specified range. The established range for commercial manufacturing (165-184 g/L) is considered a non-critical process condition to be met during routine manufacture to ensure process consistency.
Typically in Biotech processes, the final concentrated pool after ultrafiltration/diafiltration, is set clearly higher than the actual minimal needed concentration.
In addition to the target FCP protein concentration, the lower limit for the FCP protein concentration was then set and classified as a critical quality attribute (CQA).
The CQA (≥ 128.8 g/L) is the minimum FCP protein concentration necessary to ensure that the material produced will have a concentration that is compatible with further product dilution and formulation steps. Additional details are provided in Error! Reference source not found. below.
Following the ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF) unit operation, during the formulation step, there is a dilution due to the addition of the sucrose buffer, excipient buffer and dilution buffer. The acceptance criteria (≥ 128.8 g/L) was established as the minimal concentration needed at the FCP stage to ensure that the FDS will be within the final release specifications (103 - 126 g/L) after the addition of the three buffers.
B) TMP limit and result of UF/DF process in all batches
Please see below for the UF/DF feed flow rate and transmembrane pressure results and limits.
The excursions below the allowable transmembrane pressure (TMP) and feed flow rate limits of lot 8337700061 were attributed to restarting the primary concentration phase following an unintentional hold in the method, which had no impact to validation as there was not an increase in high molecular weight formation for batch lot 8337700061. (see S.2.5.01_022985518_01 point 2.1.4. Concentration and Diafiltration Process Step Performance).

While chemical stability is equipment and solution dependent, and microbial stability is equipment dependent, both chemical and microbial stability are site independent. The same hold bags and a closed system is used. A point-by-point justification for referring to PA2X hold time validation is given in Table 3-2.

Question:
Question 2
- Justification of specification by assessing release test of Vial and PFS
- MFI analysis result and consideration of PFS
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (3.2.S.4.5; 3.2.P.2.2; 3.2.P.2.4; 3.2.P.5.6; 3.2.R.2):
Justification of specification by assessing release test of Vial and PFS
The statistical methodology typically used by the applicant for the calculation of batch release comparability limits are 95% confidence/ 99% coverage tolerance intervals (TIs). This methodology was not applied here, because the same methodology was used for the calculation of the vial batch release specification acceptance criteria using almost the same set of historical vial batches that was available for the comparability exercise between drug product (DP) in vial and DP in PFS. For the calculation of specification acceptance criteria for DP in vial please refer to CTD section S.4.5.01-01 and P.5.6.01-01.
For the comparability exercise between DP in vial and DP in PFS only three further vial batches, i.e. the three vial comparator batches, were available. Therefore, the minimum/ maximum range of the available vial batches was used as a benchmark for the comparability exercise, which is a more stringent approach compared to 95% confidence/ 99% coverage tolerance intervals. The 95% confidence/ 99% TIs are provided in the Table 2 together with the statistics as reported in CTD section R.2.02-02. Note that for SE-UPLC a decimal place was added to the statistics. All TIs are wider than the respective minimum/ maximum range.
Comparing the results of the PFS against the historical vial min and max values is therefore considered justified for assessing the comparability between PFS and vial.

MFI analysis result and consideration of PFS
As the glass syringe barrel is lubricated with silicone oil to ensure the movement of plunger stoppers and as the syringe tips are manufactured under the employment of tungsten format parts, the impact on the quality of the drug product was thoroughly assessed for both components.
In a first study, silicone oil and tungsten were spiked to Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL to analyze the stability of the product using a Design of Experience approach. Spiking concentrations corresponded to 10%, 100%, and 200% of the specified maximum silicone oil content of the syringe, respectively the specified maximum tungsten content of the syringe.
Comprehensive results are presented in the CTD section P.2.2.10-02. Overall, no meaningful changes were observed in physical appearance, clarity, color, pH, protein concentration and protein integrity over the course of 24 months storage at 5 °C. Further, no meaningful increases in subvisible particulates measured by microscopy were observed. Overall, all acceptance limits were met.
The data confirmed the compatibility of the Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL formulation with potential residues of free silicone oil and tungsten and confirmed the compatibility of Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL with the container closure system (see CTD section P.2.2.10-02).
In a second study, the overall risk of a potential silicone (oil) leaching into the drug product solution was analyzed. Syringes of technical batches filled at Vetter were subjected to different stresses that were applied either under lab conditions or at commercial scale equipment.
The stressed syringes were analyzed regarding the potential silicone oil transfer using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) and flow imaging microscopy (MFI). The MFI software was applying a filter to dedicatedly count for silicone oil droplets/particles.
Samples measured by MFI and ICP-OES were subjected to pressure changes (to simulate potential stopper movement during air transport as well as during the outer surface sterilization process) and intensive shaking using a vortex device. Overall, as presented in Table 3 and Table 4 no increase of silicone oil particles and free silicone oil compared to the unstressed control was observed.
Independent of the tested scenarios and analytical methods, all data for the technical batches fall in the range of expected method and sample variability.
Further, extractable studies were performed with primary packaging components including the syringe barrel. Extraction was performed with water and 50% ethanol. Analysis was performed with LC-MS, GC-MS and HC-GC-MS. Thereby, in none of the extractable solvents silicone containing organic compounds exceeding the safety concern threshold of 1.5 ug/day were detected (see CTD section P.2.4.06-01).
The extractable results are further confirmed in the leachable stability study of three Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL PPQ finally packaged batches. Results after storage of 12 months are available, no silicone containing organic leachable compounds have been detected in concentrations above the reporting threshold of 1.0 µg/mL of AFL 114.3 mg/mL solution (CTD section P.2.4.07-01). The study is continued up to the end of 24 months shelf life.
Overall, the studies performed do not indicate a product quality risk with regards to silicone and tungsten particles and confirmed the compatibility of Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL with the container closure system.

Question 3

Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 3 (3.2.P.2.4; 3.2.P.2.6; 3.2.P.8.3):
3.1)
Detailed results of the extractable study are provided and leachable study data including study design, storage conditions and results were included in the respective CTD sections P.2.4.06-01 and P.2.4.07-01, respectively.

3.2)
The applicant would like to describe the difference between the evaluated in-use stability time of 6 hours at 25°C (for the PFS as prepared for dosing) and the 24 h at 25°C reserved for Health Care Professionals (HCP´s) handling of the unopened blister of Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in prefilled syringe (PFS).
The proposed label of Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in PFS includes the following statement: “Prior to usage, the unopened blister pack of EYLEA 8 mg may be stored at room temperature (25 °C / 77°F) for up to 24 hours”. The applicant would like to point out that 24 hours described in this statement does not refer to the compatibility (“in-use stability”) study described in CTD section P.2.6.01-01.
Whereas the proposed label statement refers to the unopened blister with intact sterile barrier and is based on the assessment of the overall time out of refrigeration (TOR) described in section P.8.3.11-04.
In this dedicated study the maximum TOR for Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in PFS was assessed as part of the overall process validation. The total TOR for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL drug product (DP) in PFS covers the end-to-end manufacturing time consisting of filling, labeling, assembly, blistering, sterilization and packaging as well as the time for distribution and delivery of the finished goods to the patient. For Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in PFS, the overall TOR is defined and controlled, and the maximum TOR includes 24 h reserved for HCP´s handling to allow storage of the unopened blister prior to usage at room temperature. For this study, currently, all available 24 months stability results are within the shelf-life specification. Very few data points were pending at the time of finalization of this response document.
Furthermore, as the results of the analytical comparability program demonstrate that the PFS manufacturing process (sterilized PFS were used) yields Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL drug product that is analytically comparable to the drug product manufactured in vial, the generated vial data should provide sufficient confidence that also for PFS storage at 25°C for 24 h is supported.
The overall data supports the claim that the unopened blister can be stored at room temperature for up to 24 hours.
On the other hand, the applicant provided data proving the compatibility of the drug product solution with the injection needle. This dedicated “in-use stability” study is described in CTD section P.2.6.01-01. After exposure to the maximum TOR following the concept described in P.8.3.11-04 PFS were taken out of blister, needles were attached, PFS were primed and held primed (prior the injection step) for up to 6 hours at 25°C. Subsequently, the DP was analyzed. The data confirm that there was no quality impairment due to the contact of the DP with the inner lumen of the injection needle for up to 6 hours at 25 °C and that the product is stable in a primed syringe stage. This study was intended to confirm the compatibility with the administration configuration prior to application. The data was obtained to increase the knowledge of the drug product and it is not foreseen to define a specific in-use stability time.

- The data of functional performance test of Drug Product considering shelf-life
- In the DP process validation, the actual result of functional performance test (including justification of functional test of PFS considering shelf-life)
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (3.2.P.3.5; 3.2.P.8.3):
Functional performance has successfully been tested as part of ongoing real-time stability studies for a duration of 24 months to date. Results are provided in the CTD section P.8.3.11-02. All acceptance criteria were met for the functional performance tests during long term storage.
Functional performance is evaluated as an in-process control within the overall control strategy. This testing has been conducted during the DP process validation and will continue to be upheld throughout commercial manufacturing.
Functional performance testing is conducted in accordance with ISO 2859-1 Sampling procedures for inspection by attributes — Part 1: Sampling schemes indexed by acceptance quality limit (AQL) for lot-by-lot inspection“, which provides a sampling plan and procedure for the acceptance of batches based on the inspection of a sample set. This standard outlines the methodology for determining whether a batch of product meets specified quality requirements without providing specific actual results or values.
The evaluation process under ISO 2859-1 involves the testing of a representative sample size from a manufacturing batch and the assessment against predetermined acceptance criteria. The acceptance or rejection of manufacturing batches is based on the number of samples found in the batch specific sample set that are conforming or nonconforming with the acceptance criteria. The test results are reported as “pass” or “complies” as shown in P.3.5.01-01.

Question:
Question 5
A) Assessment data on effects of exposure to refrigeration and room temperature of drug product on Endotoxin test result (Low Endotoxin Recovery)
B) Justification of specification of Particulate Matter Content
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 5:
A)
Endotoxin test results after exposure to refrigeration and room temperature are available for the formulated drug substance (FDS) and are provided in CTD section S.4.3.01-02. The results show no impact to endotoxin recovery for FDS when held at refrigerated conditions or at room temperature.
The FDS has the same composition as the drug product solution and resultantly, it can be assumed that also for the drug product testing low endotoxin recovery does not occur.
To confirm the absence of LER, a dedicated study was conducted at the manufacturing and testing site at Vetter Pharma. The results met the predefined requirements and are provided in the final study report.

B)
Specification acceptance criteria for Subvisible Particulate Matter Content are integral part of Ph. Eur. chapter 2.9.19. The sub-chapter “ Method 2. Microscopic particle count test” states under Evaluation “Test 2.B – Solutions for infusion or solutions for injection supplied in containers with a nominal content of less than 100 mL: The preparation complies with the test if the average number of particles present in the units tested does not exceed 3000 per container equal to or greater than 10 µm and does not exceed 300 per container equal to or greater than 25 µm”. The submitted and more stringent specification acceptance criteria of ≤ 200 particles/mL for ≥ 10 µm particles and ≤ 20 particles/mL for ≥ 25 µm particles were harmonized with the specification acceptance criteria approved and in place for Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL in prefilled syringe. These proposed limits already constitute a significant tightening versus the limits allowed per Ph. Eur. for parental solutions, considering also that Ph. Eur. limits refer to particles allowed per container and the proposed limits refer to particles/mL. Based on the target fill volume of 0.184 mL/PFS the currently proposed acceptance criteria in particles/mL equate to ~37 particles/container for ≥ 10 µm particles and ~4 particles/container for ≥ 25 µm particles, and thus constitute a tightening by a factor of ~81 when compared to acceptance criteria per container stated in Ph. Eur. chapter 2.9.19.
Moreover, for particulate matter content the currently available data set for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL is considered as too limited to derive tighter specification limits. Subvisible particulate matter results are known to not be normally distributed and it is thus difficult to predict the range of future results. The applicant therefore considers the proposed limits of ≤ 200 particles/mL for ≥ 10 µm particles and ≤ 20 particles/mL for ≥ 25 µm particles as justified.

Source: Eylea_114.3 mg-mL_PFS_LER_Report_signed (new)

Question:

Variations number 4 and 5:
In principle, the replacement of an IPC with reference to a process parameter is an example of 
enhanced pharmaceutical development. No development of the manufacturing process could 
be found in the submitted documentation, and this was not discussed in the Quality overall 
summary.
Normally, demonstration that an IPC can be replaced by a controlled (set of) process 
parameter is provided in section 3.2.P.2.3. Development data should be presented to justify 
that a mixing time of 40 minutes provides assurance that the drug substance is 
homogenous in the elastomer mixture.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( P.3.3.01 ;P.3.5.01):
There is no actual change in the manufacturing process of Mirena in connection of the 
deletion of mass homogeneity IPC.  Furthermore, the IPCs, Concentration of levonorgestrel 
and Homogeneity, can’t be considered as two separate IPC tests, as they are both obtained and 
calculated from exactly the same blend analysis.
Bayer has manufactured Mirena batches for 30 years already and hence the mixing process is 
well established, and therefore proven to produce homogenous levonorgestrel-elastomer 
mixtures. In order to support the IPC deletion the actual mixing time (at least 40 minutes) 
applied on the product over the years was added and specified as an IPC to substitute the 
homogeneity test. Therefore, the proposed IPCs are only adapting to the actual conditions of 
the manufacturing process.
An updated process validation report P.3.5.01_02 in which the mixing time of min. 40 
minutes has been observed and reported is provided to the competent Health Authority for 
review. In this validation study homogenous mixtures were achieved with the mixing time of 
40 minutes.
As a further assurance of the continuously homogenous mixtures achieved in the mixing step 
of Mirena data on recent 283 batches (manufactured between 03.01.2024 and 31.01.2025) of 
Mirena is provided. The data refers to average results of 4 IPC samples collected from these 
283 batches, which means that the data in graphs and histograms is based on 1132 blend 
samples in total.
The requirement for the average levonorgestrel concentration is 48 – 52 %, and the RSD of 4 
determinations must be ≤ 2 %. The average results of 283 batches fall between 47.9 and 50.8 
%, with the average of all determinations as  49.4 %. Average of the calculated RSD values is 
0.4 %. maximum observed RSD has been 1.6 %.
The data provided reliably verifies that mixing process of Mirena results into a homogenous 
mixture when mixed for 40 minutes. Therefore, Bayer considers deletion of the homogeneity 
IPC justified.

Question:
Question 2
Variation number 6:
The IPC bioburden limit was widened, apparently without any justification or discussion. 
Justification for the widening of bioburden IPC should be provided.
Answer:
The action limit for pre-sterilization bioburden of Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery system 
52 mg with inserter (MIRENA), max 100 CFU/unit, has been widely accepted by the 
authorities.
Alert limits (internal, based on trend) and action limits for Mirena have been defined in line 
with EN ISO 11737 and EN ISO 11135. For the action level, Bayer Oy refers to ISO 11737-1 
Table C.1, where max 100 CFU is considered as a low bioburden, and the EMA guideline 
(EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015) that mentions 100 CFU/100 g as an acceptable 
limit for parenteral finished products in case of heat sterilized products.
Manufacturing of MIRENA takes place in a clean room and contains steps that may reduce 
microbial contamination, thus exceeding the action level seldom happens. However, 
bioburden spikes can occasionally be detected, that according to EN ISO 11737-1 may be a 
normal and consistent part of the bioburden but shall be evaluated for the impact as 
appropriate (A.8.5 Bioburden spikes). In cleanliness class C, microbial contamination is 
typically due to the personnel and may not be evenly distributed in the batch. The 
contamination will be eliminated by the validated overkill sterilization process. In any case, 
according to the current Bayer Oy procedure, exceeding either the action level or two 
subsequent times the alert level, will trigger a root cause investigation both in the laboratory 
and in the production. This investigation includes an assessment of the criticality of the 
contamination with respect to the sterilization process and product release.
Therefore, according to the opinion of Bayer Oy the minor change in the bioburden limit of 
Mirena does not compromise the quality of the product. The change is justified and may be 
executed after the approval of the competent Health Authority.

Source:  P.3.3.01_01 Manufacturing Process and Process Controls / Levonorgestrel
intrauterine delivery system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#022984888; 
unchanged)

Question:
Question 2

Please explain and provide evidence that removing the plastic tray covering the syringe does not affect the stability of the drug.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 2:

We propose to replace the current blister packaging with a cardboard divider for the pre-filled syringes (PFS) and plunger rods. The new packaging design will securely hold the plunger rod and PFS in place by automatically inserting the cardboard divider into the folding box. This ensures that both units remain fixed, preventing movement and reducing the risk of breakage.

The cardboard divider offers protection equivalent to the current blister by stabilizing the components inside the folding box, ensuring product integrity. This change is being implemented to improve packaging efficiency and sustainability while maintaining the same level of protection.

Please note that the new packaging design does not affect the quality or stability of the medicinal product throughout its storage period. Secondary packaging including the blister has no impact on product stability of Gadovist PFS during shelf life. Gadovist stability samples are routinely stored in climate chambers without blister or any other secondary packaging material such as plunger rods, cardboard boxes, or other country-specific packaging. Therefore, this change does not impact our ongoing stability commitments.

Additionally, this modification aligns with our sustainability goals by reducing plastic usage and minimizing associated costs, contributing to an environmentally responsible packaging solution.

Question:
Question 2
Unless data are available to support the 70% lower limit for assay of sodium calcium edetate, 
the limit should be tightened based on the results that are available for this product from the 
Japanese market.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (CTD section):
We would like to inform you, that excipient disodium edetate in the existing approved 
formulation (with star anise oil) is replaced by sodium calcium edetate serving the same 
pharmaceutical function as complexing agent in proposed formulation (without star anise oil). 
Hence, the proposed assay limits of sodium calcium edetate are kept in line with the existing 
approved assay limits of disodium edetate (70%-110%).
As the test of sodium calcium edetate is not mandatory as per Japan market requirement; it is 
not included in shelf-life specification for Japan. Hence, additional testing has been conducted 
on the available Japanese batches to verify the assay values. These results demonstrated the 
assay of sodium calcium edetate are complying with proposed limits (70%-110%). However 
as this data was collected at a different time points of  3, 40, 50 and 51 months; we would like 
to monitor real-time stability data for sodium calcium edetate in new additional batches 
(Batch Numbers: MA04L9S, MA04L9T, MA04L9U) manufactured and placed on stability 
according to established requirements in ICH Q1A. Currently 3 months stability data of these 
batches is available and provided in the 3.2.P.8.3 section with this response.
Given that the existing 3 months stability data is not sufficient to conclude the lower limit of 
the sodium calcium edetate assay, Bayer AG acknowledges and emphasizes to tighten the 
same in future based on availability of real time stability data till shelf life.

After reviewing the submitted reply on 27/01/25 , the following are required ;
Regarding the CoA of the formulated bulk FB :

1-The color test specs in the CoA is Colorless to reference standard BY6 however it is 
Colorless to reference standard BY5 in the re-reg specs
2-The Potency by Cell-based Bioassay specs in the CoA is 60 – 140% reference standard 
IC50 (4-P fit ) & 60 – 135 % reference standard IC50 (5-P fit ) however in the re-reg file it is 
60 – 140% reference standard IC50 only
3-Potency by binding assay test is present in the CoA however it is not present in the re-reg 
specs.
4-Polysorbate 20 % test is present in the CoA however it is not present in the re-reg specs.

Clarification is required
Additionally , EMA approval required for above changes
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.3.4):

The 40mg/ml formulated bulk (FB) specification P.3.4.02#019983643_02 is the same for 
Egypt and the European Union including Germany as the country of origin and for most 
countries globally.

The FB specification was approved by EMA with procedure EMEA/H/C/002392/IB/0057/G, 
in 2019 and amended with the current change MAT2023 as approved by EMA procedure with 
EMEA/H/C/002392/IB/0083/G in 2022. Therefore, the formulated bulk specifications in  
P.3.4.02#019983643_02 are approved and considered by EMA to be sufficient to control the 
product quality.

In addition to the global FB specification valid in the EU and in Egypt, some countries (for 
example China) have required additional testing according to their national Pharmacopoeia 
and Guidelines. These include a different data evaluation for the bioassay, to repeat the 
binding assay which is already part of the aflibercept drug substance intermediate
specification in Egypt and in the EU and the re-testing of the PS20 excipient concentration 
after its addition. The parameters tested by these tests are considered to already be controlled 
by earlier testing, equivalent tests or other process controls for the EU.

Because the same quality Eylea is applied globally, the CoA displays all tests even if 
performed by request for a single country.

Question:
Question 1
Uniformity of Dosage units: The MAH has tightened the L2 limit for the test (L2 = 14 %). 
The L2 limit in the release specifications should be revised accordingly. Also the minimum 
and maximum value at stage L1 should be corrected on the release specifications document.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( 3.2.P.5.2.01):
In the proposed Uniformity of dosage units test the requirements for the test are as follows:
At Level 1 (i.e.when testing with 10 individual products) L1 limit (Acceptance value) is 15.0 
%, but L2 limit (Range) is set as 14.0 % which means that all individuals must be within 
range 86.0 - 114.0%. If at Level 1 one of the individuals fall outside the limits, 20 new units 
are analyzed (Level 2) and all 30 units are used to calculate and evaluate the result.
In the proposed specifications the acceptance criteria are as follows:
• 
L1, Maximum allowed acceptance value, = 15.0
• 
L2, Maximum allowed range for deviation of each dosage unit tested from the calculated 
value of M, = 14.0 (i.e. range for individuals is 86.0 – 114.0 %)
MAH applies these same L1 and L2 limits also for testing at Level 2, i.e. when the testing is 
performed with 30 individual products. L1 limit (Acceptance value) is 15.0 %, and the L2 
limit (Range) is again set as 14.0 % which means that all individuals must be within range 
86.0 - 114.0%. The harmonized Pharmacopoeial test allows here L2 limit as 25.0 % which 
means that the individuals must be within range 75.0 - 125.0%.

Question:
Question 1
The specification should contain the requirements for microbiological quality and description 
of the procedure (specify the presence or absence of antimicrobial activity, description of 
sample preparation specifying the amount of test sample and diluent (for each dilution); if the 
membrane filtration method is used, specify the amount of washing fluid; provide a brief 
description of the procedure and culture conditions). The response to this observation should 
include the procedure description as a covering letter in Section 1.0; then the procedure 
description should be included in the Quality ND.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
Please be informed that Microbial purity test is included in both Release Specifications and 
Shelf-life specifications section (P.5.1.01 and P.5.1.02), along with the acceptance criterion 
and the method used. It is also included in the Test procedure section (P.5.2.01).
The medicinal product Diane-35 does not demonstrate antimicrobial activity under the test 
conditions. All ingredients are provided by qualified suppliers and regularly tested for 
microbial purity. The manufacturing process of the drug product is conducted under defined 
cleanliness classes and regularly controlled by appropriate environmental monitoring.
Please find the response below for Microbial Purity with the additional information which 
includes description of sample preparation indicating the diluent, dilution of the medicinal 
product, inoculation method.
Microbial purity:
The method for the microbiological purity is sufficiently described in the Ph. Eur. 2.6.12, 
USP <61> or JP 4.05 (harmonized method). The test for specified microorganisms are 
described in detail in Ph. Eur. 2.6.13, USP <62> or JP 4.05 (harmonized method) as well.
Procedure:
Weigh out not less than 10 g of the test product. Fill up with the appropriate amount of Casein 
soya bean digest broth (CSB) to obtain a 1:10 dilution (solution 1).
For TAMC prepare 2 petri dishes with each 1 mL of solution 1 and fill with 15-20 mL liquid 
Casein soya bean digest agar (CSA) (approx. 45°C). Incubate 3 – 5 days at 30 – 35°C. (Pour-
Plate Method of the Plate-Count method).
For TYMC prepare 2 petri dishes with each 1 mL of solution 1 and fill with 15-20 mL liquid 
Sabouraud-dextrose agar with chloramphenicol (approx. 45°C). Incubate 5 – 7 days at 20 – 
25°C. (Pour-Plate Method of the Plate-Count method).
For the test for absence of Escherichia coli, add 10 mL of solution 1 to 100 mL of Soya bean 
digest broth (CSB) to obtain solution 1.1. Incubate 18 – 24 h at 30 – 35°C. After incubation, 1 
mL of solution 1.1 is diluted in 100 mL MacConkey Broth and incubated 24 - 48 h at 42 -
44°C. After this incubation step, plate an aliquot on MacConkey agar and incubate 18 - 72 h 
at 30 – 35°C.

Question:
Question 1
Validation data for the manufacturing process is to be submitted for three batches in terms of 
preparation of the hormone-elastomer mixture, mechanical assembly and sterilisation stage.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.3.5):
Process validation for three Mirena batches enclosed herewith the response.
There is no actual change in the manufacturing process of Mirena in connection of the 
deletion of mass homogeneity IPC, and the manual assembly process, which has not been in 
use for years.
Bayer has manufactured Mirena batches for 30 years already and hence the mixing process is 
well established, and therefore proven to produce homogenous levonorgestrel-elastomer 
mixtures. To support the IPC deletion, the actual mixing time used in the mixing process of 
Mirena (at least 40 minutes) which has been applied on the product over the years is now 
accurately defined as an IPC. The final mixing time has been described as “Final mixing time 
is about 40 minutes”, though the mixing has been performed for exactly 40 minutes 
throughout the years. Therefore, the proposed mixing time IPC as “not less than 40 minutes” 
is only adaptation according to the actual conditions of the manufacturing process for 
supporting deletion of the homogeneity IPC test.
An updated process validation report P.3.5.01_02 in which the mixing time of min. 40 
minutes has been observed and reported is provided to the competent Health Authority for 
review. In this validation study homogenous mixtures were achieved with the mixing time of 
40 minutes. The assembly of Mirena has been performed with the mechanical process in this 
process validation. The manual assembly of Mirena has not been performed for years 
anymore. The validation batches were sterilized in the ETO3 sterilization chamber used at 
Bayer Oy. All the requirements set for the validation were fulfilled. Old ETO2 chamber has 
not been used for years.
Though the homogeneity IPC is deleted from the list of IPCs to be performed on routine 
production batches, homogeneity will be tested in connection of new validations to be 
performed on the mixing process also in future.

Question:
Question 4
In section 3.2.P.3.3 - Mechanical assembly of the IUS units - it is stated that the tubes are cut 
to a target length of 22 mm. However, the limits for the length of the tube (hormone core) are 
between 19 - 20 mm. This length inconsistency should be explained and corrected in sections 
3.2.P.3.3 and 3.2.P.3.4.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (3.2.P.3.3.):
The mechanical assembly step is described as follows:
Hormone-elastomer tubing (also called hormone elastomer core) is cut to core segments of a 
specified length (addition to this point: ca. 19.5 mm) with a cutting unit on the automated 
assembly machine. The drug core segment is inserted into poly(dimethylsiloxane) elastomer 
tubing i.e. into poly(dimethylsiloxane) metering membrane, and the tubing is cut into 
segments of a target length 22 mm. The term 'reservoir matrix' is used to describe the obtained 
product.  T-body is inserted through the lumen of the reservoir matrix.
The length of the drug core segment inserted into the tubing is ca 19.5 mm, and the length of 
the tubing is ca 22 mm. The IPC requirements for the length of the drug core are 19.0 – 20.0 
mm. The tubing must be longer (ca. 22 mm) and therefore the IPCs for the assembly step are 
containing camera check for the overhangs of tubing as 1 – 2 mm for both ends of the drug 
reservoir. 
 
We have added the length of the core piece (ca. 19.5 mm) into the description of the 
mechanical assembly step of Mirena for review to the competent Health Authority for 
attaining more clarity concerning the defined lengths in the documentation.
Source:  P.3.3.01_02 Manufacturing Process and Process Controls / Levonorgestrel
intrauterine delivery system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#022984965; 
amended)
