however, small differences in the Released amount of Levonorgestrel during the 8 days’ 
period. Therefore, slightly different limits are set, and justified, for the specified testing points 
(Days 2, 5 and 8).
A minorly decreasing trend in median of results (22.8 µg - 21.2 µg - 21.2 µg) and a minorly 
decreasing variation of the results (Standard deviation: 2.2 - 1.6 - 1.5) are seen during the 
testing period. These differences justify the small distinction in the calculated, specified limits 
for the three sampling days.
Secondly, the completely new sampling points, Days 2 and 5, and their requirements are 
based solely on the batch data currently available. This data is collected in a reasonably short 
period of time. Therefore, some space is needed for long-term variability arising from routine 
manufacturing and analytics for the complex product in question. Thirdly, the most important 
sampling point of the new method, Day 8, corresponds to the single point, Day 15, of the 
current method and their results are very comparable, almost superimposed. This has been the 
target for the new Release Rate method’s development. Earlier there were limits only for 
individuals, but now the limits are set for the batch average, with the addition of the Level 
testing procedure which is now set for the test.
In general, the new specification is tighter than the current specification as the new limits are 
set for the 3-points whereas the current method had limits for the single point only. The Level 
testing procedure is set applying by Ph. Eur. chapter 2.9.3. including criteria for batch average 
and a tighter Level L3 ranges are set than required by the pharmacopoeia (±15% is applied 
instead of ±20%). In the Level testing procedure, the batch average limits are the limits for 
individuals in the Level L1 and this is a tight criterion and therefore a powerful way to ensure 
the long-term performance of the release rate is maintained.
Based on the above Bayer considers the proposed specification as well justified. The new 
specification can be applied to Mirena IUS without compromising the quality of the 
production batches.

Figure 1:  Plot of Individual Release Rates of the 42 Batches by the 3-Point Method. 
All Results are in µg/day Units. Lines are Fitted between Medians and Averages. 
Green markers are added to visualize the limits set for individuals in the Level L1 
(note, they are the limits for the batch average in Levels L2 and L3).


Source:  P.5.6.01-03 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#007344957; unchanged)

Question:
Question 10
With regard to the dissolution limits, an explanation is requested as to why a fairly early point 
(<24 h) was not tested, given that it may be more discriminating.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.P.5.1):
The first sampling point of the proposed release rate method is Day 2. The test starts on Day 1 
and the cumulative release of the hormone is analyzed from the dissolution solution on Day 2, 
therefore the sample contains all API released during the first 24 hours (no solution is 
discharged, all released material is analyzed). The Day 2 results are slightly higher but very 
similar as the results on Day 5 and 8 (see Question 9) verifying the release during the first 24
hours is stable. Based on tests on IUSs with defects, e.g., membrane defect causing 
abnormally high release (burst) or low hormone load causing abnormally low release, Day 2 
is discriminating, and no separate sampling point earlier than at 24 hours is needed. Also, it 
should be noted that the release rate is specified as micrograms (ca. 20 µg only) of 
levonorgestrel released per day (24h, i.e. µg/day).  
 
Therefore, Bayer Oy considers the proposed testing point selection of the Release Rate 
method justified.
Source:  P.5.6.01-03 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#007344957; unchanged)

Question:
Question 11
For impurity limits, these must be included in the release and expiry finished product 
specifications for individual impurities (specified and unspecified) and total impurities. 
Therefore, removal of total impurities at release is not acceptable. On the other hand, the 
tightening from max 2.0% to max 1.0% is acceptable.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 11 (3.2.P.5.1):
The test procedure for impurities in Mirena IUS has been revised to include only 
levonorgestrel (LNG) related degradation products, not any more synthesis related impurities 
as the current test. This approach is in line with the EMA guideline CPMP/ICH/2738/99 (ICH 
Q3B). The guideline states: “impurities present in the drug substance need not be monitored 
or specified in the drug product specifications unless they are also degradation products”.
This new test is removed from Release Specifications, i.e. it will be included in the shelf life 
testing only. To support the change, the acceptance limit for the sum of the degradation 
products is tightened from NMT 2.0% to NMT 1.0%. The potential known and unidentified 
LNG degradation products above ≥ 0.1% reporting threshold are included in the test results.
Levonorgestrel is inherently stable. The long history of Mirena IUS has verified that LNG 
remains virtually unchanged in the product manufacture, and during the shelf-life. This is 
demonstrated by comparing results of five MIRENA IUS drug product stability batches with 
the results for corresponding drug substance batches (P.5.6.01). The results for drug 
substance batches in accordance with the Ph. Eur. method indicate actual low amount of the 
degradation products for Mirena IUS as the synthesis related impurities need not to 
be included in the results. This is shown to be true for the drug product batches listed, as the 
maximum result for the Sum of degradation products is only 0.1 %.
The daily dose released from a Mirena IUS is ca. 20 μg. According to the EMA guideline 
CPMP/ICH/2738/99 the identification threshold for impurities in a drug product with a 
maximum daily dose of 1 mg is 1.0% or 5 μg Total Daily Intake (TDI), whichever is lower.
The potential known and unidentified LNG degradation products above 0.1% reporting 
threshold are included in the specifications of Mirena. Calculated as daily intake an impurity 
at 0.1 % level in Mirena provides a daily intake of 0.02 μg only. The level of possible 
unspecified degradation products in Mirena are therefore far below the identification 
threshold of 5 μg TDI. Even the sum of all degradation products calculated as daily intake 
(1.0 % of 20 μg daily dose) is ca. 0.2 μg (TDI) only.
Based on the arguments above the non-inclusion of the impurity test into the release 
specification of Mirena is well justified.

Source:  P.5.6.01_03 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#007344957, unchanged)

Question:
Question 10
Transport chain validation is submitted; however, this only covers internal routes inside USA. 
Validation that supports the transportation chain to Chile (or another in the region that 
represents a worst-case situation) must be submitted.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.R):
The impact of transportation on the final packed drug product was assessed by a shipping 
simulation study. This study was performed according to ASTM D4169 “Standard Practice 
for Performance Testing of Shipping Containers and Systems” and covers global transport by 
truck, ship and aircraft as worst-case conditions. Maximum load and minimum load 
configurations were subjected to the simulations.
The executed study was performed as a shipping simulation to apply controlled and 
reproducible conditions regarding shock, vibration and pressure ensuring that the edges of the 
real-world transport were tested. The simulation approach was chosen to demonstrate product 
stability in a reproducible and controlled worst-case scenario as otherwise selected road

Question: Please justify how a delivery dose of 0.045 mL (low limit of the acceptance criterion for delivered dose volume) meets the intended dose of 0.050 mL.
Answer: Maximum efforts have been made to reduce the variability of dosing and extreme values of expelled drug from the Aflibercept 40 mg/mL PFS. The range around the mean, in this case, the minimum expelled volume, was chosen because a considerable amount of Bayer Phase 3 clinical evidence is available on the efficacy and safety of early Aflibercept 40 mg/mL PFS generations which had a lower tolerance limit of 0.045 mL. Specifically, four clinical studies within the Eylea clinical development program, each of which has an intended administered dose of 0.050 mL, provide evidence of the suitability of the lower tolerance limit of 0.045 mL. It was observed from the use of the previous Aflibercept 40 mg/mL PFS generations that the lower bound could be as low as 45 μl without signals of loss of efficacy or safety concerns. The efficacy and safety of regular dosing of Aflibercept 40 mg/mL using a PFS with a lower tolerance limit of 0.045 mL was shown in the VISTA Study (Phase 3 DME, N=466), the VIBRANT Study (Phase 3 BRVO, N=183), VGFT-OD-0702 (Phase 2 nAMD, long-term N=323) and the VIEW 1 Extension Study (Phase 3b wAMD, N=323). Based on the currently available evidence, it is concluded that the positive benefit-risk ratio of Aflibercept 40 mg/mL is not altered when administered with a PFS with a lower limit of acceptance of 0.045 mL.

Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 14 (Module 3: S.3.1 and P.2.2):
In the section P.2.2 under product development for specific activity and potency, details of 
characterization of drug substance has been included. Potency Measured by a One-Stage 
Coagulation Assay, Coagulation Potency, Study to Set the “Chromogenic–Adjusted (CS-ADJ)” 
Labelled Potency, and Study to Set the “Chromogenic–Adjusted (CS-ADJ)” Labelled Potency.
The studies concludes that results obtained by physicochemical analyses for each clinical and 
conformance DP lot using intrinsic fluorescence, far UV circular dichroism and differential 
scanning calorimetry show all lots to have equivalent conformational structure and thermal 
stability. It is also concluded that results are comparable to those obtained for the licensed 
rFVIII-FS product.
Microflow imaging analyses for study of subvisible particles show that the particle 
concentrations in the 2-10 μm size range present in the clinical, conformance and reference 
standard lot were all comparable in magnitude, with similar vial to vial variability. A significant 
proportion of the particles measured appear to be silicone oil droplets due to contact of the 
lyophilized cake with the stopper. There is no observed increase in particles related to storage 
under shelf-life or accelerated conditions.
With respect to biochemical characterization of the molecule, the results of the thrombin and 
FXa activation studies and FIXa and vWF binding studies indicate functional activity of the 
rFVIII product, with profiles and results that are consistent with the structure of the rFVIII 
molecule. All clinical and conformance DP lots have comparable results to the Product 
Reference Standard and the licensed rFVIII-FS lot.
The comparisons of the Chromogenic assay with the One-Stage Coagulation assay, tested under 
a variety of conditions, indicate that the assays are well aligned regardless of standards used. 
While the initial data (conducted with 3 lots of Kogenate–FS and 4 lots of BAY 81-8973) 
indicated the ratio of the CS to OS results was 1.23, further testing over the years, using a 
variety of standards and assignments, indicates the assay results are closer together with the 
ratio being approximately 1.1.
In the section S.3.1 Biological characterization tests for potency like  One-Stage Coagulation 
Potency (Relative to Chromogenic Potency) is performed, and it concludes that Clinical and 
conformance lots of BAY 81-8973 have expected protein size distribution, backbone sequence, 
mass, disulfide bond linkages and post-translational modifications, including glycan structures, 
sialylation and tyrosine sulfation. Physicochemical properties, including conformation profiles, 
and biological properties including binding, activation and potency, are also as expected relative 
to both product reference standard and rFVIII-FS.

LC-MS Analysis of Thrombin Digests was performed and the results concludes that there is no 
significant difference in results for activity and binding were observed for lot 270LP3G.
Section S.3.1 In the clinical development of BAY 81-8973 a study was conducted to test the 
BAY 81-8973 DP lots by each of two potency assays; the Chromogenic (CS) assay used for 
release of BAY 81-8973 and the One-stage (OS) Coagulation assay being used at that time for 
the release of the predecessor product Kogenate (rFVIII-FS). This assessment was used to set 
the labeled potency for the “Chromogenic – Adjusted (CS-ADJ)” arm of the clinical trial.
The OS Coagulation assay was subsequently used to test each of the DP production lots as 
extended characterization. In addition, a special study was conducted to compare the CS with 
the OS results using the same standard assigned against the WHO International Standard. There 
are 2 sets of results, one using the WHO 7th International Standard and one using the WHO 8th

The comparisons of the CS assay with the OS assay, tested under a variety of conditions, 
indicate that the assays are well aligned regardless of standards used. While the initial data 
indicated that the mean of the ratio of the CS to OS results was 1.23, further testing over the 
years indicates the assay results are closer together with the ratio being approximately 1.1.

Multiple glycosylation sites are present on the BAY 81-8973 structure, predominantly within 
the B-domain of the molecule. It is known (Bovenschen, N. et al) that sialylation of the terminal
galactose residues on the multiple N-glycan structures within the protein are important in the 
half-life of the molecule. Since glycan sialylation can affect the clearance of the molecule in 
the body, this attribute is tested as part of release specifications. Therefore, the ratio of 
sialylation is used as quantitative parameter for the distribution of N-Glycans of BAY 81-8973. 
The specification for the Sialylation ratio has been obtained from correlation analysis of this 
ratio to the sialylation ‘Capping’ values determined during clinical and conformance lot testing. 
The value of 0.8 corresponds to a ‘Capping’ value of approximately 89%.

Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 26 (Module 3: P.1 and P.2.2.):
The development objective was to provide a parenteral formulation of BAY 81-8973 drug 
product (DP) suitable for intravenous injection with optimum long-term storage stability and 
high patient safety. A lyophilized dosage form for injection has been selected as the dosage 
form.
The BAY 81-8973 drug product is designed to have the same formula strengths, 
container/closure, and fill sizes (2.5 mL and 5 mL) as the predecessor product known by the 
names of KOGENATE Bayer, Kogenate FS, Helixate, Helixate FS, Helixate NEXGEN and 
Helixate N2V (rFVIII-FS).
The licensed rFVIII-FS product formulation has shown satisfactory stability with at least 30 
months of shelf-life at 2-8°C and has demonstrated an excellent safety profile for patient use. 
It was therefore decided that the identical platform formulation was used in the clinical trials 
and continuing into the commercial application. The composition of the drug product 
containing all ingredients, quality grade, function and the amount needed for each dosage 
strength is presented in P.1.02.
In the composition of Kovaltry Glacial Acetic Acid is used to adjust pH as required, quantity 
of rFVIII is based on nominal fill volume i.e. 2.5 mL for 250, 500, and 1000 IU potencies; 5 
mL for 2000 and 3000 IU potencies. Quantities of Sucrose, Histidine, Glycine, Sodium 
Chloride, Calcium Chloride Dihydrate, and Polysorbate 80 are based on actual fill amount i.e. 
2.73 g/vial for 250, 500, and 1000 IU potencies; 5.25 g/vial for 2000 and 3000 IU potencies.

Question:
Question 37
Consistency and analysis of batches: 1. The firm has to state why SE-HPLC is not one of the 
parameter for purity and impurities - aggregates. 2. The firm is required to submit APQR for 
last three years (2021, 2022 and 2023) for DS and DP.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 37 (Module 3: S.3.2):
1. The BAY 81-8973 species classified as product-related impurities are dissociated free
FVIII light chains (LC) and aggregates. The company confirms that these are 
quantitatively analyzed by SE-HPLC and are included in the specifications of DS and 
DP. The chromatogram consists of 4 regions.  
Region 1: high molecular weight (HMW) peak representing aggregates in BAY 81-
8973 contains a low level of both FVIII chains.  
Region 2: The main SEC peak contains the heterogeneous glycoforms of the intact BAY 
81-8973 molecule and active rFVIII that has been partially cleaved in the C-terminal 
region of the heavy chain B-domain.  
Region 3: The peak also contains active BAY 81-8973, with the majority of the peak 
identified as the fully B-domain deleted (BDD) material, not a product related impurity.  
Region 4: Non-complexed (free) light chain elutes in the Region 4 peak. 
For DS only Region 1 and 4 have a specification and for the DP all 4 region have 
specifications.
2. As requested APQR for last three years (2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24) for DS and DP
are provided in the response.

Question:
Question 39
Description of procedures to guarantee cold chain: The firm has submitted the stability data. 
Query: The firm has to submit the Description of procedures to guarantee cold chain
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 39 (Module 3: R.5):
BAY 81-8973 lyophilisate Drug Product (DP) is transported via expedited truck and air from 
Bayer Berkeley, CA to international distribution centers within the Asia Pacific region using 
pallet-sized thermally-insulated passive shipping systems (referred to as “shipping systems”) 
that are designed to maintain product integrity and control temperature. They were qualified 
and are continuously temperature monitored to ensure temperature control during transport.
Temperature recording devices are placed at several locations on the pallet/payload to monitor 
and record the product temperature throughout the shipment duration. Upon the shipment’s 
arrival at the distribution center, the temperature data is reviewed to determine product 
acceptance.
Shipping studies, including physical, thermal and live shipment testing, were performed on MPs 
and the shipping systems to establish the suitability of the shipping process. Physical testing 
was performed to ensure the packaging design adequately protects the product from damage 
during shipment. Thermal testing was performed to ensure the passive shipping systems 
maintain product temperature within an acceptable range throughout transport duration.  Based 
on the physical, thermal, and live shipment qualification results the shipping processes, 
shipping systems and product packaging support shipments of BAY 81-8973 lyophilisate to 
international distribution centers within the Asia Pacific region.
Source:  R.5.02-01 Description of Shipping (Transportation) Studies (#022987163; new)

c) The slope ratio method has improved process capability compared to the current method and
generates similar or better mean precision using fewer vials (2 vs 14).

d) The drug product potency shelf-life specifications are based on compendia (Ph. Eur.
(01/2008:1643) for recombinant Factor VIII that prescribes potency shelf-life specifications of 
80% - 125% of the nominal stated potency and therefore, are not subject to re-evaluation.

e) For the slope ratio method, the p-value criteria is determined per the European
Pharmacopeia and hence is appropriate for setting the condition for the valid testing. 
The MAH clarifies that in addition to the use of p-value for the assay validity, additional 
conditions for the assay validity are also used as indicated in Table 4.
The samples and control validity are acceptable when the following criteria are met: 
• Probability Regression < 0.05 
• Probability Intersection ≥ 0.05 
• Probability Non-linearity ≥0.05
Probability non-linearity and probability intersection failure can be reassessed using the 
predetermined control residual error.
Ph. Eur 11.3 Chapter 5.3 Section 3.3.4 (Test of Validity) and Section 3.1.2 (slope Ratio) 
states that the assay results are said to be “statistically valid” if the outcome of the analysis 
of variance is as follows.
i) The variation due to blanks in (hd + 1)-designs is not significant, i.e. the calculated 
probability is not smaller than 0.05. This indicates that the responses of the blanks do not 
significantly differ from the common intercept and the linear relationship is valid down 
to zero dose; A significant variation due to blanks indicates that the hypothesis of 
linearity is not valid near zero dose. If this is likely to be systematic rather than incidental 
for the type of assay, the (hd-design) is more appropriate. Any response to blanks should 
then be disregarded. In our slope ratio method, the hd design is used and zero dose is not 
used.
ii) The variation due to intersection is not significant, i.e. the calculated probability is not 
less than 0.05. This indicates that condition 5B, Section 3.1 is satisfied.
“Condition 5B states that for any unknown preparation in the assay the straight 
line intersects the y-axis (at zero dose) at the same point as the straight line of the 
standard preparation (i.e. the response functions of all preparations in the assay 
must have the same intercept as the response function of the standard).”
iii) In assays including at least 3 doses per preparation, the variation due to non-linearity 
is not significant, i.e. the calculated probability is not less than 0.05. This indicates that 
condition 4B, Section 3.1 is satisfied.
“Condition 4B states that the relationship between the dose and the response can 
be represented by a straight line for each preparation in the assay over the range 
of doses used.”

Question:
Question 2
Section 1.0.4 [In-use Stability Report]
Please provide cycling studies/stress test if applicable under “in-use stability report” to 
support the statement of “Prior to usage, the unopened blister may be stored outside the 
refrigerator below 25 °C for up to 24 hours.” in the proposed SmPC (p19).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 2:
The proposed label statement “Prior to usage, the unopened blister may be stored outside the 
refrigerator below 25 °C for up to 24 hours.” is based on the assessment of the overall time 
out of refrigeration (TOR) assessment described in section P.8.3.11-03. In this dedicated 
study the maximum TOR for Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in PFS was assessed as part of the 
overall process validation. The total TOR for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL drug product 
(DP) in PFS covers the end-to-end manufacturing time consisting of filling, labeling, 
assembly, blistering, sterilization and packaging as well as the time for distribution and 
delivery of the finished goods to the patient. For Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in PFS, the overall 
TOR is defined and controlled, and the maximum TOR includes 24 h reserved for health care 
professionals handling to allow storage of the unopened blister prior to usage at room 
temperature. For this study, currently, 18 months stability data are available and all results are 
within shelf-life specification. The study will be continued until the end of shelf-life. Based
on the currently available data no trend towards out of specification is seen and the data 
suggest that the specification will be met also at the end of the intended shelf life of 24 
months.
Furthermore, as the results of the analytical comparability program demonstrate that the PFS 
manufacturing process (sterilized PFS were used) yields Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL 
drug product that is analytically comparable to the drug product manufactured in vial, the 
generated vial data should provide sufficient confidence that also for PFS storage at 25°C for 
24 h is supported.
The overall data supports the claim that the unopened blister can be stored at room 
temperature for up to 24 hours.
Additionally, the applicant commits to provide the 24 months long-term stability data once 
they are available.
Source:  P.8.3.11-03 Stability Data - Additional Data / Aflibercept solution 114.3
mg/mL in prefilled syringe for intravitreous injection (#022984600; amended)

Question:
Question 1
Submit description of the analytical methodology.
LRAM explained that the question is related to the test methods: Identity A and B, any 
unspecified impurity, total impurities
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (CTD section P.5.2):
The identification tests “Identity A (Ph.Eur.) and Identity B (Ph.Eur.) are introduced as 
additional parameter to specification for Rivaroxaban tablets as required by the Ph.Eur. 
Monograph. These test parameters are already met with the former test “Identity (HPLC)” of 
current applied Bayer specification and test procedure for Rivaroxaban coated tablets. Test 
“Identity A (Ph.Eur)” is confirmed by the UV spectrum of the main peak in the HPLC 
chromatograms of the reference standard and the test item. The test “Identity B (Ph.Eur.)”is 
met by defining both main peak retention time and size in the HPLC chromatograms of the 
reference standard and the test item
According to Ph.Eur monograph, all impurity peaks (by-products and degradants) at or above 
reporting threshold are determined compared to current in-house method where only 
degradant peaks are analyzed. The acceptance criteria of max. 0.2% applies to test “any 
unspecified impurity (Ph.Eur.)” as well as set for current determination of unspecified 
degradation product. The specification for total impurities according to Ph.Eur. is set at max. 
0.3% compared to current specification for sum of degradants of max. 0.5%. 
 
Please find enclosed the Ph. Eur. monograph 3021 <Rivaroxaban tablets> and TRDs T.02.02 
where the methods are described.
Source:  
Ph. Eur. monograph 3021 <Rivaroxaban tablets>

1. Data to support the replacement of the concentration and homogeneity measurements by 
the final mixing time of 40 minutes should be provided. In addition, a maximum mixing time 
should be defined and justified, based on manufacturer’s experience.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.3.4):
There is no actual change in the manufacturing process of Mirena in connection of the 
deletion of mass homogeneity IPC. The mixing process remains unchanged, only the 
homogeneity IPC test is proposed to be removed from the validated mixing process.
Bayer has manufactured Mirena batches for 30 years already and hence the mixing process is 
well established, and therefore proven to produce homogenous levonorgestrel-elastomer 
mixtures. In order to support the IPC deletion the actual mixing time (at least 40 minutes) 
applied on the product over the years was added and specified as an IPC to substitute the 
homogeneity test. Therefore, the proposed IPCs are only adapting to the actual conditions of 
the manufacturing process.
An updated process validation report P.3.5.01_02 in which the mixing time of min. 40 
minutes has been observed and reported is provided to the competent Health Authority for 
review. In this validation study homogenous mixtures were achieved with the mixing time of 
40 minutes.
Bayer Oy has performed mixing time study for Mirena regarding the mixing phase. 3 different 
final mixing times (20, 40 and 60 minutes) were tested. The mixture was homogenous already 
after mixing of 20 minutes. The situation did not alter significantly neither after mixing of 40 
minutes nor after mixing of 60 minutes. The average assay of 10 homogeneity samples was 
near to 50 % in all occasions, also RSD of the samples did not alter significantly.
Results of the mixing time test:

Based on the mixing study and the overall long experience regarding the mixing step, it can 
be justified that mixing time of 40 minutes produces reproducibly and reliably homogenous 
mixtures for Mirena. Therefore, when using only the 40 minutes mixing time no maximum 
mixing time needs to be defined in the manufacturing batch record.

As a further assurance of the continuously homogenous mixtures achieved in the mixing step 
of Mirena data on recent 283 batches (manufactured between 03.01.2024 and 31.01.2025) of 
Mirena is provided. The data refers to average results of 4 IPC samples collected from these 
283 batches, which means that the data in graphs and histograms is based on 1132 blend 
samples in total.
The requirement for the average levonorgestrel concentration is 48 – 52 %, and the RSD of 4 
determinations must be ≤ 2 %. The average results of 283 batches fall between 47.9 and 50.8 
%, with the average of all determinations as 49.4 %. Average of the calculated RSD values is 
0.4 %. maximum observed RSD has been 1.6 %.
The data provided reliably verifies that mixing process of Mirena results into a homogenous 
mixture when mixed for 40 minutes. Therefore, Bayer considers deletion of the homogeneity 
IPC justified.

Question 3
3. The functionality related parameters loading of IUS and detachment force should be added 
to the shelf-life specifications as well and tested during the stability studies to demonstrate 
that functionality remains unchanged during shelf-life.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( 3.2.P.5.1.02.):
According to the opinion of Bayer Oy performance of Loading of IUS and Detachment force 
tests in stability studies in unnecessary.  Bayer of agrees to add these two tests into the Shelf-
life Specification of Mirena but with the addition of footnote “Not tested during stability, 
complies if tested”. An updated new version of the Shelf-life Specification is provided for 
review.
To support this approach Bayer Oy provides new data for the primary stability batches 
TU037VS, TU039L2 and TU03C1T in new version of the stability report P.8.3.01. In the 
updated stability report data on Loading of IUS and Detachment force tests is provided for the 
whole 36 months’ shelf-life of Mirena. The new data supports clearly the unnecessity to test 
these two items in stability studies & during the shelf-life. As mentioned, in the footnote of 
the specification, it will be stated that a batch/sample will fulfil the requirements of these 
tests, if tested.
Bayer Oy has already a lot of experience regarding the Loading of IUS and Detachment force 
tests on Mirena. They have been internally performed on Mirena’s on-going stability batches 
for several years already. The results have continuously fulfilled the requirements. The results 
of detachment force test do not tend to increase or alter during Shelf-life. Based on the 
accumulated data and knowledge with these two functionality tests of Mirena it can be stated 
to be appropriate to perform tests for Loading of IUS and Detachment force only at release for 
Mirena. Routine performance of these tests during Shelf-life is redundant.

Question:
Question 8
8. Purity: The results provided in table 2-4 indicate maximum 0.1% for the individual and the 
total impurities, which do not justify the proposed limit of NMT 1.0%. No formal stability 
data are provided but stability results should be available as section 3.2.P.8.2 indicates that the 
stability study started in 03/2022 with batches manufactured in 2021. Therefore, the applicant 
is asked to provide the available stability data in 3.2.P.8 and to tighten the limits for 
individual impurities in function of the obtained results.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 8 ( 3.2.P.5.6):
Source:  
P.8.3.01-03 Stability Data / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery  
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#IQMS-401680; new)

The test procedure for impurities in Mirena IUS has been revised to include only 
levonorgestrel (LNG) related degradation products, not any more synthesis related impurities 
as the current test. This approach is in line with the EMA guideline CPMP/ICH/2738/99 (ICH 
Q3B). The guideline states: “impurities present in the drug substance need not be monitored 
or specified in the drug product specifications unless they are also degradation products”.
This proposed new impurity test is removed from Release Specifications, i.e. it will be 
included in the shelf life testing only. To support the change, the acceptance limit for the sum 
of the degradation products is tightened from NMT 2.0% to NMT 1.0%. The potential known 
and unidentified LNG degradation products above 0.1% reporting threshold are included in 
the test results.
Levonorgestrel is inherently stable. The long history of Mirena IUS has verified that LNG 
remains virtually unchanged in the product manufacture, and during the shelf-life. This is 
demonstrated by comparing results of five MIRENA IUS drug product stability batches with 
the results for corresponding drug substance batches (P.5.6.01_03). The results for drug 
substance batches in accordance with the Ph. Eur. method indicate actual low amount of 
degradation products for Mirena IUS as the synthesis related impurities need not to be 
included in the results. This is shown to be true for the drug product batches listed, as the 
maximum result for the Sum of degradation products is only 0.1 %.
The daily dose released from a Mirena IUS is ca. 20 μg. According to the EMA guideline 
CPMP/ICH/2738/99 the identification threshold for impurities in a drug product with a 
maximum daily dose of 1 mg is 1.0% or 5 μg Total Daily Intake (TDI), whichever is lower. 
The potential known and unidentified LNG degradation products above 0.1% reporting 
threshold are included in the specifications of Mirena. Calculated as daily intake an impurity 
at 0.1 % level in Mirena provides a daily intake of 0.02 μg only. The level of possible 
unspecified degradation products in Mirena are therefore far below the identification 
threshold of 5 μg TDI. Even the sum of all degradation products calculated as daily intake 
(1.0 % of 20 μg daily dose) is ca. 0.2 μg (TDI) only.
Based on the above arguments the proposed limits for the impurity test are well justified.

Question:
Question 9
9. Release rate: Considering the long-term use of the drug product that releases levonorgestrel 
at a mean rate of 13-20 μg/24h for 8 years, the ranges +/- 10% and 15% at levels 2 and 3 of 
the release rate test seem rather wide and are supported neither by the batch results nor by the 
clinical batches.

As shown in the summary of the results presented for 42 batches in table 2-10, the standard 
deviation is between 1.5 and 2.2 and all batches comply at level 1. The current specifications 
present only one level acceptance criteria for the average (18-26 μg/d) and the individual 
values (17-29 μg/d), and the applicant assumes that the results at day 8 with the new test are 
similar to the results at day 15 with the current test. The proposed limits are wider than the 
current ones and a non-compliant batch to the current specifications at day 15 might comply 
with the level 2 or level 3 of the proposed specifications at day 8. Therefore, to maintain 
similarity between the testing points linked to the clinical performance, i.e. the current day 15 
release rate and the proposed day 8 release rate, the applicant is asked to reduce the range at 
day 8 for level 2 and level 3 to a range representative of the presented results and 
representative of the day 15 results.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 9 (3.2.P.5.1):
Bayer recognizes the release rate acceptance limits proposed for the new method can be 
considered wider than the current method limits for the day 15. Therefore, the day 8 Level 2 
and 3 ranges are revised, as requested, and in addition more scientific data is provided to 
justify the ranges. Bayer sees that the revised specification is justified since the addition of 
sampling points and the level testing procedure increases significantly the overall control of 
the manufactured batches. 
The current and the new methods are statistically compared in the P.5.3.21 and P.5.6.01 to 
proof the day 8 of the new method ensures the intended release rate profile similarly as the 
day 15 in the current method. This justifies that the batch data can be used to set the 
specification and the link to the clinical performance has remained. In addition, it should be 
noted that the new method increases the sampling points, i.e., it brings two new test points, 
and they also have 3-level testing procedure. The discriminatory power studies presented in 
the P.5.3.21 show that some result of a defected IUS are outliers of the day 2 and 5 proposed 
limits but would fulfill the current specification for day 15. This is strong evidence for the 
quality control power of the new 3-point method.  
P.5.3.21 demonstrates the potential of the release method for the long-term release profile 
determination. Three MIRENA batches were tested up to eight years (2920 days) and a 
regression curve can be used to calculate the relationship between in vitro release rate and 
time. The provided graphs demonstrate that over a period of eight years the three batches 
release Levonorgestrel at the same rate, and the residual content of LNG is greater than 25% 
at eight years ensuring a continual decreasing dissolution profile over time. 
At the day 8 range of ±5% is set for Level 2 (16.5 -27.4 µg/day) and range of ±8% is set for 
Level 3 (16.0 -28.2 µg/day). The ranges correspond to the current method day 15 range for 
individuals (17-29 µg/day). The new ranges required a slight shift down from the current 
range based on the batch data. The 3-level testing procedure having the increasing sample size 
(n=6-12-24) and slightly opening limits increases the overall quality control power. The Level 
1 sample size corresponds the current method sample size but the Level 1 range for the 
individuals, 17.3 - 26.1 µg/day, is significantly tighter than the current range for individuals.

Question:
Question 10
10. Detachment force: The batch analysis results indicate that detachment force is in the range 
0.04 – 0.07 N. Therefore, the limit of max. 0.18 N for the average value and the limits for the 
individual values (0.27 N and 0.35 N) seems rather large and should be tightened unless 
otherwise justified.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.P.5.1):
Bayer recognizes that in the provided Batch Analyses document Detachment force results of 
three batches are in the range 0.04 – 0.07 N. Significantly more batch data is provided in the 
revised Justification of Specification document (P.5.6.01-03). In the amended data the results 
are in the range 0.02 – 0.21 N.  In addition, T-body bending tests have been performed using a 
specific laboratory model. The forces of such testing causing T-body to bend from T-shape to
slightly Y-shape have ranged approximately from 0.2 N to 0.4 N and averaging at 0.27 N. 
These results support the proposed limits for the batch average (max. 0.18 N) and individual 
values (0.27 N and 0.35 N). The results have a link to clinical study which verified the correct 
deployment of the IUS in the uterine cavity in vivo. 
Detailed justification for the Detachment force test and the applied limits are provided in the 
revised new version of Justification of Specification.

Source:  P.5.6.01-03 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#IQMS-401664; amended)

resolution of components to be analyzed. Which in turn led to slight offset of the results 
between the two methods, when the same samples were analyzed in parallel (see P.5.6.01 
section 3.1).

In line with EDQM rounding rules (https://faq.edqm.eu/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1376855), 
the result is first rounded to the required number of decimal places before comparing to the 
specification. A result from 96.50% to 97.49% would be rounded to 97%. Therefore the lowest 
unrounded result to comply with the present end of shelf life specification of ≥ 97% would be 
96.50%, the lowest unrounded result to comply with the proposed new limit of ≥ 96.2% would be 
96.150%. 
Because of the previous rounding of the limit to  ≥ 97%, but the new proposed limit of ≥ 96.2% is 
stated to one decimal point, the largest possible difference between the old and the new limit would 
be rather 0.35%. But the shift would still be within the difference measured for the reference 
standard (see P.5.6.01, section 3.1). The same previous rounding of the limit to ≥ 97% also previously 
applied in the European Union and ≥ 96.2% is the currently approved limit (specification document 
P.5.1.02#022974830_01, which is the same as included in this application for Korea). 
(For other countries (for example Australia), which had previously required that the specification is 
stated with a decimal point (≥ 96.5%), the lowest compliant unrounded result was 96.450 and 
therefore the largest possible difference to the now limit is 0.3%.)

Please find below the comparison of results from accelerated stability studies at 25°C/ 60% relative 
humidity for the quality attributes purity by SE-UPLC and potency by cell-based bioassay.

Stress stability studies have also been performed for Eylea 2mg at 45 °C in the past. However, at 
45 °C both purity by SE-HPLC / SE-UPLC and Potency decrease to a notable extent. Note that the 
stress stability condition of 45 °C is explicitly intended to induce major changes in protein integrity 
for the purpose of comparing the degradation behavior between batches under this condition. The 
stress stability condition was therefore only performed as part of comparability exercises (see CTD 
section 3.2.R.2.02). A comparison of results against the shelf-life specification acceptance criteria was 
not in scope of these stress studies. The major changes in protein integrity at the stress condition 
include e.g. an increased formation of higher order oligomers. Thus, the degradation pathway at the 
stress condition is not representative of the degradation pathway of the product at 2-8 °C and at 
25 °C/ 60% relative humidity. 
 
In contrast, the accelerated stability condition still mainly induces the formation of dimers as it is the 
case under real-time stability conditions.

At the accelerated stability condition SE-UPLC main peak and aggregates are beyond the proposed 
real-time (2-8°C) shelf-life specification acceptance criteria (for certain batches after 6 months) while the potency results are still within the acceptance criteria.

In P.5.6.01 (submitted during the initial registration of Eylea 2 mg), reference was made to 
two sets of clinical studies, the pivotal VIEW 1 and VIEW 2 and an early clinical study.

In the pivotal VIEW 1 and VIEW 2 studies, no patients were administered with a higher dose 
or a higher amount of %HMW. The only treatment doses used in these studies were 0.5 mg 
and 2 mg, where 2 mg is the marketed dose and 0.5 mg was a lower dose which was not 
pursued for marketing authorization.
Therefore the only evidence contributed by these studies is that they showed no evidence of a 
dose response in safety outcomes.
This has now been clarified in the P.5.6.01 document.

In addition, reference was made to an early clinical study, where a cohort of patients received 
a dose higher than 2 mg:
As stated in P.5.6.01:  In addition, a cohort of patients that were injected with a dose of 
aflibercept dimer (equivalent to 4-5.4% in a 2 mg dose) exceeding the proposed expiry 
specification of 3.8%, did not reveal any unusual tolerability issues,
Here reference was made to study VGFT-OD-0603, a phase I clinical trial to assess the safety 
and tolerability of repeated doses of intravitreal administration of two Aflibercept 
formulations in subjects with neovascular Age Related Macular Degeneration. Patients 
received 4 mg aflibercept every 4 weeks for 12 weeks, then as needed through week 52.
The safety profile of the N=20 patients who all received 4 mg Aflibercept did not indicate a 
safety concern. No intraocular inflammation (IOI) was reported through week 52.

The following summarises the available supportive data for the proposed Eylea 2mg end of shelf life 
specification limits obtained from both Eylea 2 mg and Eylea 8 mg studies:

Analytical data:
The change is made based on the comprehensive analysis of the SE-HPLC and SE-UPLC data that has 
shown that when analyzing the same reference standard and the stability batches, the SE-UPLC 
method introduced in 2019 is 0.3% more sensitive to the high molecular weight (HMW) / aggregate 
species. Therefore, the corresponding shift of 0.3% is due to the analytical method only and the 
actual amount of HMW in Eylea 2mg is unchanged.

Supporting data:
For Eylea 2mg, the HMW specification limit continues to be supported by toxicology data and clinical 
data from the initial registration of Eylea 2 mg.

Supporting toxicological data:
The limit (%aggregate) for the HMW species (≤ 3.8% as amended for SE-UPLC) continues to be 
supported by toxicology studies with higher doses and higher exposure to HMW species than in 
human patients. To support the initial registration of Eylea 2 mg, reference was made in P.5.6.01 
to the relevant toxicology study VGFT-TX-05011. With this response, this section in P.5.6.01 is 
further clarified.

In a 8-month pivotal IVT study in monkeys (Module 4.2.3.2, VGFT-TX-05011) conducted to support 
the marketing authorization of aflibercept 2 mg, aflibercept doses ranging from 0.5 to 4 mg/eye (in 
50 µL/eye) were administered bilaterally every 4 weeks for 9 doses in total, followed by a 5-month 
treatment free recovery period. Ocular findings were limited to non-adverse mild and transient 
ocular inflammation up to and including the high dose of 4 mg/eye. When normalized for the 
smaller vitreal volume in monkeys compared to humans (approximately 2 vs. 4 mL), the 4 mg/eye 
are expected to produce an initial vitreal concentration which is equivalent to that expected 
following an approximate 8 mg dose administered to a human eye. With an approximate high 
molecular weight species (HMWs) concentration of 1-1.5% the 8 mg dose corresponds to an initial 
HMWs dose of 0.08-0.12 mg/human eye ... This concentration is equivalent to a 
content of 4-6% HMWs ... which is covered by this 8-month pivotal IVT study in monkeys on aflibercept 2 mg.

Eylea 2 mg ongoing post-marketing pharmacovigilance surveillance data and analytical stability data 
continue to support the specification limits.

Supporting post-marketing pharmacovigilance surveillance data:
In addition, post-marketing pharmacovigilance data was evaluated from the time of initial 
submission until the end of 2024.
The safety profile for IOIs with Eylea 2 mg is continuously monitored. No significant change was 
seen in the rate of IOI in the period before and after the introduction of the SE-UPLC method (1.2 
cases per 10 000 injections and 1.0 case per 10 000 injections respectively).
Overall, no new safety concern potentially related to protein aggregate formation in terms of IOIs 
was observed from 2020 and onwards for Eylea 2 mg.

Supplemental toxicology data at a higher dose is now also available from study VGFT-TX-20170 made 
to support the registration of Eylea 8 mg. These toxicology data were generated specifically on 
aflibercept with a higher content of HMW species (6 and 10% HMW).

Supporting toxicological data (Eylea 8mg):
Supplemental toxicology data at a higher dose is now also available from study VGFT-TX-20170.
An additional study, intended to investigate the tolerability of high concentrations of HMWs to 
support the specification of aflibercept 8 mg, covers even higher HMWs – equivalent 
concentrations in humans. In this 3-month IVT toxicology study in monkeys utilizing the high 
concentration aflibercept formulation enriched with approximately 6% and 10% HMWs (Module 
4.2.3.2, VGFT-TX-20170), doses of 5.6 mg/eye (in 40 µL/eye) were administered bilaterally every 4 
weeks for a total of 4 doses... repeated 
IVT administration of 5.6 mg aflibercept per eye containing approximately 6 or 10% HMWs was 
well tolerated, with no adverse ocular inflammation evident... 
In conclusion, HMWs contents of up to 14% are covered by toxicological data and were well 
tolerated.

The positive clinical data from Eylea 8mg could also be considered to support the HMW limit for 
Eylea 2mg: 
While no material of with higher HMW was used during the 8mg clinical trials, the absolute amount 
of aggregate per 8mg injection ... is already higher than the absolute amount of aggregate in the 
2mg injection when the specification limit of 3.8% ... at the 
end of shelf life is considered.

Environmental risk assessment
Answer:
Procedural, physical, and environmental practices are designed to prevent contamination.
Contamination control is achieved by: Area Environment, Heating, Ventilation and Air
Conditioning (HVAC) Design, Personnel, Workflow and Access Control, Gowning, Cleaning
and Sanitization, and Preventive Maintenance, Routine Environmental Monitoring, Inventory
Control, Product Change-Over, Product Labeling, Storage, and Identity Confirmation.

The raw materials used for manufacturing Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Drug Substance are not of
animal or human origin. Some animal or human origin materials were used in the early stage
of cell line development prior to accession cell banking (Table 2–1). However, these raw
materials were manufactured by processes that included treatment minimizing potential risk
of TSE transmission.

During early cell line development, the host cell passaging, transfection, and clone selection
were performed with culture media containing fetal bovine serum (FBS), human plasma
protein solution (HPPS), cholesterol and recombinant human insulin. These raw materials
were assessed for TSE risk and deemed to have minimal TSE risk according to the Note for
Guidance referenced above. In addition, FBS and cholesterol were certified to be free of TSE
transmitting agents via certification standards by the European Directorate for the Quality of
Medicines (EDQM). Prior to establishing the Accession Cell Bank, the cell line was adapted
to protein free media that did not contain animal derived components. No animal or human
derived materials were used in subsequent preparation of the Master Cell Bank and Working
Cell Bank.

Question:
Question 3
General description and history of starting material (Strain,Gene Construct, System of 
seed/Cell Line/master/working banks,Embryonated eggs and other cell substrates).
Answer:
Mammalian cell line baby hamster kidney 21 (BHK-21) acquired from the American Type
Culture Collection (ATCC catalog number CCL-10) was used as the parent cell line, and
tested negative for microbial growth, mycoplasma and non-endogenous virus (adventitious
virus and mouse minute virus) before being used for the cell line development as described in
S.2.3.54 Source, History and Generation of Cell Substrate.

Construction of the expression system (BHK-21 clone W20-19-38 transfected with expression
vector pBET14A-PEG14W) for the production of B-domain deleted recombinant Factor VIII
(BDD-rFVIII) variant K1804C is described in S.2.3.54 Source, History and Generation of
Cell Substrate. Site-directed mutagenesis was performed to make the K1804C mutation by
introducing cysteine in place of lysine at position 1804 in the BDD FVIII. The expression
system or vector does not have a quality certificate. The DNA construct and vectors were
created and verified as described in S.2.3.54.
Post-translational modification of the BDD-rFVIII protein is inherent in BHK-21 mammalian
cell line and not introduced as a genetic mutation. Endotoxin production is not expected from
a mammalian cell line. Endotoxin level is monitored and maintained within acceptable limit
in the upstream and downstream manufacturing process.
Preparation and characterization of the Master Cell Bank (MCB) and Working Cell Bank
(WCB) are described in S.2.3.50 Cell Banking System, Characterization and Testing - Master
Cell Bank and S.2.3.51 Cell Banking System, Characterization and Testing - Working Cell
Bank, respectively. The description includes the culture medium used in growing the cells for
the preparation of the MCB (S.2.3.50) and WCB (S.2.3.51). Culture conditions (process
parameters controlled and performance attributes measured) for the cell expansion step
described in S.2.2.62 Manufacturing Process - Process Controls for fermentation/cell culture,
including the initial or seeding cell density, incubation temperature, pH, culture time or
passage duration and cell viability, were followed in growing the cells prior to the
cryopreservation step.

Analyses performed to characterize and establish quality of the MCB were non-viral tests
(identity, mycoplasma and sterility) and viral tests (in vitro, in vivo and species specific 
nonendogenous
adventitious agents, and retrovirus and other endogenous virus) as described in
S.2.3.50. Analyses performed to characterize and establish quality of the WCB were nonviral
tests (identity, mycoplasma and sterility), while analyses performed for WCB end of
production (EOP) cells characterization were non-viral tests (mycoplasma and sterility) and
viral tests (in vitro, in vivo and species specific non-endogenous adventitious agents, and
retrovirus and other endogenous virus) as described in S.2.3.51.
No animal or human derived materials were used in the medium for the preparation of the
MCB and WCB. These cell banks can be regarded as safe with respect to the risk of
contamination by potential transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (TSE) agents, mitigated
through raw material selection and control, as described in A.2.01 TSE Assessment.

Question:
Question 5
Validation of manufacturing process
Answer:
The process validation information is contained in the documents S.2.5.61 Process Validation 
– Fermentation/Cell Culture, S.2.5.71 Process Validation – Harvest and Isolation and in 
S.2.5.81 Process Validation – Purification.
These documents describe the process validation study design and results, and demonstrate 
the robust control of the manufacturing process.
As described in S.2.5.61 Process Validation – Fermentation/Cell Culture, a full-scale 
conformance campaign was conducted in order to demonstrate that the Damoctocog Alfa 
Pegol cell culture process can be maintained within established process parameter and process 
performance attribute ranges, and can consistently produce product meeting in-process and 
release specifications.  The process steps covered in this validation include cell expansion, 15 
L scale-up bioreactor and 200 L production bioreactor operations.
The validation protocol was designed to cover the maximum process duration (maximum cell 
culture age in cell days) and capacity for production (maximum number of 200 L bioreactors 
in parallel).  Critical process parameters (CPPs) and key process parameters (KPP) were 
controlled within operating ranges, and process performance attributes and critical quality 
attributes (CQA) were monitored to demonstrate the consistency and reproducibility of the 
cell culture process.
All runs were maintained within defined process parameters with the exception of the process 
excursions that were assessed and resolved through the deviation management process and 
found to have no impact on the validated state of the process.  All CPPs and KPPs were
assessed and deemed acceptable.  All acceptance criteria for CQAs were met.  The individual 
and collective impact of all deviations was evaluated and it was determined that there was no 
adverse impact to the overall outcome of the validation.  Together, this data demonstrates the 
consistency and reproducibility of the cell culture process.  Based upon the result of the 
validation, the process is considered to have been successfully validated.
As described in S.2.5.71 Process Validation – Harvest and Isolation, a full-scale conformance 
campaign was conducted in order to demonstrate that the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol harvest and 
isolation processes can be maintained within established operating parameters and 
consistently produce product meeting in-process and release specifications.  The harvest 
process is implemented using a continuous cell separation unit operation and the isolation 
process is implemented using a membrane adsorber unit operation.
The prospective validation was designed to cover the maximum cell culture duration (75 cell 
days) and capacity for production (six 200 L bioreactors operating in parallel).  Two 200 L 
bioreactor batches (originating from two different vial thaws) were run up to 75 cell days 
(days from vial thaw) in order to validate the maximum cell age.  The protocol also called for 
six 200 L bioreactors to be harvested in parallel for a minimum of 7 days to demonstrate that 
the process was in control at maximum capacity.  The harvests from all 200 L bioreactors 
were continuously clarified and then processed by membrane adsorber chromatography to 
MAEF.  Of the 232 MAEF batches generated during the conformance campaign, 226 were 
successfully produced (97%).  Six of the 232 MAEF batches were either partially or fully 
discarded.  Each incident was investigated and determined not to impact the validation.
As described in S.2.5.81 Process Validation – Purification,  a full-scale conformance Drug 
Substance (DS) manufacturing campaign was conducted to demonstrate that the Damoctocog 
Alfa Pegol purification processes can be maintained within established operating parameters 
and consistently produce Drug Substance (DS) meeting in-process and release specifications.  
The purification process starts with the thaw of frozen Membrane Adsorber Eluate 
Formulated (MAEF) and ends with the transfer of the blast frozen DS to storage.
The process validation protocol was designed to evaluate purification of DS manufactured 
from material produced during a maximum 75 day cell culture campaign.  Critical and key 
process parameters were controlled within the defined ranges and process performance 
attributes were monitored to demonstrate the consistency and reproducibility of the 
purification process.  Data generated were used to demonstrate that the commercial 
manufacturing process for the production of Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is consistent, 
reproducible, and produces DS material meeting pre-defined quality attributes for identity, 
quality, safety, purity, potency, strength, and composition. All conformance batches met 
process validation acceptance criteria.  Of the fifteen DS batches manufactured during the 
process validation, four were placed on stability.

Chromatography resin use life and tangential flow filtration (TFF) membrane use life 
validation protocols were executed concurrently with the process validation, during which the 
performance and cleanability of each of the chromatography columns and TFF membranes 
used for DS purification at the commercial scale were evaluated.

All acceptance criteria were met with the exception of the deviations which were assessed and 
were determined not to adversely impact the outcome of the validation.  During validation of 
the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS manufacturing process, CPPs and KPPs were controlled 
within defined process ranges; performance attributes (e.g., step yields) were within defined 
process limits; DS test results met all acceptance criteria demonstrating that the commercial 
purification process results in in-process intermediates and DS meeting in-process and final 
release specifications.  The manufacturing process has demonstrated robustness and 
consistency and has been successfully validated.
Additional information about process parameters and in-process tests is provided in S.2.4.60 
In-Process Control of Critical Steps – Fermentation/Cell Culture, S.2.4.70 In-Process 
Control of Critical Steps – Harvest and Isolation and in S.2.4.80 In-Process Control of 
Critical Steps – Purification.  As described in these documents, the cell culture, isolation and 
purification manufacturing processes do not include reprocessing steps.
Information pertaining to the analytical procedures and method validations have been 
provided in CTD sections S.4.2 and S.4.3.

Question:
Question 7
Biological Characterization data not submitted. Please submit data for biological 
characterization w.r.t. biological activity, binding assay, activation in comparison with 
reference std.
Answer:
The Damoctocog Alfa Pegol conformance run Drug Substance and drug product batches were 
evaluated in an extended characterization program for primary, secondary and tertiary protein 
structure characteristics compared to the Phase 3 clinical material.  The testing included SDS-
PAGE analysis for evaluation of the heterodimer of BDD-rFVIII with PEGylation on the A3 
domain in the heavy chain.  Peptide mapping using LC/MS techniques for protein sequence 
identification, verification of post-translational modification such as tyrosine sulfation, N-
linked and O-link glycosylation, disulfide bonds, and methionine oxidation.  Secondary and 
tertiary structure evaluation were conducted using physical chemical techniques such as UV 
circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, and differential scanning 
calorimetry (DCS).  All of the testing results show that the Drug Substance and drug product 
batches produced in the commercial facility are comparable to the Phase 3 clinical material 
(S.2.5.03).
Characterization of the impurities included host cell proteins (HCP) by SDS PAGE gels and 
westerns, aggregates by SEC-MALS and AFFF-MALS, trace elements (metals) by ICP-MS, 
monosaccharides, API purity by SDS-PAGE gels, tryptic map LC/MS and thrombin map 
LC/MS, and PEGylation site ID by N-terminal sequencing all confirm that the commercial 
material is comparable to the Phase 3 clinical material (S.2.5.03).
Finally, the commercial API in the conformance drug product batches were compared to the 
Phase 3 clinical drug product batches in different functional testing methods.  This included 
binding to vWF, one-stage coagulation potency testing, thrombin activation, FXa activation, 
FIXa binding, and APC inactivation.  All of the functional characterization results show that 
the conformance batches are comparable to the Phase 3 clinical batches (S.2.5.03).

unchnaged)

Question:
Question 9
The firm is required to submit the protocol and report of validation of analytical testing 
parameters related to identity, purity and potency.
Answer:
Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography RP-HPLC
(2.5 µm)
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the purity and the ratio of light chain relative to 
heavy chain in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples.  The purpose of the assay is also to 
determine the identity of DS.  The method is used for testing release and stability DS samples 
from commercial manufacturing.
The assay is a Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) method 
that uses fluorescence detection.  Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is a heterodimer composed of a 
heavy chain (HC) and a PEGylated light chain (LC).  This procedure uses RP-HPLC 
separation on a non-porous polymeric column to separate the principle components of 
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol preparations according to their hydrophobic properties.  Fluorescence 
detection is used and the percent peak area of LC and HC proteins is determined. All other 
protein peaks are integrated as impurities. Damoctocog Alfa Pegol purity, LC/HC ratio and 
identity are reported.
Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography RP-HPLC  
(10 µm)
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the purity and the ratio of light chain relative to 
heavy chain in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Drug Substance (DS) samples. The purpose of the 
assay is also to determine the identity of DS.  The method is used for testing release and 
stability DS samples from clinical and conformance manufacturing.
The assay is a Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) method 
that uses fluorescence detection. Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is a heterodimer composed of a 
heavy chain (HC) and a PEGylated light chain (LC).  This procedure uses RP-HPLC 
separation on a C18 polymeric column to separate the principle components of Damoctocog 
Alfa Pegol preparations according to their hydrophobic properties.  Fluorescence detection is 
used and the percent peak area of LC and HC proteins is determined.  All other protein peaks 
are integrated as impurities.  Damoctocog Alfa Pegol purity, LC/HC ratio and identity are 
reported.

High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (5
μm)
The High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (HPLC SEC 
5 μm) assay is a method for the determination of total protein and molecular size distribution 
in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples.  This assay is used to estimate the relative amounts of 
high molecular weight protein (HMW) and low molecular weight protein (LMW) in 
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples.  This assay is used for testing release and stability 
samples from commercial manufacturing.
The HPLC SEC (5 μm) procedure separates the principle components of Damoctocog Alfa 
Pegol preparations according to their hydrodynamic volume, or molecular size, and is capable 
of resolving proteins over a wide range of molecular weights.  Total protein concentration is 
determined by regression analysis on a linear fit standard curve of the total integrated peak 
area versus protein concentration, calibrated with a Damoctocog Alfa Pegol reference 
standard.  The high molecular weight protein region elutes prior to the product main peak. 
The integrated peak areas with retention times in the high molecular weight proteins window 
are used to calculate and report the relative percent (%) area of high molecular weight product 
related impurities, including aggregates.  The low molecular weight product related impurities 
include a portion of the main peak tail side and a protein peak eluting after the main peak in 
the chromatogram.
High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (10 
μm)
The High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (HPLC SEC 
10 μm) assay is a method for the determination of total protein and molecular size distribution 
in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples.  This assay is used to estimate the relative amounts of 
high molecular weight protein (HMW) and low molecular weight protein (LMW) in 
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples.  This assay is used for testing release and stability 
samples from clinical and conformance manufacturing.
The HPLC SEC (10 μm) method separates the principal components of the Damoctocog Alfa 
Pegol preparations, which includes intact conjugate active ingredient and product related 
impurities such as low molecular weight (LMW) protein species, non-conjugated 
rFVIII-BDD, free light chain, free heavy chain and high molecular weight (HMW) protein 
species including aggregates.  Separation of these components is dependent on the 
hydrodynamic volume or molecular size of the individual species.  Low molecular weight 
impurities are reported as the sum of the relative percent peak areas of all proteins smaller 
than intact Damoctocog Alfa Pegol. The high molecular weight impurities are reported as the 
sum of the relative percent peak areas of all proteins larger than the intact Damoctocog Alfa 
Pegol.  Total protein concentration is determined by regression analysis on a linear fit 
standard curve of the total integrated peak area versus protein concentration, calibrated with a 
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol reference standard.

Tryptic Digest Peptide Map
The Tryptic Digest Peptide Map (peptide map) assay is a procedure by which Damoctocog 
Alfa Pegol DS samples are digested with trypsin and analyzed by Reversed Phase High 
Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) to evaluate the protein for identity.  The 
assay determines identity of DS, distinguishing Damoctocog Alfa Pegol from Bayer’s full 
length recombinant Factor VIII (rFVIII) products, BAY 81-8973 and Antihemophilic Factor 
(recombinant) Formulated with Sucrose (rFVIII-FS).
The peptide map assay enzymatically cleaves Damoctocog Alfa Pegol into a number of 
peptides which can then be separated and characterized in order to confirm the identity of a 
protein.  In this assay, the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is denatured and then digested by the 
protease trypsin.  Separation of the peptides in the digested sample is achieved by RP-HPLC, 
and the eluted peptides are visualized with fluorescence detection.  The resulting 
chromatographic profiles are integrated and the ratios between certain key peptides are 
calculated and reported.  This method compares the internal Damoctocog Alfa Pegol peak 
ratios for peaks 8, 14, and 19 to those from a reference standard analyzed in the same run.  
This information is utilized to confirm the identity of the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol protein, and 
allows for its differentiation from other full-length rFVIII products.
PEG-Maleimide
This qualitative analysis method is used to identify and control the residual amount of a 
process-related impurity, Polyethylene glycol-Maleimide (PEG-Maleimide), in Damoctocog 
Alfa Pegol DS samples.
The assay is a Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography with Charged 
Aerosol Detection (RP-HPLC-CAD) method.  It uses a water/acetonitrile gradient with 
Trifluoroacetic Acid on a reverse phase HPLC column.  Protein is precipitated by addition of 
acetone and the resultant supernatant is dried down and analyzed by reverse phase HPLC.  
The presence of trace PEG-Maleimide is determined by comparing the response (peak area) 
of sample to the lowest response of the 10 ppm PEG-Maleimide Assay Working Standard 
injections.

Potency and Content
The chromogenic potency assay is used to measure the recombinant factor VIII (rFVIII) 
activity in release and stability samples of Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS and MAEF 
intermediate.  The measured values (IU/mL) of the DS are then used, along with the total 
protein concentration (µg/mL), to calculate the specific activity (IU/mg) of the DS.
The chromogenic reaction consists of two consecutive steps where the intensity of color is 
proportional to the Factor VIII activity.  In the first step, Factor X is activated to Factor Xa by 
Factor IXa with its cofactor, Factor VIIIa, in the presence of optimal amounts of calcium ions 
and phospholipids.  Excess amounts of Factor X are present such that the rate of activation of 
Factor X is solely dependent on the amount of Factor VIII.  In the second step, Factor Xa 
hydrolyzes the chromogenic substrate to yield a chromophore and the color intensity is 
determined photometrically at 405 nm.  The validity of the assay is confirmed by parallelism 
of the standard curve with the sample dilutions and sample potency is calculated using a linear 
regression statistical method against the in-house reference standard.  The in-house reference 
standard has an assigned value based on the World Health Organization (WHO) International 
Standard for FVIII concentrates.  Activity is reported in International Units per mL (IU/mL).  
The method is performed using a robotic liquid handling platform.  The robotic system 
performs dilutions, places the materials into a 96-well test plate and performs a series of 
reagent additions and incubations to achieve the chromogenic reaction.  The completed 
reaction is then read by a plate reader and results are uploaded to a validated data analysis 
system that calculates the samples' FVIII potency (IU/mL).

Host Cell Protein
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the levels of baby hamster kidney (BHK) Host 
Cell Protein (HCP) present in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Q Eluate samples, an in-process step 
prior to pegylation, using a Homogeneous Time-Resolved Fluorescence (HTRF) 
immunoassay.
This immunoassay utilizes an affinity purified rabbit polyclonal anti-BHK HCP antibody 
conjugated with europium cryptate (K, the fluorophore donor) and a rabbit polyclonal anti-
BHK HCP antibody conjugated with D2 (the fluorophore acceptor) to generate the HTRF 
signal.  Lon-lived K, the fluorophore donor, is excited at 337 nm and emits at 620 nm with a 
long fluorescence half-life.  D2, the fluorophore acceptor, emits light at 665 nm efficiently, 
but with a very short half-life if no energy is transferred from a donor.  When the two 
fluorophores, donor and acceptor, are in close proximity, as a result of a biomolecular 
interaction, the donor induces a long-lived emission at 665 nm from the acceptor which can 
be clearly distinguished from the donor signal by using time resolved detection.  The 
concentration of the HCP in the sample is interpolated from a HCP standard curve using a 
four-parameter fit and regression analysis.

Host Cell Protein (Specific)
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the levels of baby hamster kidney (BHK) Host 
Cell Protein (HCP) present in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Q Eluate samples, an in-process step 
prior to pegylation, using a Homogeneous Time-Resolved Fluorescence (HTRF) 
immunoassay.
This immunoassay utilizes a Damoctocog Alfa Pegol process-specific affinity purified rabbit 
polyclonal anti-BHK HCP antibody conjugated with europium cryptate (K, the fluorophore 
donor) and a Damoctocog Alfa Pegol process-specific rabbit polyclonal anti-BHK HCP 
antibody conjugated with D2 (D2, the fluorophore acceptor) to generate the HTRF signal.  
Long-lived K, the fluorophore donor, is excited at 337 nm and emits at 620 nm with a long 
fluorescence half-life. D2, the fluorophore acceptor, emits light at 665 nm efficiently, but with 
a very short half-life if no energy is transferred from a donor. When the two fluorophores, 
donor and acceptor, are in close proximity, as a result of a biomolecular interaction, the donor 
induces a long-lived emission at 665 nm from the acceptor which can be clearly distinguished 
from the donor signal by using time resolved detection.  The concentration of the HCP in the 
sample is interpolated from a HCP standard curve using a four-parameter fit and regression 
analysis.

Mouse IgG
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the level of residual C7F7 mouse 
immunoglobulin (mIgG) present in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Q Eluate samples.
Residual mIgG in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol samples is detected using a homogeneous time 
resolved fluorescence (HTRF) immunoassay.  This immunoassay utilizes an affinity purified 
rabbit anti-mouse IgG polyclonal antibody conjugated to XL665 (XL, a modified 
allophycocyanin) as the fluorescence acceptor, and Europium Cryptate (K) as the 
fluorescence donor, to generate the HTRF signal.  Long-lived K, the fluorophore donor, is 
excited at 337 nm and emits at 620 nm with a long fluorescence half-life. XL, the fluorophore 
acceptor, efficiently emits light at 665 nm, but with a very short half-life if no energy is 
transferred from a donor.  When the two fluorophores, donor and acceptor, are in close 
proximity, as a result of a biomolecular interaction, the donor induces a long-lived emission at 
665 nm from the acceptor which can be clearly distinguished from the donor signal by using 
time resolved detection.  The concentration of the mIgG in the sample(s) is interpolated from 
a standard curve using a 2nd degree polynomial fit and regression analysis.

Host Cell DNA
The purpose of this method is to measure the amount of residual host cell DNA from Baby 
Hamster Kidney (BHK) cell lines in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol MAVF samples using  
Real-Time Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR).
The Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction method is based on DNA amplification using 
target-specific oligonucleotide primers.  The levels of amplified DNA are determined using a
dual labeled fluorogenic probe with both reporter (Carboxyfluorescein (FAM)) and quencher 
(Carboxytetramethylrhodamine (TAMRA)) dyes attached.  The PCR primer set defines an 
87-base pair (bp) fragment in the highly conserved region of the rodent Alu B1 repeat 
nucleotide sequence which is specific and not likely to cross-react to non-rodent nucleotide 
sequences.  The DNA in the samples acts as a template for primer extension. Then during 
thermal cycling extension, DNA polymerase cleaves the reporter dye from the probe, which 
results in an increased fluorescence.  A fluorescence detector determines a reporter dye 
fluorescence value (RN) for each sample well during each amplification cycle (Real-Time).  
During PCR amplification, there is an exponential increase of the fluorescence signal above 
its baseline that eventually reaches a plateau due to rate limiting reagents.  It is this threshold 
cycle (CT) number at the point at which the signal is detected above the background in the 
exponential phase that defines the amount of BHK DNA present in MAVF test samples.  
Sample DNA is quantified by measuring CT against a BHK DNA standard curve.

Mouse Minute Virus
The purpose of this procedure is to detect the presence of Mice Minute Virus (MMV) DNA in 
BHK cell culture samples from the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol manufacturing process by 
polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
The PCR assay is an in vitro method of nucleic acid synthesis by which a particular segment 
of DNA can be specifically replicated.  The primers used for PCR detection are located in the 
DNA sequence coding for a structural viral protein (VP-1) that is highly conserved among 
known species of MMV.  PCR amplification of DNA extracted from MMV results in a 
specific fragment which can be detected by agarose gel electrophoresis.  As control for the 
assay, amplification of a plasmid results in a specific fragment of a different size than the 
MMV product.
• 
Silver Stain Analysis
The silver stain analysis is used as an identity test to confirm the identity of incoming bagged 
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS relative to other rFVIII products after receiving from off-site 
storage.
Protein components of Damoctocog Alfa Pegol samples are first separated by polyacrylamide 
gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) based on molecular weight in a precast gradient 
polyacrylamide gel, and then silver stained.  A visual comparison of the sample pattern to the 
reference standard is made.  The results are reported as comparable or not comparable to 
standard.

Answer:
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is a recombinant B-domain deleted (BDD) human coagulation factor 
VIII (FVIII) variant site-specifically conjugated to a large polyethylene glycol (PEG) 
polymer.  It is a coagulation factor bioconjugate to be administered to hemophilia A patients 
with decreased levels of endogenous FVIII.  The administration of Damoctocog Alfa Pegol 
restores the coagulation process, correcting bleeding time and bleeding episodes with reduced 
administration frequency.  In the final Drug Product (DP) form, the bioconjugate is stabilized 
in solution with excipients and lyophilized.  General properties are listed in Table 0–2.
