Question:
Question 1
Tests of particle size, residual solvents, and related impurities in the batch analysis are inconsistent with the information in the CEP and EP, please explain.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
Please find below explanation for each item:
Particle size:
The particle size distribution is determined using a laser diffraction spectroscopic procedure, which is a standard pharmacopeial procedure. Standard requirements applied for hormonal drug substances are set as limits in the specification. With the specification of particle size, a safe content uniformity and dissolution is guaranteed even in low doses.

Compared to the CEP from Newchem S.p.A., the specification includes additionally the evaluation of larger particles via optical microscopy and the specification limits for particle size analysis by laser diffraction is tighter. This is to make sure that the material from external manufacturing has the same particle size distribution as the known Bayer material. The particle size distribution is determined by the validated laser diffraction method also applied for the Bayer material and not by the method described on the CEP. The aim is to maintain the current approved and stricter particle size specification from Bayer material to ensure maintenance in the quality of the drug product.

Residual solvents:
Methylene chloride, methanol, ethyl acetate and acetone are relevant solvents and therefore specified. A standard head-space gas chromatographic procedure is applied. All four residual solvents are specified according to the limits proposed by the ICH Q3C guideline on residual solvents.
Methylene chloride: Class 2 ICH limit not more than 600 ppm
Methanol: Class 2 ICH limit not more than 3000 ppm
Ethyl acetate: Class 3 ICH limit not more than 5000 ppm
Acetone: Class 3 ICH limit not more than 5000 ppm

In the CEP from Newchem, only the Class 2 solvents methylene chloride and methanol are listed with the limits stated in ICH Q3C guideline. The limits presented here also include the class 3 solvents to allow a better control of the process and the residual solvents present in the drug substance. The determination is carried out according to a validated standard inhouse head-space method and not by the method described in the CEP.

Related impurities:
The limits for related substances of cyproterone acetate are determined based on the Ph. Eur. requirements described in the general chapter 5.10 Control of Impurities in substances for pharmaceutical use and in the ICH Q3A guideline for impurity testing. Please find more detailed information in the shared S.4.5.01 section (justification of specification).
The CEP from Newchem S.p.A. refers to the impurity specification according to the Ph.Eur. monograph. Therefore the impurity specification selected is even tighter in most cases. This is to make sure that the material from external manufacturing has the same impurity profile as the known Bayer material.
Source: S.4.5.01 Justification of Specification and Skip Testing / Cyproterone acetate micronized drug substance (#022982414; /unchanged)

Question:
Question 1
In accordance with BPOM Regulation No. 23 Year 2022 regarding Standards 
and/or Requirement on Quality of Drug Product and Drug Material, please review 
the document of specification and analytical method of drug product and drug 
materials (active substances and excipients) used in this product in the form of a 
matrix of comparisons for each parameter so that it is clear:
• Are there any test parameters that are not carried out according to Indonesian
Pharmacopoeia or BPOM regulation No. 23 Year 2022 along with the detailed 
justification.
• Are there differences in the test parameters against Indonesian Pharmacopoeia
or BPOM regulation No. 23 Year 2022 along with the detailed justification
• If the monograph is not available in Indonesia Pharmacopoeia or BPOM
Regulation No. 23 Year 2022, then which monograph is used as a reference, 
along with the detailed justification
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
For the Drug Product, Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L for parenteral use 
(PRIMOVIST) as well as for the employed drug materials (drug substance and 
excipients), Bayer has performed a detailed analysis on the availability and 
suitability of pharmacopeial monographs including the Indonesian Pharmacopeia. 
The following approach was followed:
• In case a monograph is available for a Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L
for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST) component in the Indonesian Pharmacopeia, 
Bayer has prepared a matrix comparison between current implementation 
versus Indonesian Pharmacopoeia including a justification for the implemented 
procedure.
• In case a monograph is not available for a Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25
mol/L for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST) component in the Indonesian 
Pharmacopoeia / BPOM Regulation No. 23 Year 2022, but it is listed in 
established pharmacopoeia in other country (Ph.Eur., USP, JP), Bayer has 
prepared a matrix comparison between current implementation versus 
established pharmacopoeia (e.g., USP, Ph. Eur. and JP) including a justification.
• In case no monograph is available, Bayer provides a statement on the in-house
testing.

1. Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST), 
drug product
Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST) itself is 
not monographed, neither in the Indonesian Pharmacopoeia (FI), nor in the 
European Pharmacopoeia (Ph.Eur.) or the United States Pharmacopoeia (USP). The 
drug product is tested according to an in house specification and testing standard, 
that it submitted to the Health authorities and approved in all respective countries. 
Bayer considers current implementation of specifications and test procedures fully 
appropriate to ensure quality and safety of the drug product. Please refer to 
P.5.1.01-02 and P.5.2.01-02 for specification and test procedure.

2. Sodium gadoxetate (Gd-EOB-DTPA), drug substance
Sodium gadoxetate, drug substance is not monographed, neither in the Indonesian 
Pharmacopoeia (FI), nor in the European Pharmacopoeia (Ph.Eur.) or the United 
States Pharmacopoeia (USP).
Note: Sodium gadoxetate (Gd-EOB-DTPA) is formed in situ while manufacturing 
the PRIMOVIST bulk solution and cannot be isolated, for this reason its quality is 
ensured by strict quality control of the starting materials gadolinium oxide and 
EOB-DTPA and verified by adequate control tests on the finished drug product.
Please refer to S.4.1.01-05 - Specification - Gadolinium oxide drug substance and 
S.4.2.01-05 - Test Procedure - Gadolinium oxide drug substance as well as to 
S.4.1.01-02 – Specification - EOB-DTPA drug substance and S.4.2.01-02 - Test 
Procedure - EOB-DTPA drug substance and P.5.1.01-02 and P.5.2.01-02 sections.

3. Caloxetic acid, trisodium (Ca-EOB-DTPA), excipient
Caloxetic acid, trisodium (Ca-EOB-DTPA), excipient is not monographed, neither 
in the Indonesian Pharmacopoeia (FI), nor in the European Pharmacopoeia 
(Ph.Eur.) or the United States Pharmacopoeia (USP).
Note: Caloxetic acid, trisodium (Ca-EOB-DTPA) is formed in situ during the 
manufacturing of the PRIMOVIST bulk solution and is not isolated for this reason 
its quality is ensured by strict quality control of the starting materials calcium 
chloride and EOB-DTPA and verified by adequate control tests on the finished drug 
product.
Please refer to Sections A.3.4.1.901-01 and A.3.2.3.901-02  besides, S.4.1.01-02 – 
Specification - EOB-DTPA drug substance and S.4.2.01-02 - Test Procedure - 
EOB-DTPA drug substance and P.5.1.01-02 and P.5.2.01-02 sections.

4. Trometamol, excipient
For Trometamol, no monograph is available in the FI, however, Trometamol is 
monographed in the Ph.Eur., USP and JPC (Japanese Pharmaceutical Codex) and 
compliant to all three standards (P.4.1.01-02).
Please refer to the tables included in P.4.4.03-01 Excipients - Additional 
Information for a comparison between the current implementation at Bayer versus 
the established pharmacopoeia Ph.Eur., USP and JPC (also enclosed here for your 
convenience: Table 1 – 1 and Table 1 – 2). Bayer considers current implementation 
of specifications and test procedures fully appropriate to ensure quality and safety 
for this excipient.

5. Sodium hydroxide, excipient
For Sodium hydroxide a monograph is available in the FI, as well as in the Ph.Eur., 
USP and JP.
Please refer to the tables included in P.4.4.03-01 Excipients - Additional 
Information for a comparison between the current implementation at Bayer 
(P.4.1.01-01) versus the Indonesian Pharmacopoeia (also enclosed here for your 
convenience: Table 2 – 1 and Table 2 – 2).
Bayer considers current implementation of specifications and test procedures fully 
appropriate to ensure quality and safety for this excipient.
Bayer would like to point out that the comparison tables provided with this response 
represent the status at time of document compilation. As such, it is considered 
informative and non-binding, and it is not necessarily updated in case of changes.

6. Hydrochloric acid 3.6 % (w/w), excipient
For Hydrochloric acid, no monograph is available in the FI, however, Hydrochloric 
acid 10% is monographed in the Ph.Eur., USP/NF and JPC (Japanese 
Pharmaceutical Codex) and compliant to all three standards (P.4.1.01-01).
Please refer to the tables included in P.4.4.03-01 Excipients - Additional 
Information for a comparison between the current implementation at Bayer versus 
the established pharmacopoeia Ph.Eur., USP and JPC (also enclosed here for your 
convenience: Table 3 – 1 and Table 3 – 2). Bayer considers current implementation 
of specifications and test procedures fully appropriate to ensure quality and safety 
for this excipient.

7. Water for injection, excipient
For Water for injection a monograph is available in the FI, as well as in the Ph.Eur., 
USP and JP.
Please refer to the tables included in P.4.4.03-01 Excipients - Additional 
Information for a comparison between the current implementation at Bayer 
(P.4.1.01-01) versus the Indonesian Pharmacopoeia (also enclosed here for your 
convenience: Table 4 – 1 and Table 4 – 2).
Bayer considers current implementation of specifications and test procedures fully 
appropriate to ensure quality and safety for this excipient.

stated in the monograph, validation of these procedures by the user is not required. When 
implementing a  Ph. Eur. analytical procedure, the user must assess whether and to what extent 
its suitability under the actual conditions of use needs to be demonstrated according to relevant 
monographs, general chapters and quality systems.

bracketing approach. The HPLC method is identical for all dose strengths. As a result, a 
bracketing approach is considered to be scientifically justified. All reportable results from the 
comparison tests are shown in Table 5–2 to Table 5–4 (2.5 mg) and in Table 5–5 to Table 5–7 
(20 mg). All results met the acceptance criteria and demonstrate that adopting the Ph. Eur. 
<3021> has no impact on product quality.

Question:
Question 1
In the manufacturing method of the drug substance, some are found where the amount of the 
solvent, catalyst, and reagent to be used is not shown. Based on the "Guidelines for Items to 
be Used in Application for Marketing Approval of Drugs, etc. in accordance with the revised 
Pharmaceutical Affairs Law" (Notification No. 0210001 of the Evaluation and Licensing 
Division, PFSB dated February 10, 2005), present all the amounts of raw materials, solvents, 
catalysts, and reagents, and describe them in the application form.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.S.2):
Bayer acknowledges the request to include further information in Module 3.2.S.2.2 
manufacturing process descriptions.
The process knowledge obtained during development, which is based on process robustness 
studies, including multivariate (DoE) and OVAT-(one-variable-at-a-time-method) 
experiments, allowed for a sound selection of parameters presented in Module 3.2.S.2.2. 
Further experimental details can be found in Module 3.2.S.2.6. Based on the process 
knowledge and the experimentally established proven acceptable ranges (PARs) or design 
spaces certain non-critical parameters were omitted in the submitted Module 3.2.S.2.2 process 
descriptions.
For the process steps after the final intermediate Gd-GlyMe-DOTA, i.e. steps 4a, 4b, 4c and 
4d where potential impact of each parameter may be increased compared with the earlier 
process steps, it has been demonstrated that non-critical process parameters have no impact on 
quality attributes even if they are varied in a broad range and thus, they can be omitted in the 
manufacturing process description. The respective process parameter understanding studies 
are added to S.2.6.01 including variation of amounts for the following solvents and reagents:
• 
Process step 4a: variation of amounts of acetonitrile and water used as work-up 
solvents (Subchapters of 5.1.5.1: “Input quantity acetonitrile for dilution after 
reaction” and “Input quantity water for dilution after reaction”)
• 
Process step 4a: variation of amount of acetonitrile used for washing isolated Gd-
Glydonip (Subchapter of 5.1.5.1: “Input quantity acetonitrile for washing of Gd-
Glydonip”)
• 
Process step 4b: variation of amount of water and aqueous sodium hydroxide within 
aqueous basic work-up (Subchapters of 5.1.5.2: “Quantity of water added for dilution 
before basic treatment” and “DoE on basic treatment”)
• 
Process step 4b: variation of amount of t-butyl methyl ether used for washing the 
neutralized aqueous phase (Subchapter of 5.1.5.2: “Washing quantities t-butyl methyl 
ether”)
• 
Process step 4b: variation of amounts of ethanol and acetone used for crystallization of 
gadoquatrane crude after defined distillation endpoint is reached (Subchapters of 
5.1.5.2: “Quantity ethanol added to distillation residue” and “Quantity acetone added 
to distillation residue”)
• 
Process step 4b: variation of amount of acetone used for washing isolated 
gadoquatrane crude (Subchapter of 5.1.5.2: “Quantity acetone used for washing”)
• Process step 4c (for the diafiltration-/ultrafiltration process, the introductory passage
of chapter 5.1.5.3 in S.2.6.01 already contained the following information): Being a 
physical separation method of solubilized components as opposed to a chemical 
reaction, the key parameter relevant for quality of step 4c is the number of diafiltration 
cycles, as other parameters (variation of water used for gadoquatrane crude 
dissolution, temperature, membrane surface area) only influence the time one cycle 
takes, not the product quality
• 
Process step 4d: variation of amount of activated charcoal used before final 
crystallization of gadoquatrane drug substance (Subchapter of 5.1.5.4: “Quantity of 
activated charcoal”)
The results of those studies demonstrate that constancy of quality of gadoquatrane is ensured 
within a broad parameter range justifying not to define setpoints for those non-critical process 
parameters.
Although demonstrated that the washing amount of ethanol in the final step 4d has no impact 
on the quality of Gadoquatrane drug substance in a broad range, Bayer agrees to amend the 
manufacturing process description by adding the respective washing amount of ethanol to 
further ensure the constancy of quality. Consequently, a subchapter to 5.1.5.4 in S.2.6.01 
(“Quantity of ethanol used for washing”) is added well.
Considering the number of steps towards the drug substance and additional control of 
intermediates, washing amounts and solvent amounts required for simple dissolution 
procedures or pH adjustments used in earlier synthesis steps have no impact on the quality of 
Gadoquatrane drug substance and therefore are not included in the manufacturing process 
descriptions. Furthermore, several in-process controls (IPCs) are implemented in the early 
steps before the final intermediate (Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate) to monitor the degree of 
conversion and level of impurities fulfilling the requirements of Notification No. 0210001 by 
ensuring the constancy of quality by additional control measures:
Steps 1a+1b: 3 IPCs plus control of Glyptac intermediate based on appropriate release 
specification (S.2.4.03 Glyptac intermediate)
Steps 1c+1d: 3 IPCs plus control of Glyptac intermediate based on appropriate release 
specification (S.2.4.03 Glyptac intermediate)
Steps 2a+2b: 4 IPCs plus control of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude intermediate based on 
appropriate release specification (S.2.4.03 Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude intermediate)
Step 3: 1 IPC plus control of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate based on appropriate release 
specification (S.2.4.03 Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate)
In conclusion, Bayer does not agree that the manufacturing process descriptions should 
provide more detailed information for process parameters which have no impact on the 
quality of Gadoquatrane drug substance but agrees to add washing amounts of ethanol used in 
the last synthesis step. Control of intermediates and in-process controls justify that such 
detailed process descriptions are generally not required for all manufacturing process steps.
The amount of ethanol used for washing the drug substance after final crystallization has been 
included in the manufacturing description (S.2.2.02 Manufacturing Process – Description / 
Gadoquatrane drug substance):
Before change:
After stirring, the mixture is cooled to『20 °C』, solids are isolated by filtration and washed 
with ethanol.
After change:
After stirring, the mixture is cooled to『20 °C』, solids are isolated by filtration and washed 
with 『2-fold w/w』ethanol with respect to gadoquatrane.

In accordance with the instruction, we will adjust the description in the approval application 
form to clarify that either double or five times the weight of ethanol will be added to the 
weight of Gadoquatrane.

and Gd-GlyMe-DOTA and the specifications for the drug substance obtained from both 
routes (S.2.6.01, chapter 5.1.1). Provide information on impurity profiles (e.g., 
chromatograms) including the related substances that were not specified in the control of 
intermediates and specifications of drug substance, and explain that the differences in 
manufacturing procedure do not affect the efficacy and safety.

Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (3.2.S.2, 3.2.S.7):
Bayer confirms that the differences in manufacturing procedure do not affect efficacy and 
safety. The quality of Gadoquatrane drug substance remains consistent, regardless of whether 
it is produced via Cyglyp route or DO3A route. The drug product Gadoquatrane solution 0.4 
mmol Gd/mL for injection is unaffected, maintaining the same quality, efficacy and safety. 
Further details are provided below.
Response to Question Q2-1:
The synthesis of Gadoquatrane drug substance includes two different routes of synthesis 
towards the first intermediate Glyptac. Both synthesis routes (DO3A route and Cyglyp route) 
are compared in detail in section 5.1.1 of S.2.6.01. The comparison includes the organic and 
inorganic impurity profile, as well as solvents and potential mutagenic impurities in the 
intermediates Glyptac and Gd-GlyMe-DOTA and in the final drug substance. Based on this 
data it is shown that the drug substance produced via DO3A route or Cyglyp route is of equal 
quality.
An additional comparison of the non-specified impurities in intermediates and in the drug 
substance is requested and is therefore provided in the following.
Organic impurities in Gadoquatrane drug substance:
In Gadoquatrane drug substance the following impurities are relevant in both routes and are 
specified with individual limits: Gd-GlyMe-DOTA (refer to Question 11), Formyl-Tris-Gd-
GlyMe-DOTA Isomer 1, Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 1 and 2 and Desmethyl-Gadoquatrane 
Isomer 1.
Besides those specified impurities no further impurities are detected in Gadoquatrane drug 
substance batches above reporting threshold (RT 0.03%). This is demonstrated by the batch 
data of Gadoquatrane drug substance in Table 1 (result for any unspecified impurity <0.03%) 
and by the chromatograms provided in Figure 1. Thus, there is no difference which has an 
impact on quality in the impurity profile of Gadoquatrane drug substance produced via either 
DO3A or Cyglyp route.
Further organic impurities which can be formed in the final chemical steps 4a to 4b are 
described in section 5.2 of S.2.6.01. None of the discussed impurities are route-specific. The 
potential impurities can occur in both routes of synthesis and are effectively purged, as 
discussed in detail in the respective section.

Question:
Question 3:
Reply to the following inquiries regarding the control of raw materials.
1. 
Explain the principles of the test method for the following control.
• 
Step 2a Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Iron: 20ppm or less (visual inspection)
• 
Step 2a Sulfuric acid: Chloride: 10ppm or less (visual inspection)
• 
Step 4b Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Chlorine: 0.0004% or less (visual inspection)
and Iron: 0.0001% or less (visual inspection)
2. 
Explain the acceptance criteria and the principle of the test method the following
control.
• 
Step 4b t-butyl methyl ether, Step 4b/4d Denatured ethanol and Step 4b Acetone:
Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (visual and titration)
• 
Step 4d Activated charcoal: Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (visual)
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 3 (3.2.S.2):
Response to Question 3-1.:
The method for all of these tests has been classified as “visual inspection”, as the final 
judgement of colorized or turbid solutions has to be done visually. Please find here the 
descriptions of the principle of the methods for the requested tests.

Step 2a Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Iron: 20 ppm or less (color reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is reacted with ammonium persulphate and 
potassium thiocyanate solution containing butanol. In parallel, the same reaction is carried out 
with a standard iron solution.
The test solution meets the requirement if the intensity of the color produced in the butanol 
layers (due to Fe(SCN)3) is less intense than that produced by standard iron solution (20 
ppm).

Step 2a Sulfuric acid: Chloride: 10 ppm or less (precipitation reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is treated with nitric acid and silver nitrate. In 
parallel, the same reaction is carried out with a standard chloride solution.
The turbidity in the sample solution, produced by precipitated AgCl, is less than in the 
reference solution.

Step 4b Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Chlorine: 0.0004% or less (color reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is treated with potassium iodide and starch solution.
Any blue coloration (due to iodine produced) must disappear when adding max. 0.2 mL 
sodium thiosulfate solution 0.01 M.

Step 4b Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Iron: 0.0001% or less (color reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is treated with citric acid monohydrate and 
thioglycolic acid. In parallel, the same reaction is carried out with a standard iron solution.
After 5 minutes the sample solution is max. as pink as the reference solution. The pink 
coloration is due to the ferric thioglycolate produced.

Accordingly we will modify the approval application form to clarify the principles of these 
testing methods. We will also make similar changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.

Response to Question 3-2.:
Please find the principles of the test methods and the respective acceptance criteria for the 
requested tests below.

Step 4a Acetonitril, Step 4b t-butyl methyl ether, Step 4b/4d Denatured ethanol and Step 
4b Acetone: Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (neutral litmus paper and titration)
The test substance mixed with water is tested with red and blue litmus paper.
The litmus paper shows neutral reaction.
If the litmus test is weakly alkaline or acidic, carry out a titration.
Test for alkaline substances: 50 mL of the test substance is titrated to color change from blue 
to yellow against bromophenol blue indicator.
The volume of hydrochloric acid 0.1 mol/L consumed must not exceed 0.3 mL.
Test for acidic substances: 50 mL of the test substance is titrated to color change from 
colorless to pink against phenolphthalein indicator.
The volume of sodium hydroxide solution 0.1 mol/L consumed must not exceed 0.3 mL.

Step 4d Activated charcoal: Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (neutral litmus paper)
The test substance is heated in water. After cooling to room temperature, the suspension is 
filtered, the filtrate has to be neutral against litmus paper.

Accordingly we will modify the approval application form to clarify the principles of these

For the first commercial scale production campaigns, the dichloromethane work-up in Step 2a 
was carried out for every batch produced as part of the regular process with the aim to ensure 
consistent quality control of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate obtained in Step 3. Batch 
analysis data of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate batches, which were manufactured with 
execution of the dichloromethane workup during Step 2a are shown in S.2.4.05_01 
(Manufacturing date in 2022: 37148971, 37148972, 37148973). Likewise, batch analysis data 
of Gadoquatrane drug substance obtained from Gd-GlyMe-DOTA batches, which were 
manufactured with execution of the dichloromethane workup during Step 2a are shown in 
S.4.4.01 (Manufacturing date in 2022: UN623TE, UN623TG, UN623TI)
With ongoing manufacturing experience and development of the DO3A route of synthesis, it 
was determined that the dichloromethane work-up is not always required to meet the 
specifications of the downstream impurity Bis(Gd-GlyMe-DOTA) (limit max. 0.2% on Gd-
GlyMe-DOTA intermediate). To exert control of this impurity during manufacturing, in-
process-control 2 will need to comply to levels of the respective precursor species (Bis-
carboxylic acids controlled as RRT 0.84) of not more than 0.3% in step 2a (a detailed 
discussion including the structure of the controlled species can be found in S.2.6.01).
Batch analysis data of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate batches, which were manufactured 
with no dichloromethane workup performed during Step 2a are shown in S.2.4.05 
(Manufacturing date in 2024: 37169824, 37169825, 37169826). Likewise, batch analysis data 
of Gadoquatrane drug substance obtained from Gd-GlyMe-DOTA batches, which were 
manufactured with no dichloromethane workup performed during Step 2a are shown in 
S.4.4.01 (Manufacturing date in 2024: UN62XIK, UN62XIM, UN62XK7).
The batches of drug substance produced in 2022 and 2024 showed no difference in impurity 
profile and all batches complied with the current specification. Based on the experience 
gained during routine production on commercial scale, retaining the in-process control-
governed dichloromethane workup in the manufacturing description of Step 2a as reworking 
is justified by the quality-based arguments.

Question:
Question 6
Explain the criteria for decision to perform the following manufacturing process (underlined). 
In addition, consider additionally describe the criteria in the manufacturing description in the 
application form.
• 
Step 2b: washed with acetone and optionally ethanol
• 
Step 3: The mixture is heated to dissolve solids, and the pH is increased to a range of 
2.4 - 2.6 using barium hydroxide octahydrate if required"
• 
Step 4a: At this point, the mixture can be optionally seeded with Gd-Glydonip.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 6 (3.2.S.2):
We will modify the approval application form as follows to clarify each cleaning procedure. 
we will also make similar changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.
Additionally, after the consumption of the drug substance lot using Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude 
intermediate manufactured in the initial commercial production scale campaign, we commit to  
remove the description regarding the cleaning process using only acetone.

Re: Step 2b: Solids are isolated by filtration, washed with acetone and ethanol, or only with 
acetone.
For the first commercial scale production campaigns, Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude was produced 
only using acetone as the washing solvent for the isolated product. As was presented in 
S.2.6.01 in section 5.1.3, washing with either acetone, or acetone followed by ethanol, is not 
strictly indicated by quality considerations, but indeed has a (non-critical, but favorable) 
impact on the levels of free Gadolinium in Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude: While not strictly 
required to meet the quality requirements of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate after process step 
3, the additional ethanol washing favorably lowers the free gadolinium input into the 
downstream synthesis towards gadoquatrane drug substance. Based on these findings, the 
ethanol wash was included in routine manufacturing on commercial scale henceforth.
To conclude, Bayer prefers to keep the option for both washing procedures: Firstly, it was 
demonstrated that the purity requirement of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude is not impacted by the 
mode of the washing operation itself – thus there is no quality-based criterion that decides if 
the additional washing takes place. Additionally, ethanol is used as a raw material in the 
following steps 3, 4b and 4d. Secondly, drug substance batches produced in commercial scale 
with either washing mode are planned to be used for commercial production of drug products.
We will modify the approval application form as follows to clarify each cleaning procedure. 
we will also make similar changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.
Additionally, after the consumption of the drug substance lot using Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude 
intermediate manufactured in the initial commercial production scale campaign, we commit to 
remove the description regarding the cleaning process using only acetone.

(underlined parts: proposed changes)
Before change:
Step 2b: ……Solids are isolated by filtration, washed with acetone and optionally 
ethanol ,…..

After change:
Step 2b: ……Solids are isolated by filtration, washed with acetone and ethanol, or only with 
acetone ,…..

Re: Step 3: The mixture is heated to dissolve solids, and the pH is increased to a range of 2.4 
- 2.6 using barium hydroxide octahydrate if required"
In the Step 3 process, after dissolving Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude intermediate in water, the pH 
is checked. If the pH is below 2.4, it is increased to a range of 2.4 – 2.6 using barium 
hydroxide octahydrate, the criterion being a pH check of the reaction mixture.
To clarify, we agree to amend S.2.2.02 Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate as such (underlined 
parts to be changed):
Before change:
Step 3: ... the pH is increased ... if required.
After change:
Step 3: ... and if the pH is lower than 2.4, it is increased to a range of 2.4 – 2.6 using barium 
hydroxide octahydrate.

Re: Step 4a: At this point, the mixture can be optionally seeded with Gd-Glydonip.
As was presented in S.2.6.01 in section 5.1.5, seeding in Step 4a is not relevant for the quality 
of gadoquatrane drug substance, but has an impact on the yield and content of Gd-Glydonip in 
the isolated product of Step 4a product Gd-Glydonip. This was also demonstrated during a 
commercial scale production campaign, where out of 19 total batches Gd-Glydonip produced, 
2 batches were not seeded during manufacturing but still met in-process control 1. 
Consequently, the quality of the resulting drug substance produced from these Gd-Glydonip 
batches was unaffected. Thus, there is no criterion which steers if a batch is seeded or not, as 
the seeding operation itself is non-critical. Nonetheless, due to the impact on the process 
step’s yield, the preferred production mode includes seeding every batch. Due to the potential 
occurrence of isolated cases in which, strictly for logistical reasons, seeding material cannot 
be supplied in time to support a tightly orchestrated high-volume production campaign, Bayer 
prefers to keep the option as it was demonstrated that the seeding process is not mandatory 
but can be performed optionally depending on the operational situation.
Accordingly we will modify the approval application form as follows, and also make similar 
changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.

Question:
Question 9
Please answer the following questions regarding the identification test, IR.
1. 
The Guideline for Drafting the Japanese Pharmacopoeia states that, in principle, the
reference spectrum method should not be used because it is difficult to set a reference 
spectrum with ATR method. Therefore, please consider deleting the method of comparing 
with a reference spectrum. If Bayer considers that it is possible to set a reference spectrum, 
please provide a justification.
2. 
In the answer to 1 above, when differences are found in comparison with spectrum of
reference standard (not comply) and repeat the comparison between spectrum of the test 
sample and reference standard, please explain a justification with a rationale (Including a 
justification for dissolving the sample and gadoquatrane reference standard in water, 
evaporating to dryness, and using it as a measurement sample).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 9 (3.2.S.4):
1. In test method S.4.2.01, identity testing by IR is described using the attenuated total 
reflection (ATR) method. A figure of the reference spectrum is shown. This reference 
spectrum was generated by measuring the qualified gadoquatrane reference substance after 
structure elucidation has been carried out and is electronically stored in the software. During 
release testing, a visual comparison of the reference spectrum and the sample spectrum is 
performed on an overlay generated in the software. Therefore, the reference spectrum and the 
sample spectrum are recorded on the same equipment in the same laboratory environment. 
Different samples lead to reproducible results during the period of the validity of the reference 
substance which comply to the reference spectrum shown in in S.4.2.01 for illustration 
purposes.
This procedure is covered by Ph. Eur. 2.2.24 “Absorption spectrophotometry, infrared”, 
where it is described that the spectrum of the reference standard may be recorded immediately 
or stored in a spectral library for future consultation. Also, JP general chapter 2.25 “Infrared 
Spectrophotometry” allows both options (3.1 “Identification by the use of a Reference 
Standard” and 3.2 “Identification by the use of a Reference Spectrum”) without limitation to a 
specific sample preparation method. Recent IR-spectrophotometer are capable of generating 
reproducible ATR spectra, so that the shown example reference spectrum in S.4.2.01 will 
remain valid for comparison throughout the lifecycle of the drug substance.

The confirmation of identity by IR testing follows a stepwise approach.
1. The gadoquatrane reference standard is qualified and IR spectrum is measured with
the IR device of the laboratory responsible for release testing. The spectrum is stored 
in the software.
2. IR spectra of the release batches are generated and compared with the spectrum of the
reference standard stored in the software. If both spectra comply to each other, the 
identity is confirmed.
3. If there is any ambiguity in the confirmation of the identity, e.g. because of different
water loadings of release batch and reference standard, both the release batch and the 
reference standard are recrystallized in parallel with the same procedure so that they 
are obtained with the same water content and the same solid state form. When the 
measurement and comparison are repeated subsequently, identity can be confirmed 
unambiguously.
This procedure was chosen to reduce the amount of reference standard to be used. 
Comparison of a release batch spectrum with a reference spectrum from the reference 
standard previously measured and stored in the same laboratory equipment leads to reliable 
results in confirming the identity. Only in cases where there is ambiguity in the comparison, a 
recrystallization procedure and direct comparison with a concomitantly measured reference 
standard is necessary. This is line with the Japanese Pharmacopoeia's infrared absorption 
spectroscopy method which states that if the spectrum differs from the reference spectrum, the 
sample should be treated under specified conditions and then remeasured. Therefore, we think 
it is appropriate to use a reference spectrum for comparison first and only in case of ambiguity 
use direct comparison to the reference standard after recrystallization.

2. Gadoquatrane drug substance can exist in different polymorphic forms (Hydrate I, II, III 
and amorphous phase), with a wide range of water loadings (up to 21.0 %, see S.4.1.01) and is 
classified as very hygroscopic. Depending on the water content, slight differences in the IR 
spectrum might be observed when compared to the reference spectrum of the reference 
standard. By dissolving the substance and the reference standard in water and drying them 
under the same conditions, both sample and reference standard can be obtained with the same 
water content. When the measurement and comparison are repeated subsequently, identity can 
be confirmed unambiguously.
In the following figure the comparison is shown between the reference standard before 
recrystallization (hydrate II, pink line) and after recrystallization (amorphous form, red line).

Question:
Question 10
Regarding the purity test “Appearance of solution color”, please provide a reason why two 
methods (visual test and automatic colorimeter test) are set, and what is a criterion for 
choosing which to use.
Also, please consider describing the criterion for choosing which to use in the specifications 
and test methods in AAF.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.S.4):
The test “Appearance of solution color” as described in S.4.2.01-04 is based on the Ph. Eur. 
general chapter 2.2.2 “Degree of coloration of liquids”, method I. This method applies visual 
comparison between test solution and standard solutions and is equivalent to JP 2.65
“Methods for Color Matching”, Method 1. The test is routinely evaluated visually. To allow 
for further laboratory improvement and automation of testing routines, the use of an automatic 
colorimeter is explicitly permitted. This is only possible with the pre-condition that the 
equipment is adequately qualified and that it has been proven that the equipment will lead to 
the same quality decision as the visual evaluation (refer to general chapter Ph. Eur. 2.2.2 
“Degree of coloration of liquids“, method 3 and JP <G1-4-181> “Instrumental Measurement 
of Coloration of Liquids”).
We confirm, that at present JP 2.65 “Methods for Color Matching”, Method 1 is used for the 
testing of the clarity of solution of gadoquatrane drug substance. It is intended to use 
instrumental measurement in the future after evaluation of the equivalence as it was done in 
the laboratory for testing of gadoquatrane solution (see question 9), but it is not implemented 
yet. We agree that the option for using the automatic colorimeter will be deleted from 
S.4.2.01-04 for the time being.

(underlined parts: proposed changes)
Before change:
Perform the test with gadoquatrane hydrate solution in water (1 in 10) as directed under 
Methods for Color Matching, Method 1 or Instrumental Measurement of Coloration of 
Liquid: the solution is colorless or not more intense in color than matching fluid B6 or BY6 or 
Y6 or GY6.
After change:
Perform the test with gadoquatrane hydrate solution in water (1 in 10) as directed under 
Methods for Color Matching, Method 1: the solution is colorless or not more intense in color 
than matching fluid B6 or BY6 or Y6 or GY6.

Response to Question Q11-1

Gadoquatrane Isomer 1, and Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 2 has been set based on batch data,

of all clinical development batches and representative commercial batches are shown in 
S.4.4.01 (commercial) and S.4.4.01 (development). Fate and purge data of impurities in

toxicologically qualified level of each impurity is listed in S.4.5.01, Table 1-8.

...

since the impurity was not detected in any commercial or development batch above the 
reporting threshold of 0.03%. Therefore, the limit will be reduced from max. 0.10% to 
max. 0.05% in Gadoquatrane drug substance. Gd-GlyMe-DOTA will be removed from the 
list of individually specified impurities and will be controlled by the limit for any unspecified

For the impurities Formyl-Tris-Gd-GlyMe-DOTA amide Isomer 1, Desmethyl-Gadoquatrane 
Isomer 1, Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 1, and Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 2 the respective 
limits are justified based on the fate and purge studies and the batch data summarized in Table 
4. The impurities have been detected in batches at levels above 0.05% and fate and purge data 
have proven that levels above 0.05% can occur in the drug substance.
Moreover, the limits for these impurities are justified by the toxicological qualification. As 
can be seen in S.4.5.01, Table 1-8, the qualification level of each impurity is significantly

Additionally, an “in silico” assessment according to ICH M7 has been performed, confirming

Question:
Question 14
Regarding the symmetry factor in the system suitability of Assay, please provide a 
justification for setting "0.8 - 2.2", because symmetry factor for peaks of actual values in 
analytical validation and assay should be, in principle, set at "0.8 to 1.8" (supplement I to the 
JP 18, page 2812: “Unless otherwise stated, in a test or assay, the symmetry factor (tailing 
factor) of the peak used for quantitation is 0.8 to 1.8.”, based on Control Strategies and 
Change Control Concepts at Each Stage of Chromatography Lifecycle (Change Control in 
Chromatography Lifecycle (G1-5-181)).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 14 (3.2.S.4):
Gadoquatrane drug substance consists of three diastereomers which are separated in the 
HPLC method for assay. The symmetry factor criterion must be fulfilled for all three peaks of 
the diastereomers to accept the respective HPLC sequence. When the SST criterion for 
symmetry factor was established, all HPLC sequences run at standard laboratory equipment 
have been taken into account (30 in total). The results are presented in the table below.
...
Actual values show a tailing of up to 1.9 for 
diastereomer 1 and 2. As all other system suitability criteria were met and the symmetry 
factors are in a similar range as the symmetry factors experienced during the validation 
experiments (see S.4.3.01 and table below), the tailing was deemed acceptable even if it does 
not meet the default criterion of JP and Ph. Eur. of 0.8 to 1.8.
...
The tailing cannot be avoided in total, as the method was designed in a way that also 
diastereomer 3 is detectable. Therefore, the concentration of the sample solution was chosen 
with a slight overloading of the column with regard to diastereomer 1 and 2. Based on the 
validation data and actual data from 30 HPLC sequences run on standard laboratory 
equipment the upper limit was therefore set to 2.2.

Impurities / Gadoquatrane drug substance (unchanged)

technique according to the “4.01 Bacterial Endotoxins Test”.

Describe reasons why setting the two types of tests (LAL kinetic-turbidimetric test and
rCR kinetic-chromogenic method) and a criterion how to decide which to use. In addition, 
consider describing the criterion in the specifications and test methods in AAF.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 15 (3.2.S.4):
1. 
In the test for endotoxin detection using the Limulus amebocyte lysate (LAL), a
cascade reaction is triggered with the naturally occurring factor C, factor B and the pro-
clotting enzyme (see figure). In the turbidimetric test, the naturally occurring coagulation of 
coagulogen is detected as gel or as turbidimetry. In the case of the chromogenic test according 
to USP <85> / Ph. Eur. 2.6.14 / JP 4.01 (harmonized general chapters), a synthetic 
chromogenic substrate is added to LAL, which develops a color after activation of the cascade 
reaction by endotoxins. This color development can be measured in a microtiter plate based 
assay, either as kinetic method (measuring the onset time until a predefined absorbance value 
has been reached) or end-point method (measuring the absorbance value after a predefined 
incubation time).

In S.4.2.01-04 the kinetic-chromogenic method according to USP <86> (equivalent to JP 
<G4-4-180>) using a recombinant cascade reagent (rCR) is described for detection of 
endotoxin content in gadoquatrane drug substance. This test is a microtiter plate based test, 
where the onset time is measured until a predetermined absorbance value is reached at a 
wavelength of 405 nm. In contrast to the test described in USP <85> / Ph. Eur. 2.6.14 / JP 
4.01, the used reagent is not based on naturally occurring LAL, but on a recombinantly 
manufactured mixture containing recombinant Factor C, recombinant Factor B, recombinant 
proclotting enzyme, and a synthetic chromogenic substrate. As this recombinant cascade 
reagent mimics the naturally occurring cascade reaction in LAL, the test can be carried out in 
the same way as a kinetic chromogenic LAL test. Only the reagent used has to be exchanged.
2. 
In S.4.2.01-04 two equivalent, alternative test methods are described to determine the
endotoxin content of the drug substance. ... Therefore, both test 
alternatives have been included in S.4.2.01-04 as two totally equivalent and interchangeable 
options. The decision which method will be used in the testing lab is solely based on the 
availability of the respective reagent. As there is no quality impact on which test method is to 
be used, we consider it justified not to include a criterion in the dossier. ...
We acknowledge that option 2) is different from JP 4.01, as a new alternative reagent is used 
instead of the reagents derived from horseshoe crab described in the chapter. Therefore, the 
test procedure for option 2) will be described in detail in the approval application form as well 
as in S.4-section.

Question:
Question 17
For Gadoquatrane reference standard, please answer the following questions:
1. 
Considering that the standard solution for the Identity (HPLC) on the gadoquatrane
drug substance is that gadoquatrane reference standard dissolved in water. Considering this, 
please describe appropriately how to prepare the standard solution for the identity test (HPLC) 
on gadoquatrane standard substance.
2. 
Please explain whether the purity (78.0%) is appropriate for the intended use of the
reference standard with providing a rationale.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 17 (3.2.S.5, AAF):
1. To clarify the solutions used in the identity test (HPLC) of the reference standard, they are 
described as follows:
Sample solution: New standard substance dissolved in water (gadoquatrane hydrate: approx. 1 
mg/mL)
Standard solution: Current standard substance dissolved in water (gadoquatrane hydrate: 
approx. 1 mg/mL)

2. The purity of the reference standard with the specification limit min. 78.0 % is defined as 
“assay as is” by using the following formula (see S.5.06-01):

assay as is (in percent) = 100.0 – I – E – W – free Gd
I 
= 
sum of all organic impurities (in percent)
E 
= 
ethanol (in percent)
W 
= 
water content (in percent)
free Gd 
= 
free gadolinium (in percent)

To define a lower limit for the assay as is, all specification limits of the test parameter that are 
part of the equation have to be considered:
• Free gadolinium, calculated on the anhydrous and ethanol-free substance: max. 0.01%
• Water: max. 21.0%
• Ethanol, calculated on anhydrous substance: max. 0.5%
• Sum of all organic impurities: max. 0.5%

As these test parameters may sum up to 22.01 %, a lower limit for the assay as is of 100.0 – 
22.0 % = 78.0 % is justified. The upper limit is per logical derivation 100.0 % and is therefore 
not mentioned.
Is has to be pointed out, that besides the specification for assay as is, all other specification 
parameters listed in S.5.6-01 must be fulfilled for qualifying gadoquatrane reference standard. 
This includes tight specifications for impurities complying with ICH Q3A, residual solvents 
complying with ICH Q3C, diastereomeric ratio and other physical quality tests.
When the reference standard is used for the test items assay of gadoquatrane drug substance 
or gadoquatrane solution, the exact content of the standard is considered for calculation 
purposes. This is based on the result of assay as is that was determined during the 
qualification of the reference standard. The exact procedure is described in the respective test 
methods. For gadoquatrane drug substance, in S.4.2.01 the “content of gadoquatrane reference 
standard (in %)” (equivalent to “assay as is” in S.5.06-01) is considered in the formula for the 
calculation of assay. For gadoquatrane solution, in P.5.2.01 the “effective content of reference 
standard” (also equivalent to “assay as is” in S.5.06) is considered for calculation of the 
calibration curve for assay gadoquatrane.
For the reference standard, it is not relevant that the “assay as is” is as high as possible, as the 
exact value is always used for the calculation of assay in release analysis.  It is not possible to 
generate a stable form of the reference standard with a defined and constant water content that 
is significantly lower. Thus, the limit of min. 78.0 % is justified and appropriate for the use as 
a quantitative reference standard.

Question:
Question 18
Both of the upper and lower limits of the filling volume in [Process Control 5] should be 
specified as PAA parameter (note: critical parameter) since the filling process is defined as a 
critical process and the filling volume is defined as a critical process parameter 
(P.2.3.01_022992732_02).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 18 (3.2.P.2, 3.2.P.3):
The filling weight has been identified as critical process parameter during the quality by 
design development process, directly impacting the extractable volume together with the 
density (which was also identified as critical process parameter). An in-process control (IPC) 
strategy has been implemented to define and verify appropriate upper and lower limits for 
filling weight during process validation. A validated automated filling line for both filling and 
closure, along with the established lower and upper limits of the filling weight, are considered 
critical measures to ensure a robust filling process throughout the entire operation and to 
guarantee a sufficient extractable volume. The filling and closure processes, as well as the in-
process control (IPC) of the filling weight, are recognized as high-risk factors, integral 
components of the manufacturing process flow chart.
Although the filling weight is classified as critical, the applicant does not consider the 
individual limits to be high risk for post-approval changes. Extractable volume, the only 
critical quality attribute affected by the filling weight, is included in the drug product 
specification to ensure consistent quality. The relationship between filling weight parameters 
and extractable volume can be predicted by controlling density in the manufacturing process.
The applicant proposes differentiating between upper and lower limits, assigning moderate 
risk to the lower limits (which impact extractable volume) and low risk to the upper limits 
(which have no impact on final product quality). The criticality of process parameters was 
defined taking risk management principles of the ICH Q12 guideline into account.
Therefore, the applicant believes that the categorization of the filling weight limits in [Process 
Control 5] is appropriate.

Question:
Question 19
Regarding the Description, it is explained that the test methods are visual inspection/method 
or calorimetry (CTD 2.3.P, p46). If the test is performed according to methods other than the 
Turbidity Measurement <2.61> and the Methods for Color Matching <2.65>, describe the test 
methods in the approval application form, explaining their contents and validity. If multiple 
test methods are to be set, explain the necessity and differentiation of these methods, and 
consider describing the acceptance criteria in the specifications and test methods.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 19 (3.2.P.5):
The clarity of solution is measured in agreement with Turbidity Measurement <2.61>.
The color of solution is determined in agreement with Method for Color Matching <2.65>, 
method 1.
Instead of the visual method, it is allowed to use a colorimeter. This is only possible with the 
pre-condition that the equipment is adequately qualified and that it has been proven that the 
equipment will lead to the same quality decision as the visual evaluation (refer to general 
chapter Ph. Eur. 2.2.2 “Degree of coloration of liquids“, method 3 and JP <G1-4-181> 
“Instrumental Measurement of Coloration of Liquids”). Both types of evaluation (visual and 
instrumental) are covered by the official compendia and can therefore be used equivalently 
and interchangeably, depending on the availability of suitable equipment. We believe there is 
no need to specify the criteria for the decision in the specification and test method. 
Nevertheless, further details are provided in the following part of the response.
Colorimeters as the LICO 690 work according the principles of JP <G-1-4-181> /Ph.Eur. 
2.2.2 method 3 and allow and allow an objective evaluation of the color of solution. As not all 
laboratories are equipped with such a device, the visual method was set as the default.
The handling of the colorimeter is appropriately described in local operating procedures at the 
testing sites.
The equivalence and appropriateness of the instrumental method following JP G1-4-181 has 
been demonstrated for the employed colorimeter (LICO 690). Please refer to the attached 
validation report “Val Report_LICO 690 PhEur 10.3 chapter 2.2.2 Degree of coloration of 
liquids”.  The colorimeter is appropriately qualified, and its performance is checked regularly 
against preset criteria in the laboratories at the manufacturing site using it.
Thus, Gadoquatrane solution is compared either directly against color reference solutions 
prepared according to the provisions of Ph.Eur. 2.2.2 / JP 2.65 when using the visual method I 
(according to Ph.Eur. 2.2.2) or against the nominal CIE-L*a*b*-values determined for these 
color reference solutions in the validation report for the LICO 690 (refer to section 4.1 of the 
validation report), when using the automatic colorimeter method (which complies with JP G1-
4-181). Both color matching methods are performed based upon color reference solutions of
the same composition and in compliance with compendial requirements Therefore, 
demonstration of product specific equivalence is not required.
Either of the color comparison tests must comply with the specification, if conducted 
appropriately.
To clarify the test procedure, the approval application form and the corresponding CTD 2.3.P 
will be modified as follows:

The product is a solution that is either clear or not more opalescent than reference suspension

GY6.

Question:
Question 21
Regarding the Purity test (2) Free gadolinium, when it cannot be judged visually, it is 
determined by ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometry. Given the limit of detection (0.0005 - 
0.001 mg/mL) (CTD 2.3.P, p57) and acceptance criterion (not more than 0.002 mg/mL) for
visual observations from the validation of analytical procedures, explain the reason and 
justification for setting.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 21 (3.2.P.5):
Test preparations of routine samples (e.g. clinical samples, release test samples, long-term or 
accelerated stability samples) of Gadoquatrane solution 0.4 mmol Gd/mL for injection are 
typically clearly distinguishable by color intensity from the reference limit solution by the 
visual method and do not require evaluation by spectrophotometry. The spectrophotometric 
method, however, provides a means of evaluating test preparations with a level of free 
gadolinium close to the specification limit of not more than 0.002 mg/mL, where it may be 
difficult to judge whether the color intensity is equal or potentially more or less intense in 
color than the reference solution by the visual method only, as free gadolinium concentration 
in the test preparation and reference preparation in such cases can be very close.
In order to clarify that judgment will be made using ultraviolet-visible spectrophotometry 
when it becomes difficult to determine by visual observation, the approval application form 
will be modified. Additionally, the relevant sections in CTD 2.3.P will be changed in the 
same manner.

Question:
Question 22
Regarding the Foreign insoluble matters, The Japanese Pharmacopoeia's General Tests 
<6.06> Method 1 states that injections in plastic containers for aqueous injections should be 
observed at a light intensity of 8000 - 10000 lx, whereas the drug products in syringes are 
observed at a light intensity of 2000 - 3750 lx. Explain the reasons for employing different
test methods from the Japanese Pharmacopoeia and explain whether the test methods 
presented can also be properly evaluated.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 22 (3.2.P.5):
In daily routines at the manufacturing sites, visible particles are observed according to Ph. 
Eur. 2.9.20 “Particulate contamination: visible particles,” where the intensity of illumination 
at the viewing point is maintained between 2000 lux and 3750 lux unless higher values are 
required.
The light transmission of the PFS material is high enough to observe visible particles in the 
drug products. As shown in Fig. 1 and Tab. 1, the light transmission of the glass vials, 10 mL 
polymer syringe bodies, and 20 mL polymer syringe bodies (20 mL not to be launched in 
Japan) showed only minor differences. In all measurements, the maximum light transmission 
exceeded 90%, indicating high transparency of all tested materials within the investigated 
wavelength range (380 nm – 780 nm).
The comparable results between the glass vials and polymer syringes justify the proposed test 
conditions at a light intensity of 2000 - 3750 lx.

Question:
Question 6
Potential residues of class 1 solvent (carbon tetrachloride) in an intermediate or in the final 
substance should be addressed since some originator solvents (e.g. chloroform and 
dichloromethane (methylene chloride)) have been used in the route of synthesis (refer to 
CPMP/QWP/450/03 Rev. 1, Annex I, B: Class 1 Solvents Present as an Impurity).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 6 ( S.2):
Below, a detailed purge factor calculation of carbon tetrachloride, a potential mutagenic 
impurity (PMI) in the starting material phenyl-oxodihydropyridine-carbothioamide of the 
manufacturing process of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance, is described.
For the calculation of purge factors, reactivity, solubility and volatility of the impurities are 
identified as physicochemical parameters that influence the removal of the specific impurity 
in the manufacturing process. Under the given process conditions these parameters are 
assessed to define the purge factors for each individual operation. Basis of the determination 
of purge factors is provided in Table 2, as described by A. Teasdale et al.2

The total purge factor is obtained by multiplication of the purge factors of each operation and 
step. The concentration of the respective impurity before purging (concentration at start) is 
estimated in a conservative way. Purge ratios are calculated by division of the obtained total 
purge factors by the total purge factor required to ensure an acceptable level of the respective 
impurity in BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance, i.e. 1000 ppm = 0.10%, in line 
with ICH guideline S9. A purge ratio of at least 1000 is considered to provide “sufficient 
confidence that the level of the impurity in the drug substance will be below the acceptable 
limit such that no analytical testing is recommended for this impurity.”3

Carbon tetrachloride is a potential impurity in dichloromethane, which is employed as solvent 
in the first part of step B-2 of the synthesis of starting material phenyl-oxodihydropyridine-
carbothioamide. Due to its high volatility (boiling point of 77 °C), carbon tetrachloride would
effectively be purged during the drying procedure of isolated solid products in steps where 
higher-boiling solvents are utilized. Moreover, solvents of low or moderate polarity as utilized 
in steps 1 and B-2 (part 2) would additionally contribute to the purge of carbon tetrachloride 
during the isolation procedures of the solid products of those steps.

Question:
Question 9
Skip testing to ensure capability of the analytical procedures to detect and measure the 
following residual solvents (n-Heptane, tert-Butyl alcohol, 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran, & 
methanol).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 9 ( S.2):
Organic solvents 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran, n-Heptane, and tert-Butyl alcohol are used to 
manufacture Pyridyl-methylammonium ethanesulfonate.
2-Methyltetrahydrofuran, n-Heptane and tert-Butyl alcohol are all below the limit of 
quantification (quantification limit is less than 10 percent of the ICH Q3C limit of 0.5% for n-
Heptane / 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran and 0.35% for tert-Butyl alcohol) in the starting material 
Pyridyl-methylammonium ethanesulfonate.
Tert-Butyl alcohol is also used to manufacture starting material Phenyl-oxodihydropyridine- 
carbothioamideand and is specified according to ICH Q3C class 2 with a limit of 0.35% in 
this starting material.

Thus, carry-over into the drug substance does not need to be considered and therefore skip 
testing of the drug substance is not required.
Methanol is used in step 2a of BAY 2927088 purified intermediate. Methanol is observed in 
BAY 2927088 purified at levels < 0.03% in development and validation campaign batches.
Thus, methanol was never observed above ten percent of the ICH Q3C limit (class 2, limit of 
3000 mg/kg) in batches of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance. The risk of a 
contamination of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance with methanol is 
therefore assessed to be very low, and the quality attribute residual methanol is not included 
in the specification of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance. The analytical 
method employed for residual solvents is selective also for methanol, thus, in case methanol 
would be present in batches it would be detected and therefore no additional skip testing is 
required.

Source:   S.2.3.03_4.0 Justification of Starting Materials / BAY 2927088 hydrate
micronized drug substance (IQMS_417984_4.0; amended)

micronized drug substance (#IQMS_260925_1.0; unchanged)

Question: For tables 4-5 and 4-6 of “P.2.4.07_022986601_01 Migration Studies.pdf”, please clarify how the concentration limit (e.g. from ICH Q3D(R2)) can be converted the same unit as to the tables for comparison.
Answer:
The appendix 2 of ICH Q3D is listing permittable daily exposure (PDE) for elements of classes 1, 2A, 2B and 3 in µg/day (see table A.2.1 of ICH Q3D). The CTD section P.2.4.07-01 expresses the results obtained for elemental impurities in leachable studies as ng/mL (refer to tables 4-5 to 4-6 of the respective document).

To convert the concentration of ng/mL into µg/day, the maximum daily injection volume of Eylea 8mg PFS of 0.14 mL (bilateral treatment with 0.07 mL) must be considered, together with a conversion factor of 1000 between µg and ng.

Resultantly:
Y µg/day =
X ng/mL × 0.14 mL/day
1000
= 0,000140 × X ng/mL

And for conversion in the other direction:
Y ng/mL =
X µg/day × 1000
0.14 mL/day
= 7142.857 × X µg/day

That means that the highest concentration found for an elemental impurity, being Aluminum concentration of 5711 ng/mL at the 12 months time point, converts into 0.80 µg/day.

On the other hand, the lowest PDE for elemental impurities in ICH Q3D Table A.2.1, being Cadmium at 2 µg/day, converts into 14285.71 ng/mL.

This means consequently that all results reported in P.2.4.07-01 are below the limits for elemental impurities given in ICH Q3D.

Source: P.2.4.07-01 Migration Studies / Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in prefilled syringe for intravitreous injection (#022986601; unchanged)

Question:
Question 1 a.
1) Relevant Regulation:
Article 7, Paragraph 2, Item (b). Appendix 3, Part 3, Section 3.2.S.2.3. Raw Material 
Management
2) Review
Comments:
Not submitted (data on the addition of starting material (SM1, SM3) manufacturers)
3) Items to be supplemented:
Submit the rationale for not establishing control specifications for solvents and catalysts used 
in starting material synthesis.
Additional request:
Re-submission for N, N- Dimethylformamide is required with measured data showing <10% 
of AI (actual measured values).
Methanol is Class 2, so loss on drying cannot be used. Please submit data demonstrating 
detection at <10% of AI.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1a.  (S.2.3):
KOEI utilizes N, N-Dimethylformamide and methanol during the manufacturing of the 
starting material 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone (SM2). As part of supplier qualification risk 
assessment, monitoring data of selected batches have been evaluated showing that  
N, N-Dimethylformamide is consistently below 1/10 of the ICH limit (ICH Q3C option 1).
Methanol is controlled by means of the test item loss on drying with an acceptance criterium 
of max. 0.3%. This acceptance criterium is equivalent to the requirement of the ICH limit 
(ICH Q3C option 1) for methanol, especially when considering that N, N-Dimethylformamide 
and methanol are controlled together with water as by means of the test item loss on drying.
Please note that loss on drying included in the specification S.2.3.08 is used for the control of 
the starting material 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone. This control determination of the 4-Amino-
5-methylpyridone is not used for the evaluation on the presence/non-presence of methanol in 
Finerenone micronized drug substance. Since methanol is used in the manufacturing process 
at a later stage (i.e. step 6: manufacturing of Finerenone crude), methanol is controlled by
introduction of a specification limit in the already established specification of Finerenone 
crude by means of headspace gas chromatography using flame ionization detection, see 
S.2.4.03. Summarizing, with regard to the control of methanol it is concluded that the control 
strategy adopts the use of methanol adequately - based on the design of the manufacturing 
process and in compliance with the requirements of the guideline ICH Q3C.
Regarding catalysts: KOEI uses Pd/C during the synthesis of 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone. As 
part of supplier qualification risk assessment, monitoring data of selected batches have been 
evaluated showing that Pd is consistently below 0.3 ppm (mg/kg). Thus, residual amounts of 
Pd in the starting material 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone are far below the control limit of ICH 
guideline Q3D (R2), which is 10 mg/kg for oral drug product formulations.
Data on N, N-Dimethylformamide and Pd are presented in amended document S.2.3.12. The 
three batches presented in S.2.3.12 indicate that the content of N,N-Dimethylformamide is 
consistently below 0.009%. According to ICH guideline Q3C, the control limit of N,N-
Dimethylformamide is 880 ppm or 0.088%. Thus, the 10% threshold of the ICH guideline 
equals 88 ppm or 0.009%. Therefore, the residual solvent N,N-Dimethylformamide is 
considered not to represent a risk with regard to carry over (from the starting material 4-
Amino-5-methylpyridone from the supplier KOEI into the manufacturing process of 
Finerenone). In the terminology of the guideline ICH Q3C, these solvents are not likely to be 
present.
Please note that according to section 3.5 of the ICH Q3C guideline, pharmaceutical 
manufacturers have to provide information as following: “If solvents of Class 2 or Class 3 are 
present at greater than their Option 1 limits or 0.5%, respectively, they should be identified 
and quantified.” Thus, since N, N-Dimethylformamide is not likely to be present, it is neither 
required by the guideline to introduce a control limit for N, N-Dimethylformamide nor to 
provide quantitative data for the residual solvent N, N-Dimethylformamide below the 
reporting threshold of 10 % of the control limit.
