Question:
Question 6
Explain the criteria for decision to perform the following manufacturing process (underlined). 
In addition, consider additionally describe the criteria in the manufacturing description in the 
application form.
• 
Step 2b: washed with acetone and optionally ethanol
• 
Step 3: The mixture is heated to dissolve solids, and the pH is increased to a range of 
2.4 - 2.6 using barium hydroxide octahydrate if required"
• 
Step 4a: At this point, the mixture can be optionally seeded with Gd-Glydonip.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 6 (3.2.S.2):
We will modify the approval application form as follows to clarify each cleaning procedure. 
we will also make similar changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.
Additionally, after the consumption of the drug substance lot using Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude 
intermediate manufactured in the initial commercial production scale campaign, we commit to  
remove the description regarding the cleaning process using only acetone.
Re: Step 2b: Solids are isolated by filtration, washed with acetone and ethanol, or only with 
acetone.
For the first commercial scale production campaigns, Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude was produced 
only using acetone as the washing solvent for the isolated product. As was presented in 
S.2.6.01 in section 5.1.3, washing with either acetone, or acetone followed by ethanol, is not 
strictly indicated by quality considerations, but indeed has a (non-critical, but favorable) 
impact on the levels of free Gadolinium in Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude: While not strictly 
required to meet the quality requirements of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate after process step 
3, the additional ethanol washing favorably lowers the free gadolinium input into the 
downstream synthesis towards gadoquatrane drug substance. Based on these findings, the 
ethanol wash was included in routine manufacturing on commercial scale henceforth.
To conclude, Bayer prefers to keep the option for both washing procedures: Firstly, it was 
demonstrated that the purity requirement of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude is not impacted by the 
mode of the washing operation itself – thus there is no quality-based criterion that decides if 
the additional washing takes place. Additionally, ethanol is used as a raw material in the 
following steps 3, 4b and 4d. Secondly, drug substance batches produced in commercial scale 
with either washing mode are planned to be used for commercial production of drug products.
(underlined parts: proposed changes)
Before change:
Step 2b: ……Solids are isolated by filtration, washed with acetone and optionally 
ethanol ,…..
After change:
Step 2b: ……Solids are isolated by filtration, washed with acetone and ethanol, or only with 
acetone ,…..
Re: Step 3: The mixture is heated to dissolve solids, and the pH is increased to a range of 2.4 
- 2.6 using barium hydroxide octahydrate if required"
In the Step 3 process, after dissolving Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude intermediate in water, the pH 
is checked. If the pH is below 2.4, it is increased to a range of 2.4 – 2.6 using barium 
hydroxide octahydrate, the criterion being a pH check of the reaction mixture.
To clarify, we agree to amend S.2.2.02 Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate as such:
Before change:
Step 3: ... the pH is increased to a range of 2.4 – 2.6 using barium hydroxide octahydrate if required.
After change:
Step 3: ... and if the pH is lower than 2.4, it is increased to a range of 2.4 – 2.6 using barium hydroxide octahydrate.
Re: Step 4a: At this point, the mixture can be optionally seeded with Gd-Glydonip.
As was presented in S.2.6.01 in section 5.1.5, seeding in Step 4a is not relevant for the quality 
of gadoquatrane drug substance, but has an impact on the yield and content of Gd-Glydonip in 
the isolated product of Step 4a product Gd-Glydonip. This was also demonstrated during a 
commercial scale production campaign, where out of 19 total batches Gd-Glydonip produced, 
2 batches were not seeded during manufacturing but still met in-process control 1. 
Consequently, the quality of the resulting drug substance produced from these Gd-Glydonip 
batches was unaffected. Thus, there is no criterion which steers if a batch is seeded or not, as 
the seeding operation itself is non-critical. Nonetheless, due to the impact on the process 
step’s yield, the preferred production mode includes seeding every batch. Due to the potential 
occurrence of isolated cases in which, strictly for logistical reasons, seeding material cannot 
be supplied in time to support a tightly orchestrated high-volume production campaign, Bayer 
prefers to keep the option as it was demonstrated that the seeding process is not mandatory 
but can be performed optionally depending on the operational situation.
Accordingly we will modify the approval application form as follows:
Before change:
Step 4a:……At this point, the mixture can be optionally seeded with Gd-Glydonip,…..
After change:
Batch size 1: ... the mixture is typically seeded with 『4.4 kg』Gd-Glydonip which complies with <In-process control 1>
Batch size 2: ... the mixture is typically seeded with 『5.2 kg』Gd-Glydonip which complies with <In-process control 1>

Question:
Question 9
Please answer the following questions regarding the identification test, IR.
1. 
The Guideline for Drafting the Japanese Pharmacopoeia states that, in principle, the
reference spectrum method should not be used because it is difficult to set a reference 
spectrum with ATR method. Therefore, please consider deleting the method of comparing 
with a reference spectrum. If Bayer considers that it is possible to set a reference spectrum, 
please provide a justification.
2. 
In the answer to 1 above, when differences are found in comparison with spectrum of
reference standard (not comply) and repeat the comparison between spectrum of the test 
sample and reference standard, please explain a justification with a rationale (Including a 
justification for dissolving the sample and gadoquatrane reference standard in water, 
evaporating to dryness, and using it as a measurement sample).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 9 (3.2.S.4):
1. In test method S.4.2.01, identity testing by IR is described using the attenuated total 
reflection (ATR) method. A figure of the reference spectrum is shown. This reference 
spectrum was generated by measuring the qualified gadoquatrane reference substance after 
structure elucidation has been carried out and is electronically stored in the software. During 
release testing, a visual comparison of the reference spectrum and the sample spectrum is 
performed on an overlay generated in the software. Therefore, the reference spectrum and the 
sample spectrum are recorded on the same equipment in the same laboratory environment.
Different samples lead to reproducible results during the period of the validity of the reference 
substance which comply to the reference spectrum shown in in S.4.2.01 for illustration 
purposes.
This procedure is covered by Ph. Eur. 2.2.24 “Absorption spectrophotometry, infrared”, 
where it is described that the spectrum of the reference standard may be recorded immediately 
or stored in a spectral library for future consultation. Also, JP general chapter 2.25 “Infrared 
Spectrophotometry” allows both options (3.1 “Identification by the use of a Reference 
Standard” and 3.2 “Identification by the use of a Reference Spectrum”) without limitation to a 
specific sample preparation method. Recent IR-spectrophotometer are capable of generating 
reproducible ATR spectra, so that the shown example reference spectrum in S.4.2.01 will 
remain valid for comparison throughout the lifecycle of the drug substance.
The confirmation of identity by IR testing follows a stepwise approach.
1. The gadoquatrane reference standard is qualified and IR spectrum is measured with
the IR device of the laboratory responsible for release testing. The spectrum is stored 
in the software.
2. IR spectra of the release batches are generated and compared with the spectrum of the
reference standard stored in the software. If both spectra comply to each other, the 
identity is confirmed.
3. If there is any ambiguity in the confirmation of the identity, e.g. because of different
water loadings of release batch and reference standard, both the release batch and the 
reference standard are recrystallized in parallel with the same procedure so that they 
are obtained with the same water content and the same solid state form. When the 
measurement and comparison are repeated subsequently, identity can be confirmed 
unambiguously.
This procedure was chosen to reduce the amount of reference standard to be used. 
Comparison of a release batch spectrum with a reference spectrum from the reference 
standard previously measured and stored in the same laboratory equipment leads to reliable 
results in confirming the identity. Only in cases where there is ambiguity in the comparison, a 
recrystallization procedure and direct comparison with a concomitantly measured reference 
standard is necessary. This is line with the Japanese Pharmacopoeia's infrared absorption 
spectroscopy method which states that if the spectrum differs from the reference spectrum, the 
sample should be treated under specified conditions and then remeasured. Therefore, we think 
it is appropriate to use a reference spectrum for comparison first and only in case of ambiguity 
use direct comparison to the reference standard after recrystallization.
2. Gadoquatrane drug substance can exist in different polymorphic forms (Hydrate I, II, III 
and amorphous phase), with a wide range of water loadings (up to 21.0 %, see S.4.1.01) and is 
classified as very hygroscopic. Depending on the water content, slight differences in the IR 
spectrum might be observed when compared to the reference spectrum of the reference 
standard. By dissolving the substance and the reference standard in water and drying them 
under the same conditions, both sample and reference standard can be obtained with the same 
water content. When the measurement and comparison are repeated subsequently, identity can 
be confirmed unambiguously.
Source:

S.4.2.01_IQMS-259360_6.0 Test Procedure/ Gadoquatrane drug substance (amended)

Question:
Question 10
Regarding the purity test “Appearance of solution color”, please provide a reason why two 
methods (visual test and automatic colorimeter test) are set, and what is a criterion for 
choosing which to use.
Also, please consider describing the criterion for choosing which to use in the specifications 
and test methods in AAF.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.S.4):
The test “Appearance of solution color” as described in S.4.2.01-04 is based on the Ph. Eur. 
general chapter 2.2.2 “Degree of coloration of liquids”, method I. This method applies visual 
comparison between test solution and standard solutions and is equivalent to JP 2.65 
“Methods for Color Matching”, Method 1. The test is routinely evaluated visually. To allow 
for further laboratory improvement and automation of testing routines, the use of an automatic 
colorimeter is explicitly permitted. This is only possible with the pre-condition that the
equipment is adequately qualified and that it has been proven that the equipment will lead to 
the same quality decision as the visual evaluation (refer to general chapter Ph. Eur. 2.2.2 
“Degree of coloration of liquids“, method 3 and JP <G1-4-181> “Instrumental Measurement 
of Coloration of Liquids”).
We confirm, that at present JP 2.65 “Methods for Color Matching”, Method 1 is used for the 
testing of the clarity of solution of gadoquatrane drug substance. It is intended to use 
instrumental measurement in the future after evaluation of the equivalence as it was done in 
the laboratory for testing of gadoquatrane solution (see question 9), but it is not implemented 
yet. We agree that the option for using the automatic colorimeter will be deleted from 
S.4.2.01-04 for the time being.
(underlined parts: proposed changes)
Before change:
Perform the test ... as directed under Methods for Color Matching, Method 1 or Instrumental Measurement of Coloration of 
Liquid...
After change:
Perform the test ... as directed under Methods for Color Matching, Method 1...

Question:
Question 11
Please respond to the following inquiries regarding the purity test “impurities”.
1. Consider changing the specifications to more strict values (max 0.05%) for Gd-GlyMe-
DOTA, Formyl-Tris-Gd-GlyMe-DOTA amide Isomer 1, Desmethyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 1, 
Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 1, and Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 2, based on the actual 
values of batch analyses and stability studies, as well as the ICH Q3A - attachment 3.
If it cannot be changed, explain the reason.
2. Coefficient of variation (CV) is set as “must not exceed 15%” in the system repeatability. 
Please set a stricter value based on the actual data (S.4.3.01_022992803_01, p52).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 11 (3.2.S.4):
Response to Question Q11-1
The specification for the individually specified impurities Gd-GlyMe-DOTA, Formyl-Tris-
Gd-GlyMe-DOTA amide Isomer 1, Desmethyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 1, Methyl-
Gadoquatrane Isomer 1, and Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 2 has been set based on batch data, 
fate and purge data, and based on the structure and the toxicological qualification. Batch data 
of all clinical development batches and representative commercial batches are shown in 
S.4.4.01 (commercial) and S.4.4.01 (development). Fate and purge data of impurities in 
Gadoquatrane drug substance are described in detail in Section 5.2.1 in S.2.6.01. The 
toxicologically qualified level of each impurity is listed in S.4.5.01, Table 1-8.
[Table 3 presented in response]
The only impurity for which the specification limit can be set to a stricter value is Gd-
GlyMe-DOTA, since a very high purge is given in the final purification steps (4c, 4d) and 
since the impurity was not detected in any commercial or development batch above the 
reporting threshold of 0.03%. Therefore, the limit will be reduced from max. 0.10% to 
max. 0.05% in Gadoquatrane drug substance. Gd-GlyMe-DOTA will be removed from the 
list of individually specified impurities and will be controlled by the limit for any unspecified 
impurities of max. 0.05% in Gadoquatrane drug substance.
For the impurities Formyl-Tris-Gd-GlyMe-DOTA amide Isomer 1, Desmethyl-Gadoquatrane 
Isomer 1, Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 1, and Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 2 the respective 
limits are justified based on the fate and purge studies and the batch data summarized in Table 
4. The impurities have been detected in batches at levels above 0.05% and fate and purge data 
have proven that levels above 0.05% can occur in the drug substance.
Moreover, the limits for these impurities are justified by the toxicological qualification. As 
can be seen in S.4.5.01, Table 1-8, the qualification level of each impurity is significantly 
higher than the specification limits and ensures that each impurity is controlled at a safe limit. 
Additionally, an “in silico” assessment according to ICH M7 has been performed, confirming 
that these structurally similar impurities related to Gadoquatrane are also non-mutagenic 
(Class 4). Finally, it is important to note that Gadoquatrane is a contrast agent, which is not 
intended for daily treatment. The qualification threshold of impurities in the drug substance 
has been set to max 0.05% according to ICH Q3A for drug substances, exceeding a daily dose 
of 2g. In case of Gadoquatrane, a daily dose of > 2g is applicable for patients weighing above 
75 kg. Therefore, the applied qualification threshold of 0.05% should be considered as worst-
case scenario.
Response to Question Q11-2
In the HPLC test for impurities described in S.4.2.01, the SST criterion “coefficient of 
variation” (CV) is defined with max. 15 %, measured on 6 replicate injections of reference 
solution R1. ... Therefore, it is proposed to 
tighten the limit from max. 15 % to max. 10 % in S.4.2.01.
This is also supported by the CV data from 33 HPLC sequences run in routine analyses.

Question:
Question 14
Regarding the symmetry factor in the system suitability of Assay, please provide a 
justification for setting "0.8 - 2.2", because symmetry factor for peaks of actual values in 
analytical validation and assay should be, in principle, set at "0.8 to 1.8" (supplement I to the 
JP 18, page 2812: “Unless otherwise stated, in a test or assay, the symmetry factor (tailing 
factor) of the peak used for quantitation is 0.8 to 1.8.”, based on Control Strategies and 
Change Control Concepts at Each Stage of Chromatography Lifecycle (Change Control in 
Chromatography Lifecycle (G1-5-181)).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 14 (3.2.S.4):
Gadoquatrane drug substance consists of three diastereomers which are separated in the 
HPLC method for assay. The symmetry factor criterion must be fulfilled for all three peaks of 
the diastereomers to accept the respective HPLC sequence. When the SST criterion for 
symmetry factor was established, all HPLC sequences run at standard laboratory equipment 
have been taken into account (30 in total). The results are presented in the table below.
[Routine and validation symmetry factor data provided]
The data show that the peaks of diastereomer 1 and 2 exhibit a clear tailing and the peak of 
diastereomer 3 shows a slight tailing. Actual values show a tailing of up to 1.9 for 
diastereomer 1 and 2. As all other system suitability criteria were met and the symmetry 
factors are in a similar range as the symmetry factors experienced during the validation 
experiments (see S.4.3.01 and table below), the tailing was deemed acceptable even if it does 
not meet the default criterion of JP and Ph. Eur. of 0.8 to 1.8.
The tailing cannot be avoided in total, as the method was designed in a way that also 
diastereomer 3 is detectable. Therefore, the concentration of the sample solution was chosen
with a slight overloading of the column with regard to diastereomer 1 and 2. Based on the 
validation data and actual data from 30 HPLC sequences run on standard laboratory 
equipment the upper limit was therefore set to 2.2.
Source:  S.4.3.01_022992303_01 (IQMS-263919) Validation of Test for Assay and Impurities / Gadoquatrane drug substance (unchanged)

Question:
Question 15
Please answer the following questions regarding bacterial endotoxin.
1. 
Regarding the chromogenic technique according to the “Bacterial Endotoxins Test and
Alternative Methods using Recombinant Protein-reagents for Endotoxin Assay <G4-4-180>”, 
please explain the detailed test methods, highlighting the differences from the chromogenic 
technique according to the “4.01 Bacterial Endotoxins Test”.
2. 
Describe reasons why setting the two types of tests (LAL kinetic-turbidimetric test and
rCR kinetic-chromogenic method) and a criterion how to decide which to use. In addition, 
consider describing the criterion in the specifications and test methods in AAF.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 15 (3.2.S.4):
1.
In the test for endotoxin detection using the Limulus amebocyte lysate (LAL), a
cascade reaction is triggered with the naturally occurring factor C, factor B and the pro-
clotting enzyme. ... In the case of the chromogenic test according 
to USP <85> / Ph. Eur. 2.6.14 / JP 4.01, a synthetic 
chromogenic substrate is added to LAL, which develops a color after activation of the cascade 
reaction by endotoxins.
In S.4.2.01-04 the kinetic-chromogenic method according to USP <86> (equivalent to JP 
<G4-4-180>) using a recombinant cascade reagent (rCR) is described ... In contrast to ... JP 
4.01, the used reagent is not based on naturally occurring LAL, but on a recombinantly 
manufactured mixture containing recombinant Factor C, recombinant Factor B, recombinant 
proclotting enzyme, and a synthetic chromogenic substrate. ... Only the reagent used has to be exchanged.
2.
In S.4.2.01-04 two equivalent, alternative test methods are described to determine the
endotoxin content of the drug substance. ... The rCR kinetic-chromogenic test method ... was
fully validated and was shown to give equivalent results to the LAL kinetic-turbidimetric method (see S.4.3.07).
... both test alternatives have been included ... as two totally equivalent and interchangeable
options. The decision which method will be used in the testing lab is solely based on the
availability of the respective reagent. ... we consider it justified not to include a criterion in the dossier.
... option 2) will be described in detail in the approval application form as well as in S.4-section.
Proposed AAF/spec update text and analytical procedure details (wavelength 405 nm; reagent rCR; example supplier).

Question:
Question 17
For Gadoquatrane reference standard, please answer the following questions:

drug substance is that gadoquatrane reference standard dissolved in water. Considering this, 
please describe appropriately how to prepare the standard solution for the identity test (HPLC) 
on gadoquatrane standard substance.
2. 
Please explain whether the purity (78.0%) is appropriate for the intended use of the
reference standard with providing a rationale.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 17 (3.2.S.5, AAF):
1. To clarify the solutions used in the identity test (HPLC) of the reference standard, they are 
described as follows:
Sample solution: New standard substance dissolved in water (gadoquatrane hydrate: approx. 1 
mg/mL)
Standard solution: Current standard substance dissolved in water (gadoquatrane hydrate: 
approx. 1 mg/mL)
2. The purity of the reference standard with the specification limit min. 78.0 % is defined as 
“assay as is” by using the following formula (see S.5.06-01):
assay as is (in percent) = 100.0 – I – E – W – free Gd
I = sum of all organic impurities (in percent)
E = ethanol (in percent)
W = water content (in percent)
free Gd = free gadolinium (in percent)
To define a lower limit for the assay as is, all specification limits of the test parameter that are 
part of the equation have to be considered:
• Free gadolinium ... max. 0.01%
• Water: max. 21.0%
• Ethanol ... max. 0.5%
• Sum of all organic impurities: max. 0.5%
As these test parameters may sum up to 22.01 %, a lower limit ... of 78.0 % is justified.
... When the reference standard is used for the test items assay of gadoquatrane drug substance 
or gadoquatrane solution, the exact content of the standard is considered for calculation 
purposes ... described in ... S.4.2.01 ... and ... P.5.2.01.
... Thus, the limit of min. 78.0 % is justified and appropriate for the use as 
a quantitative reference standard.

Question:
Question 1
In the manufacturing method of the drug substance, some are found where the amount of the 
solvent, catalyst, and reagent to be used is not shown. Based on the "Guidelines for Items to 
be Used in Application for Marketing Approval of Drugs, etc. in accordance with the revised 
Pharmaceutical Affairs Law" (Notification No. 0210001 of the Evaluation and Licensing 
Division, PFSB dated February 10, 2005), present all the amounts of raw materials, solvents, 
catalysts, and reagents, and describe them in the application form.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.S.2):
Bayer acknowledges the request to include further information in Module 3.2.S.2.2 
manufacturing process descriptions.
The process knowledge obtained during development, which is based on process robustness 
studies, including multivariate (DoE) and OVAT-(one-variable-at-a-time-method) 
experiments, allowed for a sound selection of parameters presented in Module 3.2.S.2.2. 
Further experimental details can be found in Module 3.2.S.2.6. Based on the process 
knowledge and the experimentally established proven acceptable ranges (PARs) or design 
spaces certain non-critical parameters were omitted in the submitted Module 3.2.S.2.2 process 
descriptions.
For the process steps after the final intermediate Gd-GlyMe-DOTA, i.e. steps 4a, 4b, 4c and 
4d where potential impact of each parameter may be increased compared with the earlier 
process steps, it has been demonstrated that non-critical process parameters have no impact on 
quality attributes even if they are varied in a broad range and thus, they can be omitted in the 
manufacturing process description. The respective process parameter understanding studies 
are added to S.2.6.01 including variation of amounts for the following solvents and reagents:
• Process step 4a: variation of amounts of acetonitrile and water used as work-up 
solvents (Subchapters of 5.1.5.1: “Input quantity acetonitrile for dilution after 
reaction” and “Input quantity water for dilution after reaction”)
• Process step 4a: variation of amount of acetonitrile used for washing isolated Gd-
Glydonip (Subchapter of 5.1.5.1: “Input quantity acetonitrile for washing of Gd-
Glydonip”)
• Process step 4b: variation of amount of water and aqueous sodium hydroxide within 
aqueous basic work-up (Subchapters of 5.1.5.2: “Quantity of water added for dilution 
before basic treatment” and “DoE on basic treatment”)
• Process step 4b: variation of amount of t-butyl methyl ether used for washing the 
neutralized aqueous phase (Subchapter of 5.1.5.2: “Washing quantities t-butyl methyl 
ether”)
• Process step 4b: variation of amounts of ethanol and acetone used for crystallization of 
gadoquatrane crude after defined distillation endpoint is reached (Subchapters of 
5.1.5.2: “Quantity ethanol added to distillation residue” and “Quantity acetone added 
to distillation residue”)
• Process step 4b: variation of amount of acetone used for washing isolated 
gadoquatrane crude (Subchapter of 5.1.5.2: “Quantity acetone used for washing”)
• Process step 4c (for the diafiltration-/ultrafiltration process, the introductory passage
of chapter 5.1.5.3 in S.2.6.01 already contained the following information): Being a 
physical separation method of solubilized components as opposed to a chemical 
reaction, the key parameter relevant for quality of step 4c is the number of diafiltration 
cycles, as other parameters (variation of water used for gadoquatrane crude 
dissolution, temperature, membrane surface area) only influence the time one cycle 
takes, not the product quality
• Process step 4d: variation of amount of activated charcoal used before final 
crystallization of gadoquatrane drug substance (Subchapter of 5.1.5.4: “Quantity of 
activated charcoal”)
The results of those studies demonstrate that constancy of quality of gadoquatrane is ensured 
within a broad parameter range justifying not to define setpoints for those non-critical process 
parameters.
Although demonstrated that the washing amount of ethanol in the final step 4d has no impact 
on the quality of Gadoquatrane drug substance in a broad range, Bayer agrees to amend the 
manufacturing process description by adding the respective washing amount of ethanol to 
further ensure the constancy of quality. Consequently, a subchapter to 5.1.5.4 in S.2.6.01 
(“Quantity of ethanol used for washing”) is added well.
Considering the number of steps towards the drug substance and additional control of 
intermediates, washing amounts and solvent amounts required for simple dissolution 
procedures or pH adjustments used in earlier synthesis steps have no impact on the quality of 
Gadoquatrane drug substance and therefore are not included in the manufacturing process 
descriptions. Furthermore, several in-process controls (IPCs) are implemented in the early 
steps before the final intermediate (Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate) to monitor the degree of 
conversion and level of impurities fulfilling the requirements of Notification No. 0210001 by 
ensuring the constancy of quality by additional control measures:
Steps 1a+1b: 3 IPCs plus control of Glyptac intermediate based on appropriate release 
specification (S.2.4.03 Glyptac intermediate)
Steps 1c+1d: 3 IPCs plus control of Glyptac intermediate based on appropriate release 
specification (S.2.4.03 Glyptac intermediate)
Steps 2a+2b: 4 IPCs plus control of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude intermediate based on 
appropriate release specification (S.2.4.03 Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude intermediate)
Step 3: 1 IPC plus control of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate based on appropriate release 
specification (S.2.4.03 Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate)
In conclusion, Bayer does not agree that the manufacturing process descriptions should 
provide more detailed information for process parameters which have no impact on the 
quality of Gadoquatrane drug substance but agrees to add washing amounts of ethanol used in 
the last synthesis step. Control of intermediates and in-process controls justify that such 
detailed process descriptions are generally not required for all manufacturing process steps.
The amount of ethanol used for washing the drug substance after final crystallization has been 
included in the manufacturing description (S.2.2.02 Manufacturing Process – Description / 
Gadoquatrane drug substance):
Before change:
After stirring, the mixture is cooled to『20 °C』, solids are isolated by filtration and washed 
with ethanol.
After change:
After stirring, the mixture is cooled to『20 °C』, solids are isolated by filtration and washed 
with 『2-fold w/w』ethanol with respect to gadoquatrane.
In accordance with the instruction, we will adjust the description in the approval application 
form to clarify that either double or five times the weight of ethanol will be added to the 
weight of Gadoquatrane.

The synthesis of Gadoquatrane drug substance includes two different routes of synthesis 
towards the first intermediate Glyptac. Both synthesis routes (DO3A route and Cyglyp route) 
are compared in detail in section 5.1.1 of S.2.6.01. The comparison includes the organic and 
inorganic impurity profile, as well as solvents and potential mutagenic impurities in the 
intermediates Glyptac and Gd-GlyMe-DOTA and in the final drug substance. Based on this 
data it is shown that the drug substance produced via DO3A route or Cyglyp route is of equal 
quality.
An additional comparison of the non-specified impurities in intermediates and in the drug 
substance is requested and is therefore provided in the following.
Organic impurities in Gadoquatrane drug substance:
In Gadoquatrane drug substance the following impurities are relevant in both routes and are 
specified with individual limits: Gd-GlyMe-DOTA (refer to Question 11), Formyl-Tris-Gd-
GlyMe-DOTA Isomer 1, Methyl-Gadoquatrane Isomer 1 and 2 and Desmethyl-Gadoquatrane 
Isomer 1.
Besides those specified impurities no further impurities are detected in Gadoquatrane drug 
substance batches above reporting threshold (RT 0.03%). This is demonstrated by the batch 
data of Gadoquatrane drug substance in Table 1 (result for any unspecified impurity <0.03%) 
and by the chromatograms provided in Figure 1. Thus, there is no difference which has an 
impact on quality in the impurity profile of Gadoquatrane drug substance produced via either 
DO3A or Cyglyp route.
Further organic impurities which can be formed in the final chemical steps 4a to 4b are 
described in section 5.2 of S.2.6.01. None of the discussed impurities are route-specific. The 
potential impurities can occur in both routes of synthesis and are effectively purged, as 
discussed in detail in the respective section.

Question:
Question 3:
Reply to the following inquiries regarding the control of raw materials.
1. 
Explain the principles of the test method for the following control.
• 
Step 2a Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Iron: 20ppm or less (visual inspection)
• 
Step 2a Sulfuric acid: Chloride: 10ppm or less (visual inspection)
• 
Step 4b Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Chlorine: 0.0004% or less (visual inspection)
and Iron: 0.0001% or less (visual inspection)
2. 
Explain the acceptance criteria and the principle of the test method the following
control.
• 
Step 4b t-butyl methyl ether, Step 4b/4d Denatured ethanol and Step 4b Acetone:
Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (visual and titration)
• 
Step 4d Activated charcoal: Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (visual)
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 3 (3.2.S.2):
Response to Question 3-1.:
The method for all of these tests has been classified as “visual inspection”, as the final 
judgement of colorized or turbid solutions has to be done visually. Please find here the 
descriptions of the principle of the methods for the requested tests.
Step 2a Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Iron: 20 ppm or less (color reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is reacted with ammonium persulphate and 
potassium thiocyanate solution containing butanol. In parallel, the same reaction is carried out 
with a standard iron solution.
The test solution meets the requirement if the intensity of the color produced in the butanol 
layers (due to Fe(SCN)3) is less intense than that produced by standard iron solution (20 
ppm).
Step 2a Sulfuric acid: Chloride: 10 ppm or less (precipitation reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is treated with nitric acid and silver nitrate. In 
parallel, the same reaction is carried out with a standard chloride solution.
The turbidity in the sample solution, produced by precipitated AgCl, is less than in the 
reference solution.
Step 4b Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Chlorine: 0.0004% or less (color reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is treated with potassium iodide and starch solution.
Any blue coloration (due to iodine produced) must disappear when adding max. 0.2 mL 
sodium thiosulfate solution 0.01 M.
Step 4b Hydrochloric acid concentrated: Iron: 0.0001% or less (color reaction)
An aqueous dilution of the test substance is treated with citric acid monohydrate and 
thioglycolic acid. In parallel, the same reaction is carried out with a standard iron solution.
After 5 minutes the sample solution is max. as pink as the reference solution. The pink 
coloration is due to the ferric thioglycolate produced.
Accordingly we will modify the approval application form to clarify the principles of these 
testing methods. We will also make similar changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.
Response to Question 3-2.:
Please find the principles of the test methods and the respective acceptance criteria for the 
requested tests below.
Step 4a Acetonitril, Step 4b t-butyl methyl ether, Step 4b/4d Denatured ethanol and Step 
4b Acetone: Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (neutral litmus paper and titration)
The test substance mixed with water is tested with red and blue litmus paper.
The litmus paper shows neutral reaction.
If the litmus test is weakly alkaline or acidic, carry out a titration.
Test for alkaline substances: 50 mL of the test substance is titrated to color change from blue 
to yellow against bromophenol blue indicator.
The volume of hydrochloric acid 0.1 mol/L consumed must not exceed 0.3 mL.
Test for acidic substances: 50 mL of the test substance is titrated to color change from 
colorless to pink against phenolphthalein indicator.
The volume of sodium hydroxide solution 0.1 mol/L consumed must not exceed 0.3 mL.
Step 4d Activated charcoal: Acidity or alkalinity: must comply (neutral litmus paper)
The test substance is heated in water. After cooling to room temperature, the suspension is 
filtered, the filtrate has to be neutral against litmus paper.
Accordingly we will modify the approval application form to clarify the principles of these 
testing methods. We will also make similar changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.
In addition, we have standardized the descriptions for "acidity or alkalinity"...

Question:
Question 5
Explain the justification of the reworking based on the experiences of reworking and the 
analytical results of the reworked lots for Step 2a, "If in-process control 2 is not met, a 
dichloromethane work-up is performed." If there is no cases of reprocessing so far, remove 
the description related to the reprocessing.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 5 ( 3.2.S.2, 3.2.S.4 ):
For the first commercial scale production campaigns, the dichloromethane work-up in Step 2a 
was carried out for every batch produced as part of the regular process with the aim to ensure 
consistent quality control of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate obtained in Step 3. Batch 
analysis data of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate batches, which were manufactured with 
execution of the dichloromethane workup during Step 2a are shown in S.2.4.05_01 
(Manufacturing date in 2022: 37148971, 37148972, 37148973). Likewise, batch analysis data 
of Gadoquatrane drug substance obtained from Gd-GlyMe-DOTA batches, which were 
manufactured with execution of the dichloromethane workup during Step 2a are shown in 
S.4.4.01 (Manufacturing date in 2022: UN623TE, UN623TG, UN623TI)
With ongoing manufacturing experience and development of the DO3A route of synthesis, it 
was determined that the dichloromethane work-up is not always required to meet the 
specifications of the downstream impurity Bis(Gd-GlyMe-DOTA) (limit max. 0.2% on Gd-
GlyMe-DOTA intermediate). To exert control of this impurity during manufacturing, in-
process-control 2 will need to comply to levels of the respective precursor species (Bis-
carboxylic acids controlled as RRT 0.84) of not more than 0.3% in step 2a (a detailed 
discussion including the structure of the controlled species can be found in S.2.6.01).
Batch analysis data of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate batches, which were manufactured 
with no dichloromethane workup performed during Step 2a are shown in S.2.4.05 
(Manufacturing date in 2024: 37169824, 37169825, 37169826). Likewise, batch analysis data 
of Gadoquatrane drug substance obtained from Gd-GlyMe-DOTA batches, which were 
manufactured with no dichloromethane workup performed during Step 2a are shown in 
S.4.4.01 (Manufacturing date in 2024: UN62XIK, UN62XIM, UN62XK7).
The batches of drug substance produced in 2022 and 2024 showed no difference in impurity 
profile and all batches complied with the current specification. Based on the experience 
gained during routine production on commercial scale, retaining the in-process control-
governed dichloromethane workup in the manufacturing description of Step 2a as reworking 
is justified by the quality-based arguments.

Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 6 (3.2.S.2):
We will modify the approval application form as follows to clarify each cleaning procedure. 
we will also make similar changes to the relevant sections of CTD 2.3.S.
Additionally, after the consumption of the drug substance lot using Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude 
intermediate manufactured in the initial commercial production scale campaign, we commit to  
remove the description regarding the cleaning process using only acetone.
Re: Step 2b: Solids are isolated by filtration, washed with acetone and ethanol, or only with 
acetone.
For the first commercial scale production campaigns, Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude was produced 
only using acetone as the washing solvent for the isolated product. As was presented in 
S.2.6.01 in section 5.1.3, washing with either acetone, or acetone followed by ethanol, is not 
strictly indicated by quality considerations, but indeed has a (non-critical, but favorable) 
impact on the levels of free Gadolinium in Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude: While not strictly 
required to meet the quality requirements of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA intermediate after process step 
3, the additional ethanol washing favorably lowers the free gadolinium input into the 
downstream synthesis towards gadoquatrane drug substance. Based on these findings, the 
ethanol wash was included in routine manufacturing on commercial scale henceforth.
To conclude, Bayer prefers to keep the option for both washing procedures: Firstly, it was 
demonstrated that the purity requirement of Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude is not impacted by the 
mode of the washing operation itself – thus there is no quality-based criterion that decides if 
the additional washing takes place. Additionally, ethanol is used as a raw material in the 
following steps 3, 4b and 4d. Secondly, drug substance batches produced in commercial scale 
with either washing mode are planned to be used for commercial production of drug products.

Question:
Question 9
Please answer the following questions regarding the identification test, IR.
1. 
The Guideline for Drafting the Japanese Pharmacopoeia states that, in principle, the
reference spectrum method should not be used because it is difficult to set a reference 
spectrum with ATR method. Therefore, please consider deleting the method of comparing 
with a reference spectrum. If Bayer considers that it is possible to set a reference spectrum, 
please provide a justification.
2. 
In the answer to 1 above, when differences are found in comparison with spectrum of
reference standard (not comply) and repeat the comparison between spectrum of the test 
sample and reference standard, please explain a justification with a rationale (Including a 
justification for dissolving the sample and gadoquatrane reference standard in water, 
evaporating to dryness, and using it as a measurement sample).
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 9 (3.2.S.4):
1. In test method S.4.2.01, identity testing by IR is described using the attenuated total 
reflection (ATR) method. A figure of the reference spectrum is shown. This reference 
spectrum was generated by measuring the qualified gadoquatrane reference substance after 
structure elucidation has been carried out and is electronically stored in the software. During 
release testing, a visual comparison of the reference spectrum and the sample spectrum is 
performed on an overlay generated in the software. Therefore, the reference spectrum and the 
sample spectrum are recorded on the same equipment in the same laboratory environment. 
Different samples lead to reproducible results during the period of the validity of the reference 
substance which comply to the reference spectrum shown in in S.4.2.01 for illustration 
purposes.
This procedure is covered by Ph. Eur. 2.2.24 “Absorption spectrophotometry, infrared”, 
where it is described that the spectrum of the reference standard may be recorded immediately 
or stored in a spectral library for future consultation. Also, JP general chapter 2.25 “Infrared 
Spectrophotometry” allows both options (3.1 “Identification by the use of a Reference 
Standard” and 3.2 “Identification by the use of a Reference Spectrum”) without limitation to a 
specific sample preparation method. Recent IR-spectrophotometer are capable of generating 
reproducible ATR spectra, so that the shown example reference spectrum in S.4.2.01 will 
remain valid for comparison throughout the lifecycle of the drug substance.
The confirmation of identity by IR testing follows a stepwise approach.
1. The gadoquatrane reference standard is qualified and IR spectrum is measured with
 the IR device of the laboratory responsible for release testing. The spectrum is stored 
 in the software.
2. IR spectra of the release batches are generated and compared with the spectrum of the
 reference standard stored in the software. If both spectra comply to each other, the 
 identity is confirmed.
3. If there is any ambiguity in the confirmation of the identity, e.g. because of different
 water loadings of release batch and reference standard, both the release batch and the 
 reference standard are recrystallized in parallel with the same procedure so that they 
 are obtained with the same water content and the same solid state form. When the 
 measurement and comparison are repeated subsequently, identity can be confirmed 
 unambiguously.
This procedure was chosen to reduce the amount of reference standard to be used. 
Comparison of a release batch spectrum with a reference spectrum from the reference 
standard previously measured and stored in the same laboratory equipment leads to reliable 
results in confirming the identity. Only in cases where there is ambiguity in the comparison, a 
recrystallization procedure and direct comparison with a concomitantly measured reference 
standard is necessary. This is line with the Japanese Pharmacopoeia's infrared absorption 
spectroscopy method which states that if the spectrum differs from the reference spectrum, the 
sample should be treated under specified conditions and then remeasured. Therefore, we think 
it is appropriate to use a reference spectrum for comparison first and only in case of ambiguity 
use direct comparison to the reference standard after recrystallization.
2. Gadoquatrane drug substance can exist in different polymorphic forms (Hydrate I, II, III 
and amorphous phase), with a wide range of water loadings (up to 21.0 %, see S.4.1.01) and is 
classified as very hygroscopic. Depending on the water content, slight differences in the IR 
spectrum might be observed when compared to the reference spectrum of the reference 
standard. By dissolving the substance and the reference standard in water and drying them 
under the same conditions, both sample and reference standard can be obtained with the same 
water content. When the measurement and comparison are repeated subsequently, identity can 
be confirmed unambiguously.
In the following figure the comparison is shown between the reference standard before 
recrystallization (hydrate II, pink line) and after recrystallization (amorphous form, red line).

Question:
Question 10
Regarding the purity test “Appearance of solution color”, please provide a reason why two 
methods (visual test and automatic colorimeter test) are set, and what is a criterion for 
choosing which to use.
Also, please consider describing the criterion for choosing which to use in the specifications 
and test methods in AAF.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.S.4):
The test “Appearance of solution color” as described in S.4.2.01-04 is based on the Ph. Eur. 
general chapter 2.2.2 “Degree of coloration of liquids”, method I. This method applies visual 
comparison between test solution and standard solutions and is equivalent to JP 2.65 
“Methods for Color Matching”, Method 1. The test is routinely evaluated visually. To allow 
for further laboratory improvement and automation of testing routines, the use of an automatic 
colorimeter is explicitly permitted. This is only possible with the pre-condition that the 
equipment is adequately qualified and that it has been proven that the equipment will lead to 
the same quality decision as the visual evaluation (refer to general chapter Ph. Eur. 2.2.2 
“Degree of coloration of liquids“, method 3 and JP <G1-4-181> “Instrumental Measurement 
of Coloration of Liquids”).
We confirm, that at present JP 2.65 “Methods for Color Matching”, Method 1 is used for the 
testing of the clarity of solution of gadoquatrane drug substance. It is intended to use 
instrumental measurement in the future after evaluation of the equivalence as it was done in 
the laboratory for testing of gadoquatrane solution (see question 9), but it is not implemented 
yet. We agree that the option for using the automatic colorimeter will be deleted from 
S.4.2.01-04 for the time being.

Question:
Question 1
Gadoquatrane drug substance is a mixture of three diastereomers. The CMC reviewer is 
interested in understanding the scientific rationale behind classifying all three diastereomers 
as drug substance (DS). Specifically, they would like more information on which studies (PK/ 
in vivo comparison?) were conducted to support this classification and the guidelines those 
studies were based on.
CDE has expressed interest in learning from global experts about best practices and scientific 
approaches related to this topic. So, they raised this question.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section):

Gadoquatrane is a mixture of three diastereomers, two of them are pairs of enantiomers, 
whereas one diastereomer is a meso compound.
All isomers of Gadoquatrane were characterized with regard to their relaxivity (in vitro), as 
well as their pharmacokinetic parameters in an animal study (rats). Both relaxivity and PK, 
revealed to be very similar for the three isomers.

It is the fundamental principle of a contrast agent to catalyze the relaxation of water 
molecules, by their coordination to the paramagnetic metal ion. A multi-purpose contrast 
agent molecule is not supposed to interact physiologically with e.g. membrane channels, 
enzymes, receptors, etc. In that sense, a contrast agent is not comparable to a e.g. highly 
selectively active molecule of a therapeutic drug.

Question: 3.2.P.2.2 – Dissolution method: In module 3.2.P.2.2.02-01 “Pharmaceutical development – Dissolution profiles”, the quality control method is used to show that all clinical batches meet the release acceptance criteria of Q = 80% in 15 minutes. Section 3 states that “Riociguat drug substance exhibits the solubility profile of a week base with high solubility at acidic pH and lower solubility at higher pH. Thus, the riociguat granules show a very rapid dissolution at pH 1.2 and a lower dissolution rate at pH 4.5 and 6.8”. Based on the pH solubility dependency, the use of a surfactant does not appear to be justified. Similarly, the choice of pH 6.8 phosphate buffer as the dissolution medium with surfactant is not explained. While acidic pH may not be discriminative enough, pH 4.5 appear to be an alternative dissolution medium. The proper development of the dissolution method challenging the pH medium and use of surfactant is not demonstrated. The development of the dissolution method should cover the choice of the method, the selection of the medium (composition, volume, pH) and should justify the use and level of a surfactant. Please update the module section 3.2.P.2.2.3 to include the full dissolution method development for Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral suspension as an immediate release formulation and justify the selection of dissolution acceptance criterion (Q = 80% in 15 minutes) based on the justification of the selected dissolution method in line with Ph. Eur. 5.17.1 “Recommendations on dissolution testing.
Answer:
A dissolution test method has already been developed for several dose strengths of Riociguat coated tablets in the range of 0.5 mg to 2.5 mg using phosphate buffer pH 6.8R 10% + 0.1% Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). Applied volumes of Riociguat suspensions are 1.0 mL to 11.0 mL, corresponding to 0.15 mg to 1.65 mg of riociguat. Thus, doses are in a similar range as Riociguat coated tablets. Therefore, the first choice is to use the same dissolution medium that was developed for Riociguat coated tablets. The dissolution methods for the granules and the coated tablets use the same medium (phosphate buffer pH 6.8R 10% + 0.1% SDS). The methods only differ in the rotational speed. The Riociguat coated tablets are tested with 75 rpm, whereas the Riociguat granules are tested with 50 rpm.
Dissolution profiles of 11.0 mL suspension in 900 mL of different media without surfactant are shown in Figure 1. The very rapid dissolution at pH 2 demonstrates that there is no or almost no discriminating power. At pH 4.5 and 6.8 ≥ 3-fold sink conditions are given, however, without surfactant a plateau is not reached within 30 min. To optimize the discriminatory power of the dissolution testing, a phosphate buffer with pH 6.8 was chosen for further development.
Different levels of SDS were added to the aqueous buffer systems. Sink-conditions are achieved without the addition of SDS as a surfactant for the 1.65 mg dosage (amount of riociguat in 11.0 mL suspension). However, as can be seen in Figure 2, the dissolution without SDS is relatively slow and reaches only approx. 80% after 30 min.
Sodium dodecyl sulphate (SDS) is generally suitable as a surfactant and wetting agent. The addition of 0.1% SDS is below the critical micelle concentration. Thus, it serves as a solubilizer and leads to a complete dissolution after 30 min. The amount of SDS needed was evaluated in the range of 0.05 to 0.12% SDS. The best results were achieved with 0.1% SDS while maintaining a high discriminatory power. A higher amount of SDS did not further improve the dissolution.
Based on the developed dissolution method, the specification was set to Q=80% of labelled claim of active substance after 15 min, which is in compliance with the Ph. Eur. 5.17.1 where the Q-value should be at least 75% within 45 minutes.
For more details please refer to the source document. The P.5.3.21 has been amended based on questions 14.

Source: P.5.3.21-02 Method Development - Dissolution - Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral suspension (#022974449; amended)

Question:
3.2.P.2.3 – Manufacturing process development: Overall development and characterization of particle size of granules. 
In the design space (Table 3-5), quality attribute Riociguat particle size is stated between 0.3 – 12 μm. Based on the 3.2.S.4.1, Specifications of Riociguat micronized drug substance, the particle size specifications are X10: min. 0.3 μm, X50:1 - 6 μm, X90: max 8 μm). The development does not explain how the design space was established for the quality attribute of Riociguat drug substance to be 0.3 and 12 μm. 
Granule particle size (either Particle fractions: > 63 μm, > 125 μm, > 250 μm and/or Particle size X10, X50 and X90 fractions) were measured at laboratory scale (Table 1-9), pilot scale (Table 2-7 and Table 2-9), commercial scale (Table 2-18). No recommendations are made on granule particle size at the end of development and prior to the execution of the process validation batches.
In 3.2.P.2.3, section 1.4.3 (page 13), it is stated that “The two batches manufactured with the higher spray pressure (0RB-120503A-400 and 0RB-120503B-400) show high assay and dissolution values”, demonstrating the importance of the granule particle size. In 3.2.P.2.1.1 “Pharmaceutical development Components”, section 1.4, it is stated that “It could be demonstrated that drug product granules manufactured with drug substance covering a broad range of particle size distribution showed sufficient homogeneity in granules and suspension independently of riociguat particle size”. Question is raised whether the discriminative power of the dissolution method discussed at section 1.4 of 3.2.P.2.1.1 is related to the drug substance particle size only, to the granule particle size only or to both. If the granule particle size has an influence on the dissolution profile, the granule particle size should be characterized.
Particle characterization of granules that will suspend upon reconstitution is a critical quality attribute and along with viscosity, they will determine whether the suspension will result in a flocculated (easily dispersible) or deflocculated (less prone to redispersion) systems. The presence of the protective colloid, Xanthan gum controls flocculation to some extent upon reconstitution, but the suspension is not characterized either by measurement of sediment volume ratio for controlled flocculation or viscosity, (see also related question at 3.2.P.2.2.1 – Robustness test).
Please include in the development section the characterization of the particle size of the granules and the characterization of the suspension other than visual suspendability and redispersion times. The physical stability of the suspension can be supported by including pictures of particle sedimentation over time. However, objective criteria such as viscosity values and / or thixotropic properties of the suspension should be part of development to support the consistent manufacture and characterization of the suspension at release and shelf life.
Answer:
During development the dissolution of various granules with different particle sizes of riociguat and different particle sizes of the granules were tested.
To test the influence of different particle sizes of riociguat, drug substance batches with a X90 value from 4 µm up to 92.0 µm were used for the granules. The batches containing riociguat well within or just above the micronization specification (x90 = 4 and 10 µm) comply to the dissolution specification of Q = 80% after 15 min, whereas the other batches containing larger particle sizes, do not meet the specification. The dissolution test method is able to discriminate between granules containing different particle sizes of riociguat drug substance.
In the initial source document, an error occurred regarding the dissolution values for granules produced for the systematic investigation on spray rate and spray pressure in chapter 1.4.3. The One Variation at a Time (OVAT) studies included the preparation of granules with different spray rate and spray pressure leading to particle sizes ranging from an X90 value of 212 µm to 355 µm. For the batches 0RB-120503A-400, 0RB-120503B-400 and 0RB-120504A-400 the dissolution after 30 minutes was compared to the dissolution after 15 minutes for batch 0RB-120504B-400, which lead to the wrong conclusion. The applicant apologizes for the mistake. Figure 6 shows the complete dissolution profiles of all four batches. The dissolution is independent of the process parameters and different granule particle sizes.
Thus, the discriminative power of the dissolution method is related to the drug substance particle size only. The drug substance is micronized and its particle size is specified. The granule particle size has no influence on the dissolution profile and its characterization is not necessary. The corresponding data has been added to the P.5.3.21.
Testing of the homogeneity of the suspension with different shaking times showed that with an initial shaking time of 30 seconds a homogeneous suspension is achieved.
Taking into consideration that in the real-life conditions users might not shake long enough (as observed during the Human Factors validation testing; see Use Error UE-15 in Table 5 of STED.7.3.02 Human Factor - Report), a safety margin of double shaking time was added. Since no harm is associated with longer shaking than 60 seconds this use error is considered as negligible.
Reference is made to P.2.2.01 where - amongst others - sedimentation and agglomeration behaviour was evaluated.
Since sedimentation is a common behaviour of suspensions, before each application, the bottle must be shaken for 10 seconds. Even if the bottle is not shaken appropriately for 10 seconds, an appropriate homogeneous suspension is achieved.
Therefore, a specification of viscosity values and / or thixotropic properties is not needed. According to ICH Q6A, for relatively low viscous solutions or suspensions, it is not required to include rheological properties (viscosity/specific gravity) in the specification (P.5.6.01).

Question:
3.2.P.2.3 – Manufacturing process development: Critical steps and proposed control strategy 
The manufacture of the granulation liquid was identified as a low risk following the intermediate and final quality risk assessment (Section 3.1, Table 3-1). Considering that the homogenization speed of the Ultra Turrax T50 is not defined and the manufacture of the two commercial scale batches use significantly different homogenization speeds: between 5’000 and 8’000 rpm for batch 18-F-ADP and at 2’500 rpm for batch 20-F-ADP, the parameter homogenization speed needs to be defined.
Process parameters should in general be defined against an equipment type and working capacity. As an example, the proposed target process parameters and process controls for critical manufacturing steps at commercial site as presented in Table 3-3 (page 54) should specify the equipment capacity of the fluid bed granulator for them to be meaningful. The proposed inlet air volume during premixing of 120 – 180 m3/h does not correspond to the inlet air volume for the commercial scale batches 18-F-ADP and 20-F-ADP (Table 2-18) which were 400 m3/h, both during granulation and drying. A spray pressure of 2.5 – 3.5 bar is suggested as a process control parameter (Table 3-5). According to Table 3-5 (page 56), this range is the design space and is not the Proven Acceptable Range (PAR). Commercial scale batches (Table 2-18) were manufactured with a spray pressure of 3.0 kPa (that is 0.03 bar). Please specify the homogenization speed for the type of homogenizer used in the manufacture of the granulation liquid and provide for the equipment types and capacities for the listed process parameters throughout development (Table 3-5).
Answer:
Batch 18-F-ADP was manufactured on a GEA MP2 fluid bed granulator situated in the development department of Patheon Bourgoin. For the preparation of the granulation suspension an IKA T50 equipped with a dissolver stirrer working at 5000 to 8000 rpm and a granulation liquid vessel with a capacity of 25 L were used. Batch 20-F-ADP was manufactured on a GEA MP2 fluid bed granulator situated in the manufacturing department of Patheon Bourgoin. The preparation of the granulation suspension was optimized using an IKA T65 homogenization unit working at 2500 rpm. The capacity of the granulation suspension vessel was kept at 25 L. The granulation suspensions of the validation batches were manufactured using the adapted parameters of batch 20-F-ADP.
Limits for inlet air flow values have been evaluated separately for both premixing and spraying phase. For batch 18-F-ADP the inlet air flow was set to 400 m³/h for both premixing and spraying. Subsequently, the parameters of the premixing phase have been adapted to reduce excipient losses in the filter system during preheating/ premixing. Thus, for premixing the inlet air flow of batch 20-F-ADP was set to 150 m³/h (120-180 m³/h). For the spraying phase the inlet air flow volume was kept at 400 m³/h.
Parameters given in design space table are related to spraying phase.
Spray pressure unit in P.2.3.01 Table 2-18 is not correct and needs to be adapted. The applicant apologizes for the mistake and corrects it from kPa to bar.

Source: P.2.3.01-04 Pharmaceutical Development - Manufacturing Process / Riociguat granules 0.3 % for oral suspension (#022990836; amended)

Question: 3.2.P.2.4 – Migration studies: A leachable study was conducted on the pipettes and bottle adaptor where the leachable compounds Methyl benzoate and Oleamide were reported. While the conservative approach of 1.5 μg/day was used as the Safety Concern Threshold (SCT), the study does not conclude whether the two compounds Methyl benzoate and Oleamide remain below the Safety Concern Threshold. According to our calculation the SCT is exceeded for Methyl benzoate. Considering a maximum daily dose of 3 x 11.0 mL, 373.6 ng/mL corresponds to 12’328.8 ng/day [33 x 373.6] or 12.3 μg /day (> 1.5 μg/day). Please comment on observed values of the leachable compounds against the chosen Safety Concern Threshold of 1.5 μg/day and please explain the toxicological impact of these observed levels on patient safety.
Answer:
In general, the Safety Concern Threshold (SCT) is used to define an appropriate analytical threshold for a respective leachable study, i.e., despite its name, the SCT is not a real definitive safety limit. As such, any leachable identified can be qualified at higher levels than the SCT, dependent on a number of factors like e.g. leachable-specific information. The Product Quality Research Institute (PQRI) working group proposes a SCT of 1.5 µg/day as starting point, i.e. following the baseline default assumption that all leachables are mutagenic in nature.
After methyl benzoate and oleamide were detected in the Riociguat Liquid Dose Device (LDD) leachable study, both of these compounds were evaluated for potential mutagenicity in-silico and assessed as non-mutagenic justifying higher levels than the SCT.
Compound-unspecific Threshold of Toxicological Concern (TTC) values for non-mutagenic and non-organophosphates could be taken as basis which would be for Cramer class 3 compounds as worst case 90 µg/day (based on the original Munro publication) or 63 µg/day (based on refined RepDose TTC).
However, compound-specific toxicological data exist for methyl benzoate (CAS 93-58-3) that is also used as flavoring agent (generally recognized as safe (GRAS) by the FDA), justifying an even higher value. Data are e.g. summarized in the ECHA registration dossier.
Based on the available data derived no-effect levels (DNELs) were calculated. An oral DNEL for the general population of 1.5 mg/kg/day was calculated. For a 12 kg child this would result in a daily dose of 18 mg/day which is far above the value that could be expected in the Riociguat pediatric formulation using the LDD (> 1000), for a 50 kg child it would be even 75 mg/day.
Oleamide was detected in the leachable study with an average concentration of 41.0 ng/mL which would correspond to 1.35 μg/day considering a maximum daily dose of 3 x 11.0 mL. This is even below the SCT of 1.5 μg/day although higher levels could be justified due to the absence of a mutagenicity signal.
Overall, based on all data, no impact on patient safety is expected due to the detected leachables methyl benzoate and oleamide.

Question:
3.2.P.5.5 – Nitrosamine assessment: Basis for establishing Acceptable Intake of Nitrosamines 
The risk factors related to Nitrosated compounds were assessed per CMDh/439/2022 template (Q4 of EMA/409815/2020) and concluded that a risk for contamination with N-nitrosamines exists identifying the following as potential Nitrosamines present in the drug product 
- Nitrosated Mono-methyl compound 
- Nitrosated TH-Methylcarbamate 
Batch results at page 22 (Table 7-2 and Table 7-3) show acceptable intake (AI) as 100 ng/day for Nitrosated Mono-methyl compound and 1500 ng/day for Nitrosated TH-Methylcarbamate. Please provide the basis for establishing the AI of 100 ng/day for Nitrosated Mono-methyl compound and 1500 ng/day for Nitrosated TH-Methylcarbamate.
Answer:
Acceptable intakes for both nitrosamines were derived using the Carcinogenic Potency Categorisation Approach (CPCA) in line with the EMA guidance. Evaluations were carried out manually and confirmed by the software Derek Nexus (version 6.4.0) / Nexus: (version 2.7.0). The relevant information has been added to the document.
Since it was demonstrated that both nitrosamines are consistently below 10 % of their respective acceptable intake limit, any considerations regarding a combined limit are currently not considered necessary given that the EMA Q&A states that “N-Nitrosamines present below 10% of their respective AI do not need to be factored into the calculation of limits for individual or total N-nitrosamine(s)”.

Question: 3.2.P.5.6 – Polymorphism (Not specified Test Items): While no polymorphic change has been observed during the stability studies of the drug substance, the impact of the drug product manufacturing process (which includes wet granulation) on the polymorphic form of the drug substance need to be shown. Answer:
The solubility of Riociguat micronized drug substance is very low in water. Water is the basis of our granulation suspension. The polymorphic modification of Riociguat micronized drug substance is Modifcation I, which is stable between 0-80°C. The product temperature during granulation is below 80°C. Therefore, modification change is not expected. Additionally, dissolution testing during stability studies show rapid dissolution of riociguat to ensure availability of drug substance.

Question: 3.2.P.8.3 (and 3.2.P.5.3) – Stress tests: The stress testing (forced degradation) does demonstrate that the analytical methods for purity and potency tests are stability indicating when subject to oxidative stress. Peak purity is provided only for oxidative stress (3.2.P.8.3, Figure 1-19). Peak purity analysis with mass balance calculation should be provided for all stressed conditions to claim the method to be stability indicating. Please include these elements in the stress study to demonstrate that the analytical method is stability indicating.
Answer:
The mass balance under forced degradation conditions is presented.
Under the forced conditions of stress testing, significant decrease in assay for riociguat was observed whereas the corresponding amount of degradation products was not detected. The assay of riociguat is calculated using external standard method at a wavelength of 260 nm. Degradation products are evaluated at 324 nm. It is very likely that during the degradation process smaller fragments are formed that show a different UV absorption as the drug substance. In addition, it can be assumed that the relative response factor is also different. This explains why there are deviations in the mass balance.
Peak purity cannot be shown for alkaline stress. Peak purity is shown e.g. for oxidative and acidic stress. After 7 days treatment with 3% H2O2 nearly 19% degradation was found. In the peak purity plot for these conditions the purity angle is smaller than the purity threshold, indicating that the peak is spectrally pure and no unresolved peak was present.
The fact that peak purity could be proven under stress condition with the highest amount of degradation, demonstrate the good selectivity of the chromatographic method and in particular the stability indicating nature of it.
Peak purity with mass balance calculation is provided for all stressed conditions in P.8.3.04 amended, exceptionally for the displayed temperature and humidity stress because these results were not determined by recording the UV-spectra of the relevant peaks in the 200-400 nm range using diode array detectors.
Therefore, peak purity calculations and chromatograms of temperature and humidity stress are summarized for two further batches of Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral suspension in P.8.3.11 to show that under these stress conditions peak purity for riociguat is given.

Source: P.8.3.04-02 Stability Data - Stress Tests / Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral suspension (#022974495; unchanged)
P.8.3.11-01 Stability Data - Additional Data / Riociguat granules 0.3 % for oral suspension (Peak purity) (#022990942; new)

Although formal validation reports and specification justification documents were not generated at that time, the methods have been used reliably for many years, supported by routine QC performance, system suitability checks, and historical batch data. The specifications are based on compendial standards, supplier requirements, and long-term manufacturing experience, and remain appropriate to ensure excipient quality. Bayer Oy has manufactured Jadelle drug product for 30 years with the same specifications in place for the excipients, resulting consistently in finished drug product fulfilling the product specifications. From that perspective the analytical methods for the excipients can be stated to be valid for their intended purpose. The most important excipients for Jadelle 2 x 75 mg implant are the core elastomer [Poly(dimethylsiloxane) elastomer excipient core] and the tubing [Poly(dimethylsiloxane) elastomer excipient tubing]. The tubing is produced at the facilities of the drug product manufacturer. The third excipient in the implant itself [Poly(dimethylsiloxane) elastomer excipient condensation curable] is used only as a stopper in the implant ends to prevent too fast release of levonorgestrel via open implant ends. Regarding all the excipients in the implant, the identification of the materials is the most important quality test, which is performed by Infrared spectrometry (IR) for all of them. Identification by IR spectrum is quite a trivial method based simply on comparison with the reference spectrum. This identity test is performed for all three excipients of the Jadelle implant. For the tubing, in addition to identification, correct dimensions are most important features for providing appropriate release of levonorgestrel from the implant. These dimensions are ensured with the validated tubing manufacturing process in which the dimensions are continuously measured. Regarding drug core, the levonorgestrel-elastomer rod, outer diameter of the rod fulfilling the in-process control limits ensures correct amount of levonorgestrel in the implant, and for its part appropriate release of levonorgestrel also. Tubing dimensions are, however, more important to guarantee appropriate release rate for drug substance. The analytical methods for the excipients are not fully validated to fulfil current guidelines, as the product is over 30 years old. The material identification can be, however, determined with certainty by the IR method. Release analyses performed on the Jadelle implant batches, in addition to the dimensions for the core rod and for the tubing ensured by validated manufacturing processes, will guarantee and verify that the finished drug product will consistently fulfil the Quality Specifications of Jadelle implant. Question:
Kindly justify the absence of sterility and endotoxins testes from shelf-life specifications.
Kindly justify not including the related substances test in release specifications.
Answer:
The maintenance of the sterile barrier integrity, and hence the sterility throughout the shelf life is demonstrated during stability testing by testing the integrity of the primary package. The integrity of the package is tested with bubble test and the seal strength of the package with strip test.
The substitution of Sterility and Endotoxin test with Container closure integrity tests during the shelf-life is in accordance with the guidelines or principles of both FDA and EMA:
In Questions & Answers of EMA web pages (Quality of medicines questions and answers: Part 2 / Stability - Endotoxin testing and sterility testing at the end of shelf-life) the following is stated:
“Sterility is part of the shelf-life specification.
Sterility testing should be performed at least at the end of Shelf-life, but it can be replaced by testing of the container closure integrity. Depending on the nature of the container, intermittent integrity testing might be envisaged, independent of whether the sterility testing is replaced or not.”
https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/human-regulatory-overview/research-development/scientific-guidelines/quality-medicines-qa-introduction/quality-medicines-questions-answers-part-2
This approach is approved by FDA as well in Guidance document “Container and Closure System Integrity Testing in Lieu of Sterility Testing as a Component of the Stability Protocol for Sterile Products”.
FDA guideline states for example the following:
“Alternatives to sterility testing as part of the stability protocol, such as replacing the sterility test with container and closure system integrity testing, might include any properly validated physical or chemical container and closure system integrity test (e.g., bubble tests, pressure/vacuum decay, dye penetration tests or seal force tests, etc.). Such tests may be more useful than sterility testing in demonstrating the potential for product contamination over the product’s shelf life or dating period.”
FDA's Guidance-for-Industry_Container-and-Closure-System-Integrity-Testing-in-Lieu-of-Sterility-Testing in-the-Stability
Related Substance: Due to inherent stability of levonorgestrel, Impurity test parameters will be deleted from release Specification. The long history of the production has verified that levonorgestrel remains virtually unchanged in the manufacturing process of the drug product, and also during the stability studies. This is demonstrated by comparison of the results for six drug product stability batches to the corresponding drug substance batch results. Question:
Question 1
The new validated method for PSD determination may be acceptable. However, it is not 
deemed acceptable to introduce a correction factor to align the D50 values obtained with the 
new equipment to the current specifications. Furthermore, the data obtained for D90 with the 
new method despite being comparable to the current method may still result in OOS results. 
The applicant should therefore re-establish the specification limits for PSD based on the 
results obtained with the new equipment, in accordance with ICH Q6A. Ideally, the 
specifications should be based on the results obtained for active substance used in clinical 
pivotal batches and tightened to reflect the 44 batches data.
Answer:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.S.4):
Bayer acknowledges the request for setting a Malvern equipment specific specification for 
analysis of the particle size distribution. In accordance with ICH Q6A, the acceptance criteria 
should be based on the observed range of variation and should take into account the dissolution 
profiles of batches that showed acceptable performance in vivo. 
 
The particle size distribution of the batches used during clinical trials had been measured using 
the legacy instrument (Beckman Coulter). It has been demonstrated during clinical 
development (as presented in section 3.2.P.5.6) that the requirement for the dissolution (Q = 
75% after 45 min) of Darolutamide 0.3 g film-coated tablets is met if the d50 does not exceed 
100µm, measured with the Beckman-Coulter instrument (d50 of clinical batches: 22 - 63 mm), 
therefore the upper specification limit was set to 100µm (measured with Beckman Coulter). For 
a more detailed justification of the specification limits for the Beckman-Coulter method, please 
refer to section S.4.5 Justification of Specification. 
The drug substance batches used in the pivotal clinical trials are not available for reanalysis 
with the Malvern equipment, but the batches measured for the determination of the proposed 
new Malvern specification are in a similar range (measured with Beckman-Coulter) and can 
therefore be considered representative for the purposes of setting the Malvern specification 
limits. 
 
For determining a representative specification for the Malvern instrument additional batches 
have been analysed, therefore instead of previously 44 batches, data from 199 batches (09/2025-
06/2026) were used to compare the results between both methods (Beckman Coulter and 
Malvern Mastersizer). The batches are representative of the current production and the 
corresponding drug product batches have met the release specification for dissolution. The 
particle size distribution data of these batches is presented in the updated section 3.2.S.4.3 
(Method comparison report).

A brief summary of the PSD d50 and d90 results of these 199 batches is presented here below 
(Table 1).

Consequently, a Malvern method specific specification is required.
When setting specification limits for the Malvern method it is clear that an average ± 3 sigma 
cannot be used due to typical variability of PSD results within production. Specification limits 
would be wider than justified by process capability.
Therefore, in the proposal for PSD d50 and d90 specifications the variability of the analytical 
method has been taken into account. According to validation requirements of the laser 
diffraction method (USP <429> and Ph.Eur 2.9.31) a variation of up to 10% for the d50 value 
and up to 15% for the d90 is acceptable. These values have been considered in the calculation 
of the lower and upper limits.

In addition, and in accordance with ICH Q6A, for the upper limit of the PSD d50 and d90 
specifications the known increase in PSD during stability studies should be considered. 
Darolutamide has shown an increase in both the PSD d50 and d90 values in stability studies. 
Estimation of maximum particle size increase during retest period in combination with the 
variability of the PSD method results in a conservative allowance of +25%. This estimation is 
taken into account for the upper PSD specification limit. The 199 batches used for specification
