Question: CDE CMC reviewer Mr. Zhou Haohui asked for FDA and EMA HA questions and responses for Gadoquatrane injection.
Answer:
Please find below the executive Summary: Gadoquatrane solution o.4 mml Gd/mL for injection - FDA Questions and Applicant Responses (Module 3 Quality).
No questions were raised regarding drug substance.
(3.2.A.1)

Facilities:
Focus on clarification regarding detailed equipment information, floorplan location and environmental monitoring systems.

(3.2.P.2) (3.2.P.3)

Pharmaceutical Development & Process Understanding:
Focus on process understanding including mixing, filtration, and holding times. The applicant justified dynamic process controls via automated process control system (PCS), classified parameters as non-critical, and supported claims through validation data and risk assessments rather than fixed parameter specifications. Additional questions regarding holding time study, filter adsorption study as well as the chemical compatibility study were addressed and clarified.

Manufacture & Sterilization Validation:
Questions related to sterilization validation were addressed by providing full heat penetration/biological indicator (HP/BI) data, minimum and maximum load validation, bracketing strategies, and detailed autoclave control descriptions. Worst-case approach based on liquid volume and heat exposure was justified.

Microbiology & Endotoxin Control:
The applicant implemented a holistic control strategy aligned with USP <1228>, including supplier control, IPC testing, and validation data. Regulatory questions on depyrogenation and endotoxin control were addressed and clarified.

Please find below the executive Summary: Gadoquatrane solution o.4 mml Gd/mL for injection - EMA Questions and Applicant Responses (Module 3 Quality).

Drug Substance
(3.2.S.1.3)
Complex Stability:
The Rapporteur requested experimental determination of complexation constants and comparative discussion with established gadolinium agents. The Applicant explained that experimental determination was not feasible due to the molecule’s size and extremely slow dissociation kinetics. Instead, a DFT (density functional theory) -based computational approach was applied using monomeric model units representing the tetrameric structure. These calculations demonstrated that each subunit exhibits thermodynamic stability comparable to gadobutrol (log kGdL > 20).
In conclusion, the complex stability of each single gadoquatrane unit is very comparable with the complex stability of gadobutrol. The small variation in calculated complex stability between the two model units further indicates that the linker atoms, which connect the monomers in a tetramer unit, have little influence on the overall stability. Thus, the complex stability of the gadoquatrane tetramer is primarily driven by the sub-unit stability which is comparable to gadobutrol.

(3.2.S.2.2)
Manufacture - Process Description & Controls:
The Rapporteur requested clarification and improvement of the manufacturing process description. The Applicant clarified that sodium bromide addition is mandatory, described seeding as non-critical, and provided information regarding reprocessing and recovery. Critical process parameters were highlighted, and generation and use of gaseous, potable, and purified water was clarified.

(3.2.S.2.3)
Mutagenic Impurities in Starting Materials:
The Rapporteur requested clarification on control of mutagenic impurities. The Applicant applied an ICH M7 Option 4 approach supported by purge calculations, spiking studies, and analytical validation. The Applicant concludes that all mutagenic impurities are adequately controlled.

Cyclen Impurity Control:
The Rapporteur requested clarification regarding impurities in Cyclen. The Applicant demonstrated via QSAR system that Benzylethanolamine is non-mutagenic and provided batch data confirming its presence below reporting thresholds. For para-Toluenesulfonic acid (pTSA), absence was confirmed and supported by worst-case purge calculations and spiking studies.

Glypro Impurities and Specification:
The Rapporteur requested clarification on Glypro impurities. The Applicant confirmed Isopropyl tosylate classification (ICH M7 class 2), provided spiking and purge data, justified specification limits, demonstrated racemic synthesis, and confirmed that glycine is chemically manufactured without fermentation-related viral risk.

Gadolinium oxide:
The Rapporteur requested tighter control of elemental impurities. The Applicant provided improved analytical data (ICP-MS), demonstrated compliance with ICH Q3D Option 2, and supported the control strategy with purge studies. Further tightening was not considered necessary.

Neopentyltetramine (NPTA) hydrochloride Impurities:
The Rapporteur requests additional information for NPTA HCl on spiking studies to verify purge of 2-chloropropane and methyl/ethyl tosylates, discussion of isopropyl tosylate, assessment of pentaerythritol and benzylamine, and evaluation of p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and pTSA including possible downstream ethyl tosylate formation and any need for specification limits. The response adds commercial batch data, purge calculations, and dedicated spiking studies for these late-stage risks, expands the impurity discussion in the starting material justification and impurity sections, and concludes that the relevant impurity risks are adequately controlled to acceptable levels.

Raw Material Specifications:
The Rapporteur requested improved raw material specifications. The Applicant harmonized specifications regarding identity, assay, and impurity controls and clarified water system compliance with current regulations.

(3.2.S.2.4)
Control of Intermediates:
The Rapporteur requests tabulated presentation of in-process controls for each manufacturing step, tightening and clarification of selected intermediate specifications, clarification that Bis(Gd-GlyMe-DOTA) represents two regio-isomers, and additional characterisation data for intermediates. The response adds a dedicated IPC table, tightens and clarifies Glyptac and Gd-GlyMe-DOTA crude specifications, updates the regio-isomer wording, and provides additional characterisation data for Glyptac and Gd-GlyMe-DOTA.

Analytical Methods and Supporting Data:
The question requested clarification on IPC methods, spiking and purge studies, batch data, analytical validation, the PDE for diisopropylethylamine, and control of 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene. In response, the applicant provided the requested supporting documentation, tabulated batch and spiking data, detailed purge justifications, a PDE rationale, and data confirming adequate control and purge of 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene

(3.2.S.2.6)
Manufacturing Process Development:
The Rapporteur requested clarification on the scale at which PARs (Proven Acceptable Ranges) were established. The Applicant clarified scale applicability and scale verification, based on development data, process understanding, and commercial manufacturing experience.

Impurities:
The question requested clarification on possible downstream formation of des-acetyl-Gadoquatrane-like impurities, batch data and method capability for class 2 impurities, and the justification for compound-specific mutagenic impurity limits. The applicant discussed purge and spiking data showing effective clearance of des-acetyl impurities, submitted additional analytical and batch data for the relevant class 2 impurities, and justified the proposed limits for class 1 and class 2 mutagenic impurities in accordance with ICH M7 and related guidance.

(3.2.S.3.1)
Structure Elucidation:
The Rapporteur questioned structural confirmation of diastereomer 2. The Applicant explained crystallographic limitations due to pseudo-symmetry, provided alternative NMR data using lanthanum analogues, and demonstrated lack of clinical relevance.

(3.2.S.3.2)
Residual solvents and elemental impurities - Method validation:
The question requested validation documents for methods used to determine residual solvents and elemental impurities. The applicant submitted the requested validation.

(3.2.S.4.1)
Drug Substance Specification:
The Rapporteur requested clarification of the applicability of the drug substance specification at the drug product manufacturing site, and tighter limits for water and diastereomers. The applicant confirms that only one 3.2.S.4 section is provided because the drug substance manufacturer’s control is the only testing which is performed. The specification and test methods are appropriate to ensure the necessary quality of Gadoquatrane drug substance to produce Gadoquatrane drug product in the required quality. No additional specification parameters or analytical methods are employed by the finished product manufacturer upon receipt of the drug substance. Furthermore, tighter limits for water and diastereomeric ratio supported by development data and batch history were included in the specification.

(3.2.S.4.2)
Drug Substance -Test Procedure - Endotoxin Testing:
The Rapporteur requested removal of non-harmonised USP references and clarification of the need for an alternative endotoxin method. The applicant removed inappropriate USP references, retained the recombinant cascade reagent method as a validated alternative to the established endotoxin method, and provided the scientific and regulatory rationale for its continued inclusion.

(3.2.S.4.3)
Drug Substance - Method validation:
The Rapporteur requested updates of validation documents: removal of the rCR validation, updated repeatability data for several analytical procedures, and accuracy data for Gd-GlyMe-DOTA in the impurity method. The applicant maintained the rCR validation with reference to the response to previous question and provided updated repeatability and accuracy data for the requested methods, including additional validation for Gd-GlyMe-DOTA. The response confirms that analytical procedures are fully validated for their intended purpose across the specification range.

(3.2.S.4.4)
Batch Analysis:
The question requested reporting of non-limit test results using LOD/LOQ terminology and clarification of differing specifications applied to earlier development batches. The applicant updated free gadolinium reporting to the method LOQ and clarified that clinical development batches were released against phase-appropriate specifications in place at the time, whereas preclinical batches were not subject to formal release specifications.

(3.2.S.4.5)
Justification of specification and skip testing:
The question requested further justification for omission of chiral purity testing, support for omission of a separate gadolinium assay, and revision of the microbial skip-testing approach. The applicant provided exemplary results for optical rotation data supporting the racemic nature of the intermediate and final drug substance, introduced and justified a formula-based gadolinium assay, and revised microbial skip testing to a fixed testing frequency supported by stability results.

(3.2.S.5)
Reference Standards and Characterization:
The question requested clarification on establishment and characterisation of reference standards, additional structural support for selected impurity standards, and identification of standards used for free gadolinium and residual solvent methods. The applicant described the internal approach to reference and working standards, clarified the naming and retest scheme, provided additional structural support for the requested impurity standards, and identified the purchased standards used for the free gadolinium and residual solvent methods.

(3.2.S.6)
Container Closure System:
The question requested demonstration of compliance of the primary packaging materials with the cited Ph. Eur. monographs and updated specifications and certificates. The applicant clarified that pharmacopoeial compliance is covered through supplier qualification, while routine incoming control is limited to identity and thickness, and referred to supplier declarations supporting compliance of the packaging materials.

(3.2.S.7.3)
Stability Data and Stability-Indicating Parameters:
The question requested clarification on the relevance of parameters in stability studies, updated free gadolinium reporting, description of storage conditions, interpretation of assay results under stress, and additional free gadolinium stress data. The applicant justified parameters in stability studies, provided updated free gadolinium reporting to the LOQ, clarified the storage instruction. Furthermore, supportive stress data is referenced confirming that the stability control strategy remains appropriate.

Drug Product

(3.2.P.1)
Composition Tables:
The Rapporteur requested clarification on the composition tables, particularly the use of “q.s.” for certain excipients and the expression of drug substance content in mmol. The applicant explained that hydrochloric acid and water for injection are used as process-adjustable components to achieve pH and osmolality specifications and therefore cannot be fixed quantitatively. Initial quantities are defined during manufacturing and adjusted as necessary. The applicant further clarified that mmol information for gadoquatrane and gadolinium is already included within the composition tables via footnotes. Overall, the approach is maintained in line with Quality-by-Design principles.

(3.2.P.2.1)
Pediatric Use of Excipients:
The Rapporteur requested confirmation that the excipient selection considered pediatric use. The Applicant confirmed that all excipients have well-established safety profiles, including pediatric populations, and that formulation development adhered to relevant EMA guidelines. Supporting justification was added to the pharmaceutical development section.

(3.2.P.2.2)
Stress Studies:
The Rapporteur requested detailed stress study results. The applicant provided full datasets covering mechanical stress, pH variation, and freeze-thaw conditions. Results demonstrate that no significant degradation or quality changes occur, confirming robustness of the formulation.

Physicochemical and Biological Properties:
The Rapporteur requested inclusion of relevant physicochemical and biological properties. The applicant provided data on density, viscosity, osmolality, pH, solubility, and water content. These parameters are linked to product performance and manufacturability and are controlled as part of the defined quality attributes.

(3.2.P.2.3)
Manufacturing Process and Filter Validation:
The Rapporteur requested additional validation data, including filter compatibility, holding time studies, and process parameters. The applicant submitted detailed data confirming compatibility, absence of adsorption, and adequate control of extractables/leachables. Process parameters such as mixing speed and temperature were demonstrated to be non-critical and controlled dynamically via process control systems.

(3.2.P.2.4)
Container Closure System for Paediatric Use:
The Rapporteur requested justification of container closure in relation to paediatric dosing. The applicant demonstrated that multiple presentations allow weight-based dosing, and use is restricted to trained healthcare professionals. Smaller presentations support paediatric use, and the risk of dosing error is considered minimal.

Extractables and Leachables:
The Rapporteur requested detailed method descriptions and toxicological evaluation. The applicant justified the use of screening methods based on threshold of toxicological concern (TTC) and provided toxicological risk assessments confirming no safety concern for detected compounds.

(3.2.P.3.2)
Batch Formula:
The Rapporteur identified inconsistencies in batch formula descriptions. The Applicant corrected the discrepancies and harmonized relevant sections.

(3.2.P.3.3)
Process Parameters:
The Rapporteur requested details on the defined process parameters and definition of critical process parameters. The Applicant demonstrated that parameters such as mixing time, speed, and temperature are non-critical and controlled via the GMP system, supported by development data demonstrating robustness.

(3.2.P.3.3)
Shelf-Life Determination:
The Rapporteur requested confirmation that shelf life is calculated according to guideline CPMP/QWP/072/96. The Applicant confirmed full compliance.

(3.2.P.3.4)
IPC Methods:
The Rapporteur requested references and validation status of IPC methods. IPC methods were clarified as either compendial or performed using qualified equipment. Validation requirements were justified accordingly.

Filter Compatibility:
The Rapporteur requested studies on solution compatibility and extractables from filters. The Applicant provided full filter compatibility and extractables/leachables data in updated documentation, demonstrating no impact on product quality.

(3.2.P.4)
Calcobutrol Specification:
The Rapporteur requested justification for omission of microbiological and endotoxin testing and clarification of solvent impurity limits. The Applicant justified omission of microbiological and endotoxin testing based on manufacturing conditions and monitoring data. A Limit for ethanol is included in the specification, while control of benzene is ensured via the raw material specification in place for ethanol.

Analytical Procedure:
The Applicant corrected inconsistencies between validation and analytical procedure (assay), ensuring alignment of documentation.

(3.2.P.5.1)
Specification:
The Rapporteur requested clearer references and impurity nomenclature. The Applicant updated specifications accordingly.

(3.2.P.5.3)
HPLC Method:
The Applicant corrected column dimension discrepancies and updated validation documentation.

Stress Testing Methods:
The Rapporteur requested demonstration of mass balance and additional stress details. Additional forced degradation data were provided confirming the stability-indicating nature of analytical methods.

(3.2.P.5.5; 3.2.S.3.2)
Nitrosamine Risk Assessment:
The Rapporteur raised questions regarding the risk assessment of nitrosamine formation in both the drug substance and drug product which were addressed and clarified. The Applicant concluded that there is no relevant risk of nitrosamine formation.

(3.2.P.5.6)
Degradation Product Limits:
The Rapporteur requested tightening of degradation product limits. The Applicant agreed to tighten release specifications but maintained shelf-life limits based on stability data and safety considerations.

Calcobutrol Content:
The Rapporteur proposed tightening limits. The Applicant justified the existing limits, providing scientific justification that variability does not impact safety or efficacy.

Diastereomer Limits:
The authority requested tighter limits. Specifications were tightened in line with drug substance control strategy.

(3.2.P.6)
Reference Standards:
The Rapporteur requested full characterization of reference standards. The Applicant provided additional data and explained the limitations of NMR for gadolinium-containing compounds.

(3.2.P.7)
Container Closure System (prefilled syringe not applicable for China):
The authority requested extensive information on primary packaging (prefilled syringe, vials and bottle). Comprehensive updates were provided including technical drawings, updated specifications, and supplier certificates confirming compliance with pharmacopeial requirements.

(3.2.P.8)
In-Use Stability (multi-use only for large volume presentations 30 mL and 65 mL not applicable for China):
The authority requested justification for omission of preservatives and clarification of in-use stability. The Applicant justified the preservative-free formulation and updated product information to exclude manual multidose use.

Stability-Indicating Methods:
The authority requested confirmation that analytical methods are stability-indicating. The Applicant provided stress study data demonstrating appropriate mass balance and method suitability.

Updated Stability Data:
The authority requested 24-month data. The Applicant submitted updated stability results supporting the proposed shelf life.

Further questions not applicable for China:
In-Use Stability Design:
Additional studies using worst-case conditions were conducted, including batches near end of shelf-life.
Questions regarding prefilled syringes (PFS) were answered.

Question:
(i). Please provide stability data with all tests listed in the shelf-life specification. Otherwise, 
please clarify (i). if the product lots tested are representative batches, and (ii). If some tests are 
not intended to be in shelf-life specifications.
Answer:
The applicant confirms that the product lots which were tested are representative batches for 
the commercial production of Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg.
The batch analyses results of the batches no. BXA9E50, BXA9E4Z, BXA9E4V and 
BXA9E4X are shown in the document P.5.4.01_IQMS-267418_2.0_Finerenone coated tablet 
40 mg. All specification parameters according to the shelf-life specification are met.
According to ICH Q6A, the shelf-life specification includes tests with appropriate acceptance 
criteria for the confirmation of the drug products quality to ensure safety and efficacy 
covering the products' shelf life. ICH Q1A (R2) states that stability studies should include 
testing of those attributes of the drug product that are susceptible to change during storage.
A detailed overview of the stability indicating tests of the shelf-life specification is shown in 
section 2.5 “Stability indicating Test Parameters according to Shelf-Life Specification 
(P.5.1.02)” of document P.8.3.01_IQMS-261158_5.0_Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg in 
blister. The test parameters markings, identity, and uniformity of dosage are identified as not 
susceptible to change during storage and therefore not included to the stability studies.
Newest stability data of the representative batches no. BXAX5R5, BXAX5R6, BXAX5R7 
and BXAX5NT which are split batches of BXA9E50, BXA9E4Z, BXA9E4V and BXA9E4X 
are included in P.8.3.01_IQMS-261158_5.0 that is attached to the response.
